summary: 32-facet SOTA research workflow for the aurora component → synthesize a research-backed README + path-forward (batched, rate-safe)

notes.facet: OKLab/OKLCh perceptual color for gradient interpolation — why linear-light + perceptual hue paths beat sRGB; chroma/lightness bell-curves
sotaTechniques: Linear-light compositing + sRGB OETF close (the non-negotiable substrate): convert gamma-sRGB endpoints to linear-light BEFORE any blend, do all mixing/lighting/tonemap in linear, then apply the sRGB OETF (linear→gamma, the c<=0.0031308?12.92c:1.055*c^(1/2.4)-0.055 transfer) ONCE at the very end. sRGB-encoded blending is the dominant cause of muddy, too-dark gradient midpoints — the AV.W1 '~2.2x too dark' class is exactly the missing-OETF failure.

OKLab-rectangular interpolation for adjacent stops (the muddy-midpoint kill): convert the two endpoints to OKLab (L,a,b) and lerp the rectangular coordinates, NOT sRGB or HSL. Because OKLab is near-perceptually-uniform and a,b are signed opponent axes, the straight line holds chroma across the ramp instead of collapsing toward grey at the midpoint (the sRGB 'gray band' between contrasting hues). For TWO-color gradients Aras' guidance is OKLab-rectangular, not OKLCh-polar — polar hue-arc is for deliberate rainbow travel only.

CSS Color 4 hue-interpolation methods in OKLCh (shorter/longer/increasing/decreasing hue): for polar OKLCh travel, the hue angle has two arcs; 'shorter' takes the <=180deg arc (default), 'longer' the >=180deg arc, and 'increasing'/'decreasing' force a monotone cw/ccw walk that does NOT flip when the delta crosses 180deg (the key property for animatable/continuous rainbow sweeps). The canonical implementation works in normalized turns (h/2pi) with the per-method +1.0 branch, then fract()-wraps — a radians-native PI-threshold port diverges 180deg at the antipode.

Ottosson cusp-based adaptive-L0 gamut clipping (the SOTA out-of-gamut mapping): naive per-channel RGB clamp shifts hue; instead project the out-of-gamut OKLab color along a straight L-C line toward an anchor L0, preserving hue exactly. The cusp (max-chroma corner for a hue, from findCusp/computeMaxSaturation) lets one Halley iteration find the gamut intersection to <1e-6 error. Adaptive-L0 (alpha=0.05) blends chroma-compression with single-point projection — the recommended default; 'preserve lightness / compress chroma' is the simpler common baseline.

CSS Color 4 binary-search chroma reduction with deltaEOK JND gate: the spec's gamut-map algorithm binary-searches chroma downward at fixed L,H, comparing each candidate to its channel-clipped version via deltaEOK (Euclidean distance in OKLab); when deltaEOK < the JND threshold (~0.02) it accepts the clip. This is the perceptual alternative to a fixed chroma-shrink loop and is exactly what value.js's deltaEOK + DELTA_E_OK_JND + findGamutIntersection expose.

Oklch+ perceptual-distance correction (arXiv 2606.05255, 2026): Oklab nails appearance uniformity but mispredicts color DISCRIMINATION (STRESS 47 vs CIEDE2000's 29 on COMBVD). Oklch+ adds two transforms before Euclidean distance/interpolation — a lightness power L'=L^0.73 and a Naka-Rushton chroma compression C'=C^0.87/(C^0.87+0.34^0.87), hue unchanged — reaching STRESS 29.09 (~CIEDE2000) with 3 params. Interpolating in this transformed space gives gradients whose perceived rate-of-change is even more uniform than native Oklab.

Chroma/lightness bell-curves on derived ramps (the painterly 'saturated body, calm edges' shape): drive L on a monotone (or eased sine) ascent across the band but drive C on a bell C(t)=Cmid*sin(pi*t)+floor so chroma PEAKS in the mids and relaxes at both extremes — pale apex and deep base read calm, the body reads vivid. A midpoint chroma-BUMP (a small +sin(pi*t) added to a 2-stop pair) is the same trick to keep a vivid pair off the grey midpoint.

Warm-light / cool-shadow temperature coupling: the single most-cited painting rule — nudge hue toward warm (~70deg orange) as L rises and cool (~250deg blue) as L falls, by a signed delta centred on the mid. In a perceptual space this reads as physically-plausible mixed pigment rather than a flat tint, and is what makes oil/oil-pastel mediums read as real paint.

Aras' precompute-to-LMS gradient optimization: the per-pixel OKLab cbrt is the bottleneck (cbrt dominated Aras' profile). Precompute endpoints to the post-cbrt LMS' (or OKLab) representation at config-bake time, interpolate the cheap linear coords per-pixel, and skip the second matrix (M2) where full OKLab semantics aren't needed — drops OKLab overhead from ~20x to ~1.3-1.5x sRGB. The endpoint bake belongs CPU-side; the per-pixel hot path should avoid round-tripping through cbrt.

Dithering before 8-bit quantization (Interleaved Gradient Noise vs blue noise, TPDF): smooth low-contrast gradients band on 8-bit panels; add ~1-LSB noise in DISPLAY space AFTER the OETF (at the value being quantized) and prefer a TRIANGULAR (TPDF) distribution over uniform. IGN (Jimenez, fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(p,(0.06711056,0.00583715))))) is the cheapest good ALU-only mask; spatiotemporal blue noise is higher-quality but needs a texture fetch + temporal animation.

Display-P3 / wide-gamut + float framebuffer headroom: an sRGB canvas clamps saturated stops; a Display-P3 WebGL/WebGPU swapchain (canvas color-space 'display-p3') unlocks ~25% more chroma so a bell-curve chroma peak can actually paint. PBR practice is extended-linear-sRGB in fp16 framebuffers — float intermediate storage also defers banding so the OETF+dither close is the only quantization point.

Inigo Quilez cosine palette as a procedural ramp generator: color(t)=a+b*cos(2pi*(c*t+d)) with four vec3 params produces a smooth cyclic palette in one cheap GPU cosine — a complementary procedural-ramp door alongside an explicit OKLCh-stop LUT (useful for seed->palette derivation where authored stops aren't supplied).
notes.applicability: OUR ENGINE ALREADY DOES THE CORE RIGHT — the research mostly confirms current architecture and points at 4 precise upgrades. Confirmed-correct today: (1) linear-light compositing + single sRGB OETF close at main() (AV.W1 fix, locked by proof:aurora-space-gamma); (2) OKLab-rectangular default interpolation via mixPaletteOklab in aurora.frag.ts (the muddy-midtone kill — exactly Aras' recommendation); (3) the four CSS Color 4 hue methods in interpolateHueTurns (normalized-turns domain, the antipode-safe form — textbook-correct); (4) bell-curve chroma in deriveAurora (chromaEasing='bell', C=cTop+(anchor.C-cTop)*sin(pi*t)) and the midpoint chroma-bump in deriveBlobPalette; (5) warm-light/cool-shadow temperatureShift; (6) IGN dither (ign() post-OETF, Jimenez); (7) in-shader OKLCh saturate3 + brokenColorJitter at constant perceptual L (the broken-color-at-constant-value read only OKLCh makes true); (8) shared single-source Ottosson matrices (procedural-color.glsl.ts) GLSL+WGSL twins. THE FORWARD PATH (AX waves): (A) Upgrade gamutMapStop to Ottosson cusp adaptive-L0 — value.js ALREADY ships findCusp/findGamutIntersection/computeMaxSaturation/deltaEOK/DELTA_E_OK_JND, but gamutMapStop currently uses only gamutMapOKLab (preserve-lightness) + a blunt 0.999 chroma-shrink loop; swapping the shrink loop for findGamutIntersection (Halley, <1e-6) or the deltaEOK-JND binary search is a drop-in fidelity+correctness win that keeps a bell-curve chroma peak from quietly desaturating when it clips. (B) Add an optional Oklch+ interpolation path (L^0.73 + Naka-Rushton C compression before the lerp, inverse after) as a third mix method alongside OKLab-rectangular and OKLCh-arc — most valuable for the wide-hue-span presets (Crayon Rainbow, triad/split-complementary moods) where discrimination-uniformity, not just appearance-uniformity, governs how even the sweep reads. (C) Display-P3 swapchain opt-in on the WebGPU branch (AW.W7 createGPUCanvas) — the canvas color-space + an fp16 intermediate lets the bell chroma peak paint the ~25% extra gamut instead of clamping; gate behind @media(color-gamut:p3) with the sRGB path as fallback. (D) Per-pixel cbrt audit — mixPaletteOklab/mixPaletteOklchArc do the full LINEAR_SRGB_TO_LMS+cbrt round-trip per fragment per palette segment; for the static-LUT case the OKLab endpoint coords can be precomputed CPU-side into the uPalette upload (Aras precompute) so the fragment lerps OKLab directly and only round-trips back once — measurable win inside profile:budget. (E) Consider blue-noise dither as a WebGPU-branch upgrade over IGN for the quietest low-contrast wispy-sky default (the case IGN's residual pattern is most visible).
pitfalls: Polar OKLCh interpolation through low-chroma (near-grey) endpoints produces UNSTABLE hue — when C~=0 the hue angle is numerically meaningless, so an OKLCh-arc lerp can swing wildly. Use OKLab-rectangular (the current default) for any pair where an endpoint is near-achromatic; reserve the hue-arc path for deliberately-saturated rainbow travel (which the engine already gates behind uHuePath 2/3).

Naive per-channel RGB clamp on an out-of-gamut OKLCh stop SHIFTS HUE (the muddy-desaturated result Ottosson demonstrates). The current gamutMapStop preserves hue correctly via the OKLab path, but the 0.999 chroma-shrink fallback loop is a blunt instrument — under-shrinks (still slightly OOG after 6 iters for very saturated stops) or over-desaturates; the cusp/findGamutIntersection path is both correct and exact.

Oklch+ is a DISTANCE-METRIC correction, not a free interpolation upgrade — its transforms (L^0.73, Naka-Rushton C) must be applied AND inverted around the lerp, and the inverse of the Naka-Rushton compression is only well-defined within its domain; feeding it OOG chroma or doing it in the wrong order desaturates. It's also brand-new (2026, single paper) — validate against the existing presets before making it a default; keep OKLab-rectangular as the shipped default.

The OKLab cbrt (sign(lms)*pow(abs(lms),1/3)) is per-fragment-per-segment in the shader — applying Oklch+ or richer per-pixel perceptual math naively will blow profile:budget. Precompute everything that can be precomputed to the CPU palette bake; the fragment hot path should touch cbrt at most twice (decode + re-encode), ideally lerp pre-baked OKLab coords.

Dithering must happen in DISPLAY space AFTER the OETF, at the bit-depth being quantized — dithering in linear-light (before the transfer) dithers the wrong magnitude and under-corrects mid-tone banding. The current ign() placement post-OETF is correct; don't move it.

Display-P3 is a PORTABILITY HAZARD: a P3 canvas clamps when shown on an sRGB display, and color(display-p3 ...) values silently desaturate to sRGB there. Must @media(color-gamut:p3)-gate and keep the sRGB path as the tested fallback; never assume the wider gamut paints. fp16 framebuffers also aren't universal — feature-detect.

Interpolating L on a bell (peaking mid-L) rather than monotone breaks the 'deep base -> pale apex' painterly read and can make a ramp non-monotonic in lightness (two stops same L) — keep L monotone (linear/sine ascent); the bell belongs on CHROMA only, which the current deriveAurora does correctly (easeRamp linear-for-L, bell-for-C).

value.js's inline LMS->OKLab coefficients differ from its LMS_TO_OKLAB_MATRIX at the ~1e-9 digit; the shared GLSL/WGSL matrices deliberately mirror the INLINE path. Any new perceptual math added in-shader must source the SAME inline constants or it will fail the 1e-6 equivalence gates (proof:single-color-core, proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence). One source, always.

GLSL/WGSL mat3 are COLUMN-MAJOR while value.js arrays are row-major — the shared chunk transposes for GLSL and copies-verbatim for WGSL (same column-major). Any hand-added matrix must follow this or it computes a transposed (wrong) transform that looks plausibly-colored but is hue-wrong.

notes.facet: Gamut mapping for wide-gamut OKLCh → sRGB without grey-out at distant-hue midpoints; CSS Color 4 gamut clamp vs chroma reduction
sotaTechniques: CSS Color 4 'css' gamut map = binary-search chroma reduction WITH local MINDE (the canonical default). Convert to OKLCh; if already in sRGB return; else hold L,h fixed and binary-search C between [0, C_origin], at each midpoint per-channel-CLIP the reduced-chroma color and compute deltaEOK(clipped, reduced) — if that error is within one JND (deltaEOK = 0.02; 100x smaller than CIE Lab's JND=2 because OKLab L is 0..1 not 0..100), accept the CLIPPED result; loop until (max-min) < epsilon=0.0001. This is the headline: pure chroma reduction alone grays out (the P3-yellow witness drops to chroma ~25), pure clip alone hue-shifts; the hybrid keeps chroma ~103 on the same witness by clipping locally whenever clipping is perceptually invisible.

Ottosson analytical cusp gamut clipping (the GPU-portable form). Because the sRGB gamut boundary in OKLab is described by CUBIC polynomials per hue, you can solve compute_max_saturation() analytically (a cubic per channel, refined by ONE Halley + ONE Newton step from a 0.4 seed — fixes the blue-hue precision dip) to get the per-hue cusp (L_cusp, C_cusp), then find_gamut_intersection() projects the out-of-gamut point along a straight line toward a focal L0 to the boundary in closed form. No iteration loop, no deltaE — branch-free and constant-cost, the right shape for a fragment shader.

Projection-focus choice (Ottosson's four methods, the grey-out lever). (1) preserve-chroma/clip-to-closest = clamp L to [0,1] keep C — bright/dark detail loss; (2) project toward L0=0.5 C=0 (hue-independent) — simple but desaturates and can shift perceived lightness; (3) project toward L0=L_cusp (hue-DEPENDENT) — projects at the hue's own cusp lightness so saturated colors do NOT collapse to grey, the recommended look; (4) ADAPTIVE L0 with alpha — blends compression (alpha→0.05, behaves like chroma-compress, gradient-friendly) and single-point projection (alpha>5). Simon's Tech Blog verdict: 'compress chroma only looks quite decent; projection toward a single point may change perceived lightness' — so adaptive-toward-cusp with small alpha is the gradient sweet spot.

OKLCh hue-arc interpolation is what AVOIDS the grey distant-hue midpoint in the first place (distinct from gamut mapping). A rectangular OKLab (L,a,b) lerp or an sRGB lerp passes through C≈0 grey at the midpoint of a complementary pair; lerping L and C while walking H along the hue wheel (shorter/longer/increasing/decreasing arc) holds chroma across the ramp — blue→yellow travels through purple/green, never grey. Our engine already does both forms (mixPaletteOklab rectangular + mixPaletteOklchArc hue-arc); the SOTA refinement is a midpoint chroma BUMP (a bell C += k*sin(pi*t), already used in deriveBlobPalette) to actively counter the slight chroma sag a straight C-lerp leaves between two unequal-chroma stops.

Per-hue chroma ceiling / pre-flight clamp. The gamut cusp C_max(L,h) varies enormously by hue (blue/violet have a LOW sRGB chroma ceiling; yellow/green high), so any L,C the interpolation or per-stroke jitter lands on can exceed the hull even when both endpoints were in-gamut. SOTA: clamp C to the analytic cusp chroma for that (L,h) BEFORE the OKLab→linear matrix, so the value never leaves the gamut and the final per-channel clamp/ACES never fires as a hue-distorting fallback.

Kubelka-Munk / spectral mixing as the painterly distant-hue path (spectral.js, rvanwijnen). For a paint-like backdrop, mixing two pigments via Kubelka-Munk reflectance (or the RYB/CMY-curving-outward heuristic the meodai color-expert skill cites: 'CMY mixing paths curve OUTWARD = retain chroma = vivid secondaries; RGB paths curve INWARD = dull browns') gives vivid secondaries (blue+yellow→green) where OKLab linear mixing gives a duller transition. This is a stylistic upgrade to the interpolation, orthogonal to (and upstream of) the gamut-map step.

Display-P3 escape hatch (the wide-gamut payoff). On color-gamut:p3 displays, rendering to a Display-P3 canvas/context and gamut-mapping to the P3 hull instead of sRGB keeps far more of the authored OKLCh chroma (the cusp C_max is materially higher in P3 for cyan/green/magenta), so the mapping clips/compresses far less. Gate via @media (color-gamut: p3) / a WebGL drawingBufferColorSpace='display-p3' (or WebGPU 'display-p3' canvas config) probe, fall back to sRGB mapping otherwise.
notes.applicability: "Where our engine stands and the path forward. CPU side: src/composables/color/index.ts already ships gamutMapStop() = value.js gamutMapOKLab (Ottosson cusp method) + a 6-iter 0.1%-inward chroma nudge, and deriveAurora/deriveBlobPalette gamut-map EVERY authored/derived stop. So authored STOPS are safe. THE GAP is everything downstream of the stops, all in the fragment shader (aurora.frag.ts): (a) mixPaletteOklab and mixPaletteOklchArc compute an interpolated OKLab/OKLCh value then call oklabToLinearSrgb() with NO gamut map — the result is handled only by the final clamp(col*0.985+0.008,0,1) + ACES, i.e. exactly the naive per-channel CLIP that hue-shifts and the grey-out fallback; (b) brokenColorJitter (lines ~349-355) and saturate3 (~361-364) both round-trip through OKLCh and can push C past the per-hue cusp, same un-mapped clip exit. PATH FORWARD for the AX waves: (1) Splice an analytic Ottosson cusp clip into procedural-color.glsl.ts (the shared chunk that already holds OKLCH_MATRICES_GLSL) as oklchGamutClip()/oklchToLinearSrgbClamped() — compute_max_saturation (cubic + 1 Halley + 1 Newton) → find_cusp → adaptive-L0-toward-cusp projection, branch-free, ~constant cost; this is the in-shader twin of what value.js does on the CPU and keeps the WGSL twin (OKLCH_MATRICES_WGSL) at 1e-6 parity via the existing proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence harness. (2) Route mixPaletteOklab/mixPaletteOklchArc/brokenColorJitter/saturate3 through it so out-of-gamut interpolants compress chroma toward the cusp INSTEAD of clipping channels — kills the distant-hue grey/hue-twist at the source. (3) Add the midpoint chroma-bump to the hue-arc mix to counter chroma sag. (4) The full CSS-Color-4 binary-search+deltaEOK (JND 0.02) is the right CPU reference oracle for a unit test/gate (mirrors the value.js path), but is too expensive per-fragment — the shader uses the analytic cusp projection, the CPU bake can keep the iterative form. (5) OPTIONAL bigger swing aligned with DESIGN.md's painterly goal: a Kubelka-Munk/CMY-outward mix mode for distant-hue stops (vivid secondaries) — fits the medium axis, orthogonal to the gamut clamp which still runs after it. (6) Display-P3 is a forward enhancement that rides the same AW.W7 WebGPU substrate work (config the swapchain to display-p3 and map to the P3 cusp)."
pitfalls: JND units trap: deltaEOK JND is 0.02, NOT 2. OKLab L is 0..1 (CIE Lab is 0..100), so the CSS Color 4 threshold is 100x smaller. Hardcoding 2 makes the binary search accept gross errors and the map degenerates to a near-pure clip.

Analytic cusp has a blue-hue precision dip: the cubic solve for max saturation loses precision around blue (~h 264deg in OKLCh); Ottosson/Simon both add ONE Halley + ONE Newton refinement from a 0.4 seed — skip it and blue/violet stops get a visible kink. Our existing GLSL must replicate this exactly or the WGSL-vs-GLSL 1e-6 equivalence gate breaks.

ACES tonemap is NOT gamut mapping and can MASK the bug — ACES desaturates bright out-of-gamut values, so the grey-out can read as 'tonemapping' and slip past visual review; it does not preserve hue for in-gamut intent. The clamp(col,0,1) after it is the real per-channel clip. Mapping must happen in OKLCh BEFORE oklabToLinearSrgb, not be left to ACES+clamp.

Mapping order: gamut-clip must run on the per-pixel INTERPOLANT in linear/OKLab BEFORE ACES and BEFORE the OETF (linearToSrgb). Doing it after the OETF operates on gamma-encoded values and the cusp polynomials (fit in linear-light OKLab) no longer hold.

max(0,·) negatives wrap is a SILENT half-clip: oklchToLinear already does Math.max(0, linear) (CPU) and the shader does max(...,vec3(0)) — that zeroes negative channels (one face of out-of-gamut) but does nothing for >1 overshoot, so a stop reads partly hue-shifted without any obvious error. Real gamut mapping subsumes and replaces this wrap.

Hue-arc 'fade to white/black/grey/transparent' dead zone (documented across the CSS gradient literature): interpolating a hue-bearing stop toward an ACHROMATIC endpoint (white/black/grey) in OKLCh injects an arbitrary hue arc and surfaces unwanted teal/purple — for those pairs force the achromatic end to share the neighbor's hue or interpolate in OKLab-rectangular, not OKLCh-arc.

Per-fragment cost: the full CSS Color 4 binary-search + deltaEOK is dozens of OKLab round-trips per pixel — unacceptable in the WebGL2 single-pass budget (profile:budget). Use the analytic Ottosson cusp projection in-shader; reserve the iterative form for the CPU bake / the test oracle.

Portability of the matrices: the analytic cusp/max-saturation coefficients are derived FROM the sRGB primaries — a Display-P3 path needs DIFFERENT coefficients (different LMS_TO_LINEAR_*). Do not reuse the sRGB cusp polynomial on a P3 swapchain; derive or swap the constants, or the P3 map silently maps to the wrong hull.

value.js gamutMapOKLab is the CPU source of truth; any new in-shader clip must be gated for equivalence against it (the proof:single-color-core / proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence discipline) or aurora and the blob can drift again — the exact AV.W1 two-copy defect class the shared procedural-color chunk exists to prevent.

notes.facet: Procedural color-harmony generation (complementary/triadic/split/analogous) in OKLCh from a seed; perceptual even spacing
sotaTechniques: EVEN-ANGLE HUE ROTATION IN OKLCh (the baseline SOTA, ColorAide/oklch-pickers): generate harmony partners by rotating the seed hue h by fixed offsets in OKLab's polar form — complementary h+180, triad h+120/+240, split h+150/+210, tetradic h+90/+180/+270, analogous h+-30 — at FIXED L and C, so rotation produces members that read as a coherent set instead of HSL's brightness-mismatched ones. This is exactly what the engine's deriveHue already does, and it is the floor, not the ceiling.

value.js-style HUE-ARC INTERPOLATION WITH EXPLICIT LONGER/SHORTER ARC SELECTION: when walking hue across N stops you must pick the arc direction. The 'dead-gray midpoint' trap is that the SHORTER arc between a warm/cool complement cuts through low-chroma neutral; the LONGER arc keeps the path saturated. The engine's HARMONY_METHOD map (complementary/split -> 'longer', analogous/mono -> 'shorter', triad/tetradic -> 'increasing') is the correct canonical encoding of this — it is the named CSS-gradient-era fix.

OTTOSSON CUSP-AWARE GAMUT MAPPING (find_cusp + gamut-intersection): per hue, compute the cusp (L_cusp,C_cusp = peak achievable chroma) via a fitted polynomial + one Halley step (err < 1e-6), approximate the sRGB boundary as a triangle (0,0)-(1,0)-cusp, and project an out-of-gamut (L,C) point to the boundary along a chosen direction. Adaptive-L0 blends pure-chroma-clip with projection toward L=0.5 or toward L_cusp, preserving lightness when possible and degrading chroma gracefully. This is faster and more hue-faithful than a naive shrink loop.

CSS COLOR 4 / Color.js GAMUT MAPPING (binary search on chroma + deltaEOK channel-clip refinement): binary-search C downward in OKLCh; at each step compute deltaEOK between the chroma-reduced color and its naive channel-clipped twin, and when that perceptual difference drops below the JND of 0.02, return the CLIPPED color instead of the desaturated one. This recovers chroma a pure-shrink loop throws away (P3 yellow: ~103 vs ~25 chroma). It is the reference algorithm the whole ecosystem standardized on in 2024-2026.

PERCEPTUAL-AWARE (NON-NAIVE) HARMONY a la meodai/pro-color-harmonies + royalfig color-palette-generator: do NOT trust pure +-N-deg rotation. (a) MUDDY-ZONE HUE STEERING — nudge derived hues out of the orange/yellow/brown dead band; (b) THRESHOLD-ADAPTIVE L/C — dark seeds spawn LIGHTER partners and light seeds spawn DARKER partners for visibility, with SMOOTH interpolation across the L threshold (no jump at L=0.30); (c) a POLISH PASS that boosts mid-tone chroma + warms highlights so no member reads 'dead'. These are empirically-tuned corrections layered on top of the rotation, exactly where the engine currently stops.

chroma.js correctLightness() — LINEAR-LIGHTNESS REPARAMETERIZATION: sample the L* of the multi-stop ramp, then remap the t-parameter so OKLab L increases LINEARLY end-to-end (yellow gets pushed near the end, dark colors toward the start). Removes the 'plateau' where intrinsically bright members flatten the brightness curve. Directly applicable to the engine's L-ramp/easeRamp and to the in-shader mixPaletteOklchArc stop placement.

chroma.js BEZIER INTERPOLATION through perceptual space: treat interior palette members as cubic-bezier CONTROL points (not waypoints) in OKLab so the multi-hue path curves smoothly and avoids the sharp Lab corners of piecewise-linear interpolation — the smoother cousin of the engine's per-stop linear walk; the control points guide the path without all appearing literally in the output.

OKLCh NON-UNIFORMITY AWARENESS as a first-class correction: OKLab fixed CIELAB's gross blue bending, but residual non-uniformity remains — hue spacing is COMPRESSED in green and high-chroma blue and EXPANDED toward red/purple (Munsell needs 20 steps R->Y but 31 B->R), and high-chroma blue still drifts toward purple (Abney-like). So a literal +120-deg triad in OKLCh is NOT perceptually-even; a Munsell/CAM16-corrected hue wheel (or a small per-region hue-warp LUT) gives a more even-LOOKING triad than raw degrees.

PAINTING-TRADITION TEMPERATURE + WARM-COOL COUPLING as a harmony axis: the strongest 'reads as mixed paint' lever is warm-light/cool-shadow hue coupling (the engine's temperatureShift toward ~70-deg warm / ~250-deg cool). SOTA generative-backdrop work pairs this with the artist's RYB-complement intuition (RYB complements differ from spectral complements; RYB red/green & blue/orange pairs neutralize to brown/grey when over-mixed) — a deliberate input when picking which harmony reads as 'oil paint' vs 'screen color'.

Palmer-Schloss COLOR-PREFERENCE / HARMONY MODEL as a selection prior: harmony (a relational variable) explains ~48% of combination-preference variance vs ~20% for the component colors alone, and perceived harmony tracks perceived hue-SIMILARITY. Implication for a seed->palette deriver: bias toward higher hue-coherence (analogous/mono) for 'pleasant' defaults and reserve high-contrast triad/tetradic for 'vivid' moods — which is effectively what the MOOD_RECIPE table already encodes, now with a citable basis.
notes.applicability: "OUR ENGINE TODAY (color/index.ts deriveHue + gamutMapStop; aurora/color.ts deriveAurora/deriveScene) is already at the COMPETENT baseline: OKLCh-native, value.js Ottosson math single-sourced, correct longer/shorter/increasing arc selection per harmony, a painterly L-band clamp, bell-chroma easing, and temperatureShift warm/cool coupling. It is ahead of naive HSL pickers and on par with ColorAide's even-rotation. THE PATH FORWARD (AX waves) is to close the gap to meodai/pro-color-harmonies and the CSS-Color-4 gamut reference, in priority order: (1) UPGRADE gamutMapStop from the current `safeC *= 0.999` six-iteration linear shrink to the CSS Color 4 binary-search + deltaEOK-0.02 channel-clip refinement (Color.js 'css' method) — recovers visible chroma the shrink loop discards, especially on saturated blues/yellows, for ~free CPU; the bake is CPU-side so cost is negligible. (2) ADD a thin perceptual-correction layer on top of deriveHue: a muddy-zone hue-steer (avoid the orange/yellow/brown dead band) + threshold-adaptive L/C (dark seed -> lighter partners, light seed -> darker, smoothly across the L threshold) — this is the single biggest 'looks designed not generated' lever and slots cleanly between deriveHue and gamutMapStop as a pure function, preserving determinism. (3) For multi-stop ramps, REPARAMETERIZE stop placement via chroma.js-style correctLightness so OKLab L is linear across the ramp (replace/augment easeRamp + the in-shader mixPaletteOklchArc stop spacing) — kills brightness plateaus when a derived stop lands on intrinsically-bright yellow. (4) OPTIONAL: a small per-region hue-warp (Munsell/CAM16-informed LUT) so a +120 triad reads even rather than green-compressed — gate behind a flag; it is a refinement, not a correctness fix. (5) DOC the RYB-vs-spectral-complement distinction in the README so 'painterly' harmony picks (which read as mixed paint) are an explicit author choice. All of this stays CPU-side in the bake (deriveAurora is DOM-free, deterministic, SSR-safe); none of it touches the GPU hot path or the single-pass invariant, and it composes with the existing per-preset / per-mood front doors. The in-shader OKLCh arc interp (mixPaletteOklchArc) already inherits the better stops for free once the CPU bake improves."
pitfalls: OKLCh hue is NOT actually perceptually even — green and high-chroma blue are compressed, red/purple expanded (Munsell needs 20 R->Y steps vs 31 B->R). A literal +120-deg triad therefore is NOT visually-even; relying on raw degrees for 'perceptual even spacing' is the central trap this facet must not fall into. Treat even-degree rotation as 'good enough default', not 'perceptually exact'.

High-chroma blue drifts toward purple under chroma changes (Abney-like residual). Reducing C during gamut mapping can shift the APPARENT hue even though OKLCh h is held fixed — so 'hue preserved exactly' (gamutMapStop's claim) is true numerically but not always perceptually for saturated blue.

The SHORTER hue arc between a warm/cool complement passes through near-neutral gray — the 'dead-gray / muddy midpoint'. Getting the arc-direction map wrong (a single harmony mis-keyed in HARMONY_METHOD) silently produces desaturated bands. Keep the longer-arc encoding for complementary/split and test it.

Naive chroma-shrink gamut mapping (the current `safeC *= 0.999` loop) THROWS AWAY recoverable chroma — it desaturates far more than the CSS-Color-4 channel-clip refinement (P3 yellow ~25 vs ~103). It also caps at a fixed iteration count, so an out-of-gamut stop can survive under-mapped; the binary-search + JND form is both more faithful AND bounded.

meodai-style 'magic number' corrections (muddy-zone steer, polish pass, modulation knobs) are EMPIRICALLY TUNED, not derived — porting them risks overfitting to one aesthetic. Adopt the STRUCTURE (threshold-adaptive L/C, muddy-zone avoidance) but keep the constants minimal and documented, or they become unexplainable tuning debt (and trip the overfitting audit).

Gamut mapping is LOSSY and one-way: round-tripping a P3/out-of-gamut seed through sRGB gamut-map and back will not recover it. Don't gamut-map until the final sRGB bake; keep the OKLCh stops un-clamped through the harmony walk so corrections compose correctly.

Determinism / SSR safety must survive any new correction: deriveAurora is DOM-free, deterministic, and asserted by proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip (resolveAtoms(DEFAULT_ATOMS) deep-equals DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG). Any hue-warp LUT, correctLightness reparam, or adaptive-L threshold must be pure + total and must NOT move the wispy-sky default, or the roundtrip gate goes red.

Don't move the harmony math onto the GPU 'for speed' — the bake is tiny and CPU-side, and the GPU OKLCh chunk (procedural-color.glsl.ts) is single-sourced + gated (proof:single-color-core, proof:shader-shared-source). Forking a second harmony implementation into GLSL/WGSL re-opens the exact two-copy drift bug class (the AV.W1 ~2.2x-too-dark defect).

RYB/artist complements != spectral/additive complements (red's RYB complement is green, but its additive complement is cyan). A 'painterly' harmony that markets RYB intuition while computing additive +180 will surprise authors. Pick one model per harmony name and document it; don't silently mix.

correctLightness reparameterization changes WHICH t each stop lands on, which interacts with the nuclei paletteBias mapping and the in-shader mixPaletteOklchArc spacing. Reparameterizing the CPU stops without re-checking the shader's stop-index sampling can desync the placeholder CSS gradient (paletteToCssGradient) from the painted field.

notes.facet: Palette derivation from a single seed color for natural skyscape/landscape gradients (the wispy-sky default class)
sotaTechniques: Color Crafting designer-ramp model (Smart, Wu & Szafir, IEEE TVCG 2019, the canonical academic SOTA for THIS facet): fit cubic B-splines through 222 expert ramps in CIELAB, arc-length-resample to 9 control points, cluster the COLOR-AGNOSTIC curve SHAPE (SRVF elastic-shape + k-means) into 9 representative model curves, then anchor a seed by translating the model along L* so a chosen control point matches the seed and all other stops follow RELATIVE offsets. Two structural facts it proves: (a) designers reduce chroma at BOTH ends of a ramp (not a monotone falloff to one apex), and (b) ramps carry a 'characteristic twist in hue space' (a small hue rotation, not a fixed hue).

Material You / HCT tonal-palette + chroma-reduction gamut mapping (Google Material Color Utilities): hold hue+chroma fixed and sweep TONE (lightness) to make a tonal ramp, then guarantee in-gamut by reducing chroma until the stop fits sRGB — the production-grade single-seed ramp algorithm. The 'sweep one perceptual axis, then chroma-reduce to gamut' loop is exactly glass-ui's gamutMapStop's 0.999-inward nudge, but HCT formalizes it as the PRIMARY gamut strategy (preserve hue/tone, sacrifice chroma).

Atmospheric-perspective / aerial-perspective color model (landscape-painting + Rayleigh-scattering canon): distance reads as lighter + LESS saturated + COOLER (hue shifts toward blue ~250deg). Encode depth as a coupled L-up / C-down / hue-toward-cool ramp — the single strongest 'reads as a real sky/landscape' cue, stronger than value or saturation alone.

Warm-light / cool-shadow temperature coupling: the most-cited painting rule — if the light is warm (sun ~50-70deg orange), shadows go cool (skylight ~230-250deg blue), and vice-versa. Apply a SIGNED hue nudge across the ramp (warm the lights, cool the darks) so a gradient reads as mixed paint rather than a hue-rotated swatch. glass-ui already ships this as `temperatureShift`.

Hosek-Wilkie / Preetham analytic sky + zenith-horizon two-tone gradient: the physically-grounded sky is a vertical interpolation from a saturated zenith color to a brighter, hazier (lower-chroma, warmer) horizon, blended via smoothstep with a tunable exponent for the haze rolloff. The 'deep saturated top, pale warm bottom' shape is the sky's actual structure and matches the wispy-sky default's deep-blue -> cream apex.

OKLCh hue-arc interpolation with explicit arc direction (longer/shorter/increasing) — the perceptual-gradient SOTA: interpolate in OKLCh so equal numeric steps read as equal visual steps and the sRGB 'gray dead zone' midpoint is avoided. Choose the arc direction per harmony (longer arc keeps a warm->cool pair saturated; shorter arc greys it). glass-ui's deriveHue already routes harmony to value.js HueInterpolationMethod.

Inigo Quilez cosine-palette `a + b*cos(2pi(c*t+d))`: a 4-vector (bias/amp/freq/phase) generates a whole smooth multi-hue ramp from a compact seed in-shader at near-zero cost — a GPU-native alternative parameterization for a seed->ramp LUT when you want continuous procedural variation rather than discrete authored stops.

Grain/dither over the gradient (the banding fix): an 8-bit gradient over a large low-contrast sky bands visibly; a low-amplitude blue-noise/hash dither (glass-ui's `paperGrain`) breaks the steps below the perceptual threshold. This is mandatory for wide low-chroma skyscapes, which are the worst-case banding surface.
notes.applicability: ["LUMINANCE-ANCHORED seeding is the highest-value upgrade to `deriveAurora`. Today the L ramp spreads SYMMETRICALLY about the seed (`anchor.L +/- lightnessSpread/2`) then clamps into [0.35,0.95]. Color Crafting shows designers anchor the seed at a SPECIFIC luminance POSITION in the ramp and let the rest follow relative offsets. Path forward: add an `anchorPosition` (0..1, default ~0.5) so a mid-tone seed centers but a deep seed anchors near the dark end and the ramp climbs to the cream apex — making the seed's own L meaningfully place it in the sky band instead of always sitting at the midpoint.", "glass-ui ALREADY implements the two proven Color Crafting structural patterns — keep and lean in. The `chromaEasing:'bell'` default IS 'reduced chroma at both ends' (the paper's finding); the `deriveHue` walk IS the 'characteristic hue twist'. The README/AX waves can cite TVCG 2019 as the empirical backing for these two defaults rather than presenting them as ad-hoc.", "ATMOSPHERIC-PERSPECTIVE coupling is a natural new derive option. The current ramp couples L-up with C-down (bell) but does NOT systematically cool the lights toward blue with distance. Add an `aerialPerspective` axis that, as t -> pale apex, nudges hue toward ~230-250deg AND accelerates chroma falloff — turning `deriveAurora` from a generic harmonious ramp into a SKY-specific one (the 'wispy-sky default class' the facet names). This composes cleanly with the existing `temperatureShift` (which does the opposite-signed warm-light nudge); expose both and let the mood recipe pick.", "ZENITH->HORIZON should inform NUCLEI placement, not just the palette. The sky's real structure is a vertical gradient (saturated top, pale-warm bottom). `thirdsNuclei` places zones on a golden/thirds prior with paletteBias walking 0->1 left-to-right; a sky-mood variant should bias the DEEP stops to UPPER nuclei (low y) and the PALE/warm stops to LOWER nuclei (high y) so the composed field reads as a vertical skyscape rather than a horizontal blend. This is a `deriveScene` nuclei-layout change, zero shader cost.", "HCT-style chroma-reduction gamut mapping validates glass-ui's existing `gamutMapStop` and the modern-web-guidance gradient note (in-oklch preserves chroma but risks gamut; in-oklab washes out at opposite hues). glass-ui's per-stop bake into the LUT + the 0.999-inward chroma nudge is the CORRECT posture and should stay — the AX README can cite HCT as the production precedent. No change needed; this is a 'we already do the right thing' confirmation for the writeup.", "The CSS `paletteToCssGradient` placeholder (the pre-armed first paint) should declare `in oklch` interpolation per the modern-web-guidance: today it emits gamma-sRGB hex stops in a `linear-gradient(135deg,...)` which the browser interpolates in sRGB (the gray-dead-zone path), so the placeholder can read MUDDIER than the armed shader (which interps in OKLCh). Adding `linear-gradient(135deg in oklch, ...)` with the `@supports` two-variable fallback shown in the CSS guidance closes the placeholder<->shader color-path gap at zero cost.", "The Quilez cosine-palette is a candidate for an OPTIONAL continuous-ramp seed mode but is NOT a fit for the authored-stop architecture (DESIGN.md invariant: nuclei are authored per preset). Note it in the README as the GPU-native alternative for consumers who want a fully procedural seed->color map, but do not replace the OKLCh LUT — the LUT's gamut safety + harmony vocabulary are worth more than the cosine form's compactness for a design-system backdrop."]
pitfalls: OKLCh chroma OVERSHOOT on hue-arc interpolation: `in oklch` (and deriveHue's longer-arc harmonies) can swing OUTSIDE sRGB mid-arc even when both endpoints are in-gamut — the modern-web-guidance flags exactly this. glass-ui mitigates by gamut-mapping each DISCRETE stop, but the SHADER's in-fragment `mixPaletteOklchArc` interpolates BETWEEN baked stops at runtime and can still produce transient out-of-gamut mids that the linear LUT + ACES clamp silently crush. Any new hue-cooling/aerial axis must keep the per-segment chroma bounded, not just the endpoints.

The Color Crafting model is built on SEQUENTIAL/DIVERGING DATA-VIZ ramps optimized for discriminability, NOT atmospheric backdrops — its representative curves can read as too 'even'/legible-stepped for a wispy sky. Borrow the METHOD (luminance-anchored seeding, chroma-end-rolloff, hue-twist) not the literal 9 cluster curves; a viz ramp wants perceptual uniformity, a sky wants painterly non-uniformity (the existing bell + valueVariance mottling).

Warm-light/cool-shadow and aerial-perspective push in OPPOSITE hue directions (temperature warms the lights; aerial perspective cools the distant/pale). Stacking both naively on the same t-axis can CANCEL or produce a muddy mid. They must be applied on DIFFERENT axes — temperature couples to the L (light/shadow) axis, aerial perspective to the DEPTH (nucleus y / paletteBias) axis — or a consumer enabling both gets a flat result. Today both would ride the same `t` in deriveAurora.

OKLCh hue is NOT perfectly constant for blues (the residual Abney-effect / hue-non-constancy that CIELAB suffers worst but OKLab only mostly fixes per Levien): a pure-blue seed swept in L can drift slightly purple at high L. For the sky default (blue-dominant) this is the exact danger zone — validate the derived ramp's high-L stops don't read violet. Levien rates OKLab 'quite good' here, not perfect.

Banding is WORST on exactly this surface: a wide, low-chroma, low-contrast sky gradient over an 8-bit canvas bands hard. The `paperGrain` dither (default 0.008) MUST stay non-zero for sky moods; a consumer who zeroes it to 'clean up' the look will reintroduce visible stair-steps. Document `paperGrain` as load-bearing for skyscapes, not optional polish.

Portability: CSS gradient `in oklch` interpolation is unsupported in pre-2024 browsers (the modern-web-guidance mandates a non-empty preamble + `@supports` fallback or it's a SYNTAX ERROR that kills the whole rule in old engines). The placeholder gradient is the one CSS-color-path surface in aurora; if it adopts `in oklch` it MUST ship the two-variable fallback, never a bare `in oklch`.

Material You's HCT uses CAM16 hue + CIELAB tone — a DIFFERENT space from glass-ui's OKLCh. Do NOT import HCT hue numbers or chroma caps (HCT chroma tops ~120 on its own scale) as if they were OKLCh values; borrow the ALGORITHM (sweep tone, chroma-reduce to gamut) not the constants. value.js's OKLCh is the single source of truth (proof:single-color-core) and must not gain a parallel HCT path.

notes.facet: FBM + domain warping (Quilez) for organic gradient regions; double-warp; rotation-decorrelated octaves
sotaTechniques: Quilez canonical double domain-warp (LANDED, partial): replace f(p) with f(p+4r) where q=vec2(fbm(p),fbm(p+5.2,1.3)) and r=vec2(fbm(p+4q+1.7,9.2),fbm(p+4q+8.3,2.8)). The warp magnitude (length of q and r) is a free organic 'region' scalar Quilez explicitly recommends exposing for coloring. Our engine computes q+r with the EXACT canonical offsets but stops at the second level (displaces position by uWarpAmount*r) rather than doing the third fbm(p+4r) evaluation, and never reads |q|/|r| as a value channel.

Rotation-decorrelated octaves via the canonical mat2(0.80,0.60,-0.60,0.80) (~36.87 deg/octave) (LANDED): a fixed per-octave 2x2 rotation breaks the axis-aligned lattice banding pure scaled-lattice noise produces. This is byte-identical to our shared FBM_ROT_GLSL constant. SOTA confirms this exact matrix as canonical; nothing to change here, but it is the load-bearing decorrelation lever the facet names.

Lacunarity detuning to break inter-octave superposition (LANDED): use 2.01-2.04 (and gain ~0.51, not exactly 0.5) so octave zeros/peaks don't superpose into a regular grid. Our fbm() already uses 2.02 lacunarity (good); gain is exactly 0.5 (the one detune we don't do).

Selective time injection — animate only the lowest + highest frequency octaves, not every octave (NOT DONE): inject t into octave 0 (slow overall flow) and sin(t) into the final octave (detail shimmer); keep middle octaves static. Uniformly offsetting the coordinate before fbm (what we do via p*scale + t*drift) translates ALL octaves in lockstep — a rigid pan rather than an evolving boil. This is the single biggest 'reads alive vs reads scrolling' lever for the breath motion.

Advected / feedback double-warp for breathing flow (NOT DONE): animate q itself over time (q is recomputed with a time term, then r warps off the moving q) so the warp field self-advects and swirls — vortex-like 'boil' instead of a sliding translation. The feedback chain q->r->position is what produces the organic curl; advecting q over time is the temporal extension Quilez leaves to the reader.

Analytic-derivative value/gradient noise + derivative-aware (erosion-like) fBM (NOT DONE, high-value): a value-noise variant returns value AND its 2D analytic gradient in one pass (~5x faster than central differences); the running derivative accumulator d lets each octave self-modulate as a += b*n.x/(1.0+dot(d,d)), suppressing high-frequency detail on steep slopes. When octaves are rotated/scaled the derivative transforms by the chain rule d += b*(M_cumulative)*n.deriv. Gives 'smooth in the flats, crisp at the zone boundaries' — the exact organic-region falloff aurora wants, and the gradient is reusable to drive flow direction and the structure-tensor stroke field for free.

Gradient (Perlin/Simplex) noise base instead of value noise (CONSIDER): gradient noise passes through zero at every lattice point, giving a cleaner spectrum and fewer blobby/grid-biased low-frequency artifacts than value noise (random scalars at lattice points → abrupt changes, lower-frequency bias). Our fbm() is value-noise-based (hash21→vnoise). For the smooth atmospheric pole, gradient noise reads cleaner per octave; this is a quality-vs-cost tradeoff, not a defect.

High-quality integer hash (lowbias32 / TheIronBorn) for the noise lattice (CONSIDER): GPU float-sin hashes (our hash21/hash22 use the fract(sin()*43758) family) fall apart over the 32-bit input range and at large UV/time, producing repetition and shimmer. The lowbias32 bit-mix hash (x^=x>>16; x*=0x21f0aaad; ...) is the current recommended GPU hash for artifact-free noise.

Interleaved Gradient Noise (IGN) dither, post-OETF, 1/255, in display space (ALREADY LANDED — SOTA-correct): Jimenez IGN fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(p,vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715)))) added at 1/255 amplitude AFTER the sRGB transfer kills 8-bit mid-tone banding on the soft gradient with zero texture taps. Our main() already does exactly this (post linearToSrgb). Confirmed best-practice; keep it.

Any new time term (advected q, sin(t) detail octave) inherits this ONLY if it routes through uTime — a parallel clock or matchMedia would escape the freeze and break the proof:aurora-interaction-prm / proof:offscreen-pause gates. notes.facet: Structure-tensor / edge-tangent-flow (Kyprianidis & Kang) for orienting brush strokes along color edges
sotaTechniques: STRUCTURE TENSOR (the orientation source). Form the 2x2 second-moment matrix J=[[Gx*Gx, Gx*Gy],[Gx*Gy, Gy*Gy]] from luminance gradients (3x3 Sobel). Eigen-decompose closed-form: lambda1,2 = 0.5*(Jxx+Jyy +/- sqrt((Jxx-Jyy)^2 + 4*Jxy^2)). The MINOR eigenvector is the edge TANGENT (least color change = stroke direction); the MAJOR is the gradient/normal. Principal angle theta = 0.5*atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx-Jyy) is the numerically-robust form (the (lambda-Jyy, Jxy) eigenvector formula collapses to zero at Jxy~0). Anisotropy/coherence A = (lambda1-lambda2)/(lambda1+lambda2) in [0,1]. This is glass-ui's existing `structureTensorField()` — already correct and canonical.

GAUSSIAN-SMOOTHED STRUCTURE TENSOR (the keystone fidelity lever, Kyprianidis & Kang 2009). The RAW per-pixel tensor is noisy; the canonical fix is to PRE-SMOOTH the tensor field J with a Gaussian (sigma ~2.0, ~5px radius) BEFORE eigenanalysis. Critical subtlety: you smooth the tensor COMPONENTS (Jxx,Jyy,Jxy averaged componentwise), NOT the gradient vectors (which would cancel at opposite-signed edges). This is the single biggest quality jump over a per-pixel tensor and the reason the operator needs an off-screen RGBA16F target (the J products exceed [0,1] and clip on 8-bit). glass-ui's WGSL Pass-2 does exactly this.

ITERATIVE EDGE TANGENT FLOW (Kang/Lee/Chui, NPAR 2007 — the original ETF). A nonlinear vector-smoothing of the tangent field: t_new(x) = (1/k) * sum_y phi(x,y)*t_cur(y)*ws(x,y)*wm(x,y)*wd(x,y), where ws = spatial box (radius ~5), wm = (1/2)*(1+tanh(eta*(ghat(y)-ghat(x)))) lets STRONG edges dominate WEAK ones (preserves salient structure), wd = |t(x).t(y)| aligns by parallelism, and phi=sign(t(x).t(y)) fixes the 180-degree ambiguity. Run 2-3 iterations. This yields a SMOOTHER, more coherent flow than a single Gaussian-smoothed tensor and is the higher-quality alternative to Pass-2.

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA with POLYNOMIAL WEIGHTING (Kyprianidis et al. 2010 — the real-time canon, popularized by Acerola/Blender). Split a radius-R disk into N=8 overlapping sectors, ELLIPTICALLY warped by the tensor: ecc a=R*clamp((alpha+A)/alpha,0.1,2), b=R*clamp(alpha/(alpha+A),0.1,2), rotated by phi so the kernel squeezes ALONG the tangent. Sector weights use the polynomial charfunc (zeta~0.1, zeroCross~0.58, eta=(zeta+cos(zeroCross))/sin^2(zeroCross)) so sectors compute in-loop with NO precomputed mask texture. Per sector accumulate weighted mean m_k and variance s_k; combine via inverse-power weighting w_k = 1/(1+(hardness*1000*s_k)^(0.5*sharpness)) (hardness~8, sharpness~8). Output = sum(m_k*w_k)/sum(w_k) — a SOFT variance blend, NOT a hard argmin. This is the 'make a gradient read as oil paint' operator.

FLOW-GUIDED / LINE-INTEGRAL-CONVOLUTION (LIC) SMEAR (the stroke-texture half). Convolve a noise/color field ALONG the ETF streamlines (Euler-integrate the tangent field a few steps each direction, accumulate samples). LIC is what turns an orientation FIELD into visible directional BRUSH STROKE TEXTURE — the orientation source (tensor/ETF) answers 'which way', LIC answers 'draw the bristle smear that way'. DESIGN.md correctly stages this as a WebGPU multi-pass fold; ETF-without-LIC (current state) is an honest orientation-only approximation.

SEPARABLE / WORKGROUP-SHARED compute optimization (modern WebGPU). The tensor smooth is separable (H then V, glass-ui already does this). On WebGPU the Kuwahara gather (the expensive O(R^2*sectors) pass) benefits from a compute shader with workgroup shared-memory tiling (load the R-padded tile once per workgroup, all threads read from `var<workgroup>`), and the tensor field reads `rgba16float` storage. This is the 2024-2026 'order-of-magnitude faster than CPU, conforms to the papers' path Blender's realtime compositor took.
notes.applicability: "glass-ui is ALREADY at the SOTA frontier for this facet — the research validates the existing architecture rather than overturning it. The current state: (1) `structureTensorField()` in mediums.glsl.ts is a textbook-correct single-pass small-tap tensor with the robust atan2 principal-angle form, coherence A, and the coherence-weighted mix(fallback, tangent, A) relaxation — this is exactly right and should NOT change. (2) The WGSL painterly.wgsl.ts already stages the canonical 3-pass pipeline: tensor->RGBA16F, separable Gaussian smooth, 8-sector elliptical anisotropic Kuwahara. The concrete PATH FORWARD (the AX deltas, all on the already-relaxed WebGPU branch per invariant 8): (A) UPGRADE the Kuwahara combine from hard lowest-variance argmin to the SOFT polynomial inverse-power blend w_k=1/(1+(hardness*1000*var)^(0.5*sharpness)) with hardness/sharpness uniforms — the current `if(vsum<bestVar)` argmin is the OLD Papari form; the soft blend is the Kyprianidis 2010 canon and removes sector-boundary banding. (B) ADOPT the in-loop POLYNOMIAL sector weights (zeta~0.1) so sectors are smoothly windowed (the current hard floor()-into-8-bins assignment hard-cuts sector membership and aliases — the polynomial charfunc fixes this with no mask texture). (C) EXPOSE the kernel as `[a,b]` ellipse axes via ecc=(alpha+A)/alpha rather than the single `ecc=1-A*0.6` squeeze — the two-axis form matches the paper and the Godot/Blender refs exactly. (D) Optionally REPLACE Pass-2's single Gaussian tensor-smooth with 2-3 iterations of the Kang nonlinear ETF (the wm magnitude-dominance term keeps strong color-zone edges from being washed out by the breath-drift). (E) WebGPU compute + workgroup-shared tiling for the Kuwahara gather. The WebGL2 single-pass fallback STAYS as-is (the small-tap tensor + flow strokes is the honest fallback). All of this lands on `painterly.wgsl.ts` which already declares PAINTERLY_KUWAHARA_SECTORS=8 and PAINTERLY_TENSOR_FORMAT=rgba16float as consumer-owned constants — the seam is already carved for these knobs."
pitfalls: TENSOR (not gradient) smoothing is mandatory. Smoothing the gradient VECTORS averages +g and -g across an edge to ~0; you MUST smooth the tensor COMPONENTS (the outer products Jxx,Jyy,Jxy). The current WGSL does this correctly — do not regress it to a gradient blur.

RGBA16F / float-storage is non-negotiable for the tensor target. J = Gx*Gx etc. routinely exceeds [0,1]; an 8-bit LDR target clips it to garbage and the eigenanalysis returns noise. WebGPU rgba16float is fine; the WebGL2 single-pass path SIDESTEPS this by computing the tensor inline in the same fragment (no FBO) — which is exactly why the multi-tap smoothed form is WebGPU-only.

TEMPORAL COHERENCE is the dominant hazard for an ANIMATED aurora (most NPR literature is for still images/offline video). As the breath-drift warps the nuclei field, the per-pixel tensor orientation can SWING/FLICKER at low-coherence zones, reading as crawling strokes. Mitigations: the existing mix(fallback, tangent, A) already damps flat zones (keep it); favor LOW warpDrift on painterly mediums; and the Kang ETF wm term (strong-edge dominance) stabilizes orientation across frames better than a raw per-frame tensor. Do NOT temporally blend the tensor across frames naively without motion compensation — errors accumulate (the classic painterly-video flicker failure).

Hard lowest-variance sector argmin (current WGSL) produces visible sector-boundary seams and quantized stroke directions; it is the pre-2010 form. The polynomial soft-blend is both higher quality AND avoids a branchy argmin loop.

atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx-Jyy) period is PI, so the tangent is a DIRECTOR (180-degree ambiguous), not a vector. Any per-frame or per-tap sign choice must be resolved consistently (the code's dot(tangent,fallbackDir)<0 flip is the right pattern) or strokes will randomly flip and shimmer.

Kuwahara cost is O(R^2 * sectors) per pixel — at R=6, 8 sectors that is ~450 weighted samples/pixel. Full-res on a background canvas can blow the frame budget; render the painterly passes at reduced resolution (half-res tensor+Kuwahara, upsample) or cap R. This is why it is WebGPU-compute-tiled, not a naive WebGL2 fragment loop.

Portability: WebGPU is production-deployable in 2026 (all four engines ship it; Safari 26 last) but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available — keep the single-pass WebGL2 ETF as the universal fallback exactly as DESIGN.md invariant 8 mandates. `isFallbackAdapter` (software) must route to WebGL2 — a CPU WebGPU adapter is slower than the WebGL2 fragment path.

Do NOT use the smoothed tensor's MAJOR eigenvector for strokes — it is the gradient/edge-normal and makes strokes CROSS the color bands (the inverse of the intended look). The minor eigenvector / theta+90deg tangent is correct; the code is right, but it is the single easiest sign error to introduce.

notes.facet: Anisotropic Kuwahara filtering — the canonical "make a gradient read as oil paint" operator (sector count, sharpness, structure-tensor-driven elliptical kernel)
sotaTechniques: **Structure-tensor orientation field (Kyprianidis-Kang 2009 keystone)** — Sobel the luma to get (Gx,Gy), form J=[[Gx*Gx,Gx*Gy],[Gx*Gy,Gy*Gy]], eigen-decompose closed-form: orientation theta=0.5*atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx-Jyy), eigenvalues lambda1,2 = 0.5*((Jxx+Jyy) +/- sqrt((Jxx-Jyy)^2 + 4*Jxy^2)), anisotropy A=(lambda1-lambda2)/(lambda1+lambda2) in [0,1]. The minor eigenvector (edge TANGENT) is the stroke/kernel-long axis; A drives how elongated the ellipse is. This is the single load-bearing 'reads as real paint, not a pattern' lever — orientation comes from the image's own structure.

**SMOOTHED structure tensor (the non-optional stabilizer)** — the raw per-pixel tensor is noisy; orientation jitters pixel-to-pixel and the paint reads as static. The canonical fix is a separable Gaussian over the tensor COMPONENTS (Jxx,Jyy,Jxy) at sigma~=2 (sigma = radius/3 is the common rule) BEFORE the eigen-decomposition. Smoothing is linear on the tensor but geometrically a PCA on the eigenvectors, so it yields coherent, flowing orientation. This requires a real neighborhood (multi-pass / FBO ping-pong) — it cannot be done well single-pass.

**Anisotropic elliptical kernel (Kyprianidis-Kang-Doellner 2009/2010)** — rotate the round sampling kernel by theta and scale it: semi-axes a=radius*((alpha+A)/alpha) along the tangent, b=radius*(alpha/(alpha+A)) along the gradient (alpha~=1 is the eccentricity limiter, clamped to [0.1,2]). Build SR = Scale*Rotate (S=diag(0.5/a,0.5/b), R=rotation by phi); map each offset o into kernel space via SR*o. Coherent (high-A) zones get a long thin ellipse hugging the edge; flat (low-A) zones stay near-circular. This is what makes strokes follow contours and flatten ALONG them.

**N=8 weighted sectors + soft variance blend (the canonical operator)** — divide the elliptical kernel into N=8 overlapping sectors. Per sector accumulate weighted mean m_k = sum(c*w)/sum(w) and variance s_k = sum(c*c*w)/sum(w) - m_k*m_k. The 2009 paper does NOT take a hard lowest-variance winner (that is the OLD Kuwahara and it banding-stair-steps); it blends ALL sectors by w_k = 1/(1 + (255*|s_k|)^(q/2)), output = sum(m_k*w_k)/sum(w_k). The exponent q (sharpness/hardness, typ. 8) controls how aggressively low-variance sectors dominate — high q -> crisp paint splotches, low q -> soft wash. This soft blend is the difference between 'oil paint' and 'posterized stairs'.

**Polynomial sector weighting without convolution (Kyprianidis-Semmo-Kang-Doellner TPCG 2010)** — the 2009 sectors were Gaussian-weighted characteristic functions requiring a precomputed convolved disc texture. The 2010 refinement replaces them with a directly-evaluable polynomial [(x+zeta) - eta*y^2]^2 per sector (zeta~=0.1 controlling spread/overlap, eta~=0.1, lambda~=0.5), exploiting the N-fold rotational symmetry so only one sector function is evaluated and rotated. Same quality, no convolution texture, real-time on GPU. This is THE form modern shader ports (Acerola/Godot/Heckel) ship.

**Gaussian sector-membership overlap (Heckel 2024 anti-banding)** — instead of hard sector bins (floor(angle/2pi*N)), weight each sample's contribution to a sector by a smooth 2D Gaussian f(x,y)=exp(-(x^2+y^2)/(2*sigma^2)) falling off from the sector centerline, so a sample near a sector boundary contributes partially to both neighbors. Eliminates the 8-fold pinwheel seam that hard binning produces in smooth gradients — the dominant artifact on flat aurora fields.

**Per-pixel noise kernel rotation (Heckel 2024 pattern-break)** — perturb the kernel rotation angle by a small per-pixel hash/noise term so the 8-sector lattice does not repeat coherently across flat regions; breaks the residual mechanical regularity into organic brush variance. Cheap, single-instruction, large perceptual payoff on gradient backdrops.

**Multi-scale anisotropic Kuwahara (Kyprianidis-Doellner NPAR 2011)** — propagate orientation estimates and filtered results through a low-pass image pyramid and combine scales, simulating brushes of different sizes (broad lay-in + fine detail) and giving an efficient real-time scheme. The path to 'varied brush size' without an O(radius^2) blowup at large radius.

**LIC (line-integral-convolution) smear along the ETF** — convolve the color field ALONG the smoothed tangent field before/with the Kuwahara to elongate the felt 'stroke' beyond the kernel radius; the classic NPR finish that makes the flattening read directional. Multi-pass; pairs with the smoothed tensor.

**Texture/canvas + impasto relight overlay (Heckel 2024, Meier 1996 lineage)** — after the Kuwahara flatten, multiply a paper/canvas tooth texture and add a height->normal->specular impasto relight so the flat paint regains material micro-relief. The Kuwahara gives the FLAT paint shapes; the overlay gives the SURFACE. Order matters: flatten first, relight second.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for glass-ui's aurora. The engine has ALREADY staged a competent 3-pass WebGPU implementation in `src/components/custom/aurora/constants/shaders/painterly.wgsl.ts` (tensor pass -> separable Gaussian smooth -> 8-sector Kuwahara), gated correctly behind `navigator.gpu` with WebGL2 single-pass as the zero-regression fallback (DESIGN.md invariant 8, Delta09). The format choice `PAINTERLY_TENSOR_FORMAT='rgba16float'` is CORRECT and portable — rgba16float is renderable AND filterable by default in core WebGPU (no feature gate), unlike rgba32float which needs the optional `float32-filterable` feature for the linear sampling the smooth pass relies on. The sector count `PAINTERLY_KUWAHARA_SECTORS=8` matches Papari/Kyprianidis canon and lives correctly in the CONSUMER (painterly.wgsl.ts), not the substrate (proof:webgpu-substrate-single). The CONCRETE GAPS vs SOTA, in priority order: (1) The current `kuwahara_main` uses HARD sector binning (`floor(ang/(2pi)*SECTORS)%SECTORS`) plus HARD winner-take-all lowest-variance selection (`if vsum<bestVar`) — this is the 2009-or-earlier form and WILL produce visible 8-fold pinwheel banding on aurora's smooth low-structure gradient fields (its WORST case — flat fields are exactly where hard sectors seam). Replace with the soft blend output=sum(m_k*w_k)/sum(w_k), w_k=1/(1+(scale*s_k)^(q/2)) and a `q` (sharpness) uniform fanned from the existing `textureAmount`/medium atom. This is the single highest-fidelity, lowest-risk change. (2) Add Gaussian sector-membership overlap (Heckel) so boundary samples bleed across sectors — directly targets the same banding on flat fields. (3) Add per-pixel noise rotation of the kernel to break the residual lattice — fits aurora's existing hash/prng vocabulary (utils/prng.ts mulberry32). (4) The eccentricity is currently a clamped coherence proxy (`ecc=clamp(1-A*0.6,0.4,1)`); move to the canonical a/b semi-axis construction (a=radius*(alpha+A)/alpha, b=radius*alpha/(alpha+A)) so the ellipse elongates properly in coherent zones — aurora's nuclei iso-bands are high-coherence and want the long thin kernel. (5) The smooth pass is a fixed 9-tap sigma~2; expose sigma=radius/3 so a larger Kuwahara radius gets proportional tensor smoothing. (6) FUTURE/optional: multi-scale (NPAR 2011) and LIC are the 'varied brush size + directional smear' finish, but are additive luxuries — the soft-blend + overlap + noise-rotation trio is the 80/20. Wire `q` and `radius` through the two-tier atoms door (resolveAtoms) so the painterly sharpness rides the existing `textureAmount` consumer atom; keep the full knobs under the Advanced escape hatch per the AW.W6 progressive-disclosure pattern. All of this stays WebGPU-branch-only and no-op on the WebGL2 single-pass ETF floor, preserving invariant 8 and the proof:aurora-backend-fallback zero-regression contract.
pitfalls: **Hard sector binning + winner-take-all bands on smooth gradients** — the current painterly.wgsl.ts uses both. Aurora's flat low-structure fields are the pathological worst case (no edges to hide the seam): you get a rotating 8-spoke pinwheel artifact. The soft variance blend (sum m_k*w_k / sum w_k) and Gaussian sector overlap exist precisely to kill this. Do NOT ship the hard form on a gradient backdrop.

**rgba16float is renderable+filterable by default, but rgba32float is NOT filterable without the `float32-filterable` device feature** — the engine's rgba16float choice is safe; if anyone bumps the tensor target to 32-bit for precision they MUST request the optional feature or the smooth pass's linear sampling silently breaks/falls back. Keep the tensor target at rgba16float (16-bit half-float has ample range for J components after the gradient-squared writes).

**Unsmoothed structure tensor = jittery, crawling orientation** — skipping or under-sizing the Gaussian tensor smooth makes the paint shimmer frame-to-frame (orientation noise reads as boiling). The smooth pass is NOT optional; sigma must scale with the Kuwahara radius (~radius/3).

**Cost is O(radius^2 * sectors) per pixel** — at radius 6, 8 sectors, that is ~440 samples/pixel on top of the base field, every frame, full-screen. On a backdrop that runs continuously this is a battery/thermal hazard. Mitigations already partly in place: the offscreen/PRM/tab-hidden park gate (proof:offscreen-pause extends to the WebGPU dispatch), demand-driven schedule. Consider: render the painterly finish at reduced resolution (it is a flatten — half-res upscale is nearly invisible), cap radius on the auto device tier, or bake-once for static (motion=still) presets. The breath-paced motion (0.005-0.010 drift) means the field barely changes between frames — a temporally-amortized or every-Nth-frame Kuwahara is viable.

**WebGPU is production-deployable in 2026 but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available** — all four major engines ship it by default (Safari 26 / macOS Tahoe was last, Nov 2025), but ~5% of sessions still fall to WebGL2. The painterly Kuwahara CANNOT be a hard requirement; the WebGL2 single-pass ETF approximation must remain the honest floor. The wispy-sky DEFAULT must render identically on both paths — only the opt-in painterly mediums diverge.

**Texture filtering across the FBO chain needs explicit linear samplers + clamp-to-edge** — the smooth and Kuwahara passes sample neighbors; edge pixels read outside [0,1]. Use clamp-to-edge addressing and account for texel offset = 1/textureDimensions, or you get dark/wrapped border seams. The current code computes texel correctly; preserve that when refactoring.

**Color space: filter in a perceptually-uniform space, not gamma-sRGB** — variance computed in gamma-sRGB weights highlights wrong and shifts hue on the mean. The engine already centralizes OKLCh/linear math in the shared procedural-color chunk; do the per-sector mean/variance in linear (or OKLab) and close the OETF once at the end, consistent with the AV.W1 single-OETF-source fix. Computing variance per-channel in display space is a subtle but real fidelity bug.

**Sector count is a quality/cost knob, not a free dial** — N=8 is canon; N=4 bands worse, N>8 costs more for diminishing return and can over-smooth the directional character. Keep 8 unless a specific medium wants the coarser/finer look, and keep it consumer-declared (it already is) so the substrate stays generic.

**Per-pixel noise rotation must be STATIC (seeded), not time-varying** — DESIGN.md invariant 7: stroke texture is material, not process. If the kernel-rotation noise animates, the paint 'crawls'. Seed it off spatial coordinate (mulberry32/hashString in utils/prng.ts), never off uTime.

notes.facet: Cellular/Worley + softmax metaball nuclei fields for chunky vs soft region boundaries
sotaTechniques: Smooth-Voronoi as log-sum-exp softmin (IQ): res = -(1/k)·log2(Σ exp2(-k·d)) over the 3x3 cell neighborhood. This is literally a softmax/softmin over feature-point distances where k is the softmax TEMPERATURE — low k (4-8) = soft blended boundaries, high k (32-64) = hard Voronoi cells. It is the canonical 'one knob spans chunky↔soft' operator.

Polynomial/exponential smooth-minimum (smin) with a BLEND-FACTOR return (IQ smin article): the vec2 quadratic form `h=1-min(|a-b|/(4k),1); w=h*h; return (a<b)?vec2(a-w*k, w*0.5):vec2(b-w*k, 1-w*0.5)` returns BOTH the blended distance AND a 0..1 material-id used to lerp the two regions' colors. k maps directly to blend-band thickness in distance units. The CD family (quadratic/cubic/quartic/circular) is rigidity-preserving and LOCAL (only shapes within k units interact); the DD family (exponential/sigmoid/root) distorts everywhere — prefer CD for bounded region blends.

Voronoise (IQ): a 2-axis blend `noise(x,u,v)` where u jitters feature points (0=regular grid→1=Voronoi seeds) and v selects the combine op via `k=1+63·pow(1-v,4)` driving a `w=pow(1-smoothstep(0,1.414,d),k)` weighted average — v=1 → smooth value noise, v=0 → hard cellular. One function continuously spans smooth-gradient ↔ chunky-cell with two intuitive sliders.

Voronoi-edge / bisector distance (IQ voronoilines, the F2-F1 fix): naive F2-F1 gives INCONSISTENT line widths because it isn't a true distance. The two-pass fix finds the nearest cell (pass 1), then measures perpendicular distance to each neighbor's bisector `d = dot(0.5*(mr+r), normalize(r-mr))` (pass 2), giving mathematically-perfect constant-width cell borders — the lever for crisp 'chunky region seams' (cracked-earth / Memphis-block edges).

Distance-metric swap for cell SHAPE (Book of Shaders ch.12): replacing Euclidean `length(diff)` with Manhattan `|x|+|y|` (diamond cells) or Chebyshev `max(|x|,|y|)` (square/blocky cells), or general Minkowski-p, restyles cells from round→angular→rectangular WITHOUT changing the algorithm. The chunky 'Meadow block-like territory' look is a Chebyshev/high-p metric, not a separate code path.

Weighted / power-diagram Voronoi (Wikipedia weighted-Voronoi, power diagrams): per-seed weight modifies the metric — multiplicatively `d/w` (variable-radius circular-arc cells) or additively/power `d² - w` (power diagram, straight-line edges, variable cell size). Produces organically VARIABLE region sizes from equal-spaced seeds — the principled way to get '2-6 amorphous zones of different size' rather than uniform cells.

Anisotropic / elongated region kernels: rotating the difference vector into a per-seed local frame and scaling one axis before the distance (the structure-tensor / elongation trick) stretches cells/blobs along an axis — directly the 'soak-stain bleed' and 'wind-swept aurora curtain' look. glass-ui already does this for the Gaussian nuclei (uNucleiElong/uNucleiAngle); the same rotate-scale applies to a Worley metric.

SDF-union metaball field with smoothmin accumulation (Codrops 2025 droplet metaballs): accumulate per-ball SDFs via `d = smoothMin(d, sdSphere(...), k)` (exponential `-log(exp(-k·d1)+exp(-k·d2))/k`) rather than additive scalar summation — the merge stays a true distance field so the isosurface threshold gives crisp droplet edges, and the smin material-id channel attributes color per dominant ball.
notes.applicability: "glass-ui's `nucleiField` (composition.glsl.ts) is ALREADY a softmax region field — `w = exp(-uSoftmaxBeta·d²/r²)`, accumulate `w·paletteBias` / `w·valueBias`, divide by ΣW — which is mathematically a Gaussian-kernel softmin/log-sum-exp over the nuclei (it differs from IQ smooth-Voronoi only by being a normalized weighted-AVERAGE of palette ids vs a log-domain min of distances). So `uSoftmaxBeta` IS the softmax temperature: the chunky↔soft axis the facet asks for already exists as one uniform. PATH FORWARD: (1) Expose softmaxBeta as a first-class consumer 'edgeHardness' atom in resolveAtoms — low beta = wet-on-wet flood (atmospheric pole), high beta = chunky territory (Meadow/gestural pole); it spans both DESIGN.md stylistic poles with no new code. (2) Replace the naive F1 `cellular()` (currently `sqrt(min(dot(r,r)))`, used only in domainWarp cellular/hybrid modes) with a richer cellular: add the IQ voronoise (u,v) blend so WarpMode gains a continuous fbm↔cellular dial instead of the current discrete fbm|cellular|hybrid trichotomy, and add a Chebyshev/Manhattan metric option so 'cellular' actually yields the BLOCKY territories DESIGN.md §6 Δ01 claims (current Euclidean F1 still gives round-ish warp). (3) Add the two-pass bisector Voronoi-edge as an OPTIONAL region-seam overlay (a crisp hairline between nuclei zones) for the chunky pole — gated behind a new warp/edge sub-mode, single-pass-safe (it's a 5x5 neighborhood, fits invariant 8). (4) Adopt per-nucleus WEIGHTING (power-diagram style: the existing per-nucleus `radius` already plays this role inside the Gaussian via `/(r·r)`, so variable-size zones are present — document it as multiplicatively-weighted-Voronoi-equivalent and consider exposing a separate `weight` from `radius` so size and influence decouple). (5) The smin BLEND-FACTOR (material-id) form is the principled upgrade if/when nuclei coloring moves from averaged paletteBias to a true nearest-zone-with-soft-seam model — it gives crisp chunky seams that still blend over a controllable band `k`, exactly the 'chunky vs soft' boundary control, and the material-id channel maps onto the existing per-zone paletteBias. (6) All of this is OKLCh-clean already: glass-ui interpolates palette in OKLab/OKLCh (mixPaletteOklab), so softening a boundary won't produce the muddy grey midpoint that naive linear blends cause — a real differentiator vs the surveyed CSS/WebGL aurora tools that lerp in sRGB."
pitfalls: DD-family softmins (exponential/sigmoid/root) and the Gaussian softmax distort the field NON-LOCALLY — every nucleus pulls on every pixel, so adding more nuclei at low beta washes the whole frame toward grey-average. glass-ui's normalized weighted-average already mitigates this (it's an average, not an unbounded sum) but raising MAX_NUCLEI without raising beta will mud the palette. Prefer CD-family (quadratic/cubic) smin or a high-enough beta floor if a true distance-field union is ever adopted.

Worley/voronoise costs scale with the neighbor window: F1 needs 3x3 (9 hash22), the bisector-edge needs 5x5 (25 taps) in pass 2, voronoise needs 5x5. Aurora already runs domainWarp's double-fBm (up to 5 octaves × value-noise) PLUS the medium passes PLUS the structure tensor (3x3 Sobel) on a single fragment pass under profile:budget. A naive cellular-edge add could blow the per-pixel ALU budget on mobile — gate richer cellular behind the warpMode that needs it and keep the wispy-sky DEFAULT on cheap fBm.

hash22 here is `fract(sin(p)*43758.5453)` — the classic sin-hash has platform-dependent precision (different `sin` LSBs across GPUs/drivers) that shows as cell-pattern seams differing between devices; the bisector-edge method amplifies any hash mismatch into visible width jitter. If cellular fidelity grows, migrate the cellular hash to the integer/PCG-style hash glass-ui could share with the blob, and verify the WGSL twin matches at 1e-6 (proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence already polices the color core — extend the discipline to any new noise the WGSL path mirrors).

Manhattan/Chebyshev metrics break the rotational symmetry that hides the grid — angular cells make the underlying square lattice VISIBLE (axis-aligned diamonds/squares), which reads as a tiling artifact, not organic territory. Combine the metric swap with the existing domainWarp (warp the coordinate BEFORE the cellular lookup) so the lattice is hidden, exactly as DESIGN.md invariant 2 prescribes (boundaries warped by Quilez-double-fBm).

F2-F1 naive edges give inconsistent line widths (the documented IQ failure) — if a future 'cracked region seam' uses thresholded F2-F1 it will look wrong (some seams fat, some hairline). Use the two-pass bisector form for any crisp-edge work; never threshold raw F2-F1.

Voronoise's v-axis uses `k=1+63·pow(1-v,4)` and a `pow(...,k)` per-tap — at v→0 (hard cells) k→64 and the pow is sharp/expensive; the falloff also assumes the smoothstep range 0..1.414 (the 2-cell diagonal) — porting it must keep that 1.414 constant or cells clip. It's a different falloff family than glass-ui's `exp(-beta·d²)` Gaussian, so a voronoise warp and the Gaussian nuclei field won't share a single 'hardness' uniform — they'd need separate temperature knobs (don't conflate softmaxBeta with the voronoise v).

The 2x2 (vs 3x3) neighbor optimization (Gustavson) introduces edge discontinuities — do NOT shrink the window to save ALU on the region/edge passes; the discontinuities read as seams in a slow-drifting backdrop where the eye has time to find them.

Region-field changes interact with the painterly mediums: the structure-tensor/ETF orientation (AW.W4) derives stroke direction from `luma(sampleBase)` of the composed field — sharpening region boundaries (higher beta / cellular edges) makes the ETF coherence spike at seams, so strokes will hug the new hard edges. That's desirable (Van Gogh iso-band strokes) but means a chunkier field auto-changes the painterly look; tune beta and the medium together, not in isolation.
