notes.facet: Oil-pastel rendering — broken scumble, waxy burnish, paper-tooth show-through; what real oil-pastel art looks like up close
sotaTechniques: KUBELKA-MUNK PIGMENT MIXING (Mixbox / Spectral.js / spectral.glsl) — the headline. Real paint mixes subtractively via per-wavelength absorption(K)/scattering(S): blue+yellow→green, not the gray that linear-RGB/OKLab lerps produce. Spectral.js lifts an sRGB triplet to a 38-band reflectance curve (380-750nm, Scott Burns LHTSS, weights over 7 primaries W/C/M/Y/R/G/B), mixes K/S by concentration C=f²·T²·L, recombines R=1+(K/S)−√((K/S)²+2(K/S)), and projects back through CIE-1931+D65. spectral.glsl ships this as a fragment-callable `spectral_mix(c1,s1,f1, c2,s2,f2, ...)` for 2-4 colors. Mixbox is the closed-source twin (RGB→7D latent→mix→RGB).

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA FILTER (Kyprianidis & Kang; Papari circular extension) — THE canonical 'make a gradient read as oil paint' operator. Box→circular kernel split into 8 sectors weighted by a Gaussian (or the cheaper polynomial weight `max(0,(x+η)−λy²)²`, η≈0.1 λ≈0.5); output the sector mean with lowest luminance variance, so flat regions smooth into paint-blobs while edges stay crisp. The ANISOTROPIC variant warps the circular kernel into an ellipse oriented+elongated by the structure-tensor eigenvectors — strokes hug edges. Inherently MULTI-PASS (tensor pass → smoothed tensor → filter pass → tonemap).

STRUCTURE-TENSOR + EDGE-TANGENT-FLOW orientation (Kyprianidis-Kang 2009) — Sobel→J=[[Gx²,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy²]], eigen-decompose (θ=½·atan2(2Jxy,Jxx−Jyy)); the MINOR eigenvector is the edge tangent (stroke direction), coherence A=(λ₁−λ₂)/(λ₁+λ₂) gates a blend toward a smooth fallback in flat zones. Gaussian-SMOOTHING the tensor before eigen-decomposition (the multi-pass upgrade) removes the per-pixel jitter the single-tap form suffers and yields the LIC (line-integral-convolution) smear that drags color ALONG the field.

PIGMENT-ON-TOOTH DEPOSITION + SCUMBLE (Murakami & Tsuruno 2002, 'Pastel-Like Rendering'; height-field charcoal/pastel/crayon models) — model the support as a height field; pigment lands on tooth PEAKS and skips VALLEYS by thresholding stroke coverage against the paper height (smoothstep over a pressure-lowered floor). SCUMBLE = a broken upper layer at coverage<1 dragged over a base so the lower color reads through the gaps → OPTICAL mixing (the eye blends the broken film, the pointillism/broken-color principle). Net-pigment-transfer accounting (pigment on tip, pigment already on paper, max deposition) is the material-truth refinement.

WAXY BURNISH as a low-roughness BROAD specular lobe — oil-pastel binder (non-drying oil + wax) gives a soft sheen distinct from oil-impasto's sharp glint. Model as a wide Blinn lobe (low exponent ~6) whose intensity GROWS with pigment build-up/layer count (burnish), lit by a movable light over a normal derived from the paper-height gradient. Sgraffito (scratch-through to reveal under-layers) is the inverse move — a negative-coverage scratch mask.

BROKEN COLOR via per-cell OKLCh pigment jitter + DITHERED grain — hash stable pigment patches and jitter hue(±~16°)/value(±~14%) in OKLCh (NOT random RGB noise) so it reads as 'broken paint' not chroma snow; add band-limited high-frequency paper grain / ordered-Bayer dither to break gradient banding the way real pigment scatter does (the Nyquist-aware noise discipline keeps it from aliasing under DPR/zoom).
notes.applicability: ["KUBELKA-MUNK is the single biggest fidelity upgrade available to our oil-pastel/crayon path AND the whole palette interp. We currently mix the palette + per-stroke broken color in OKLCh arc (`mixPaletteOklchArc`, `brokenColorJitter`) — perceptually smooth but still ADDITIVE-ish; it cannot produce the subtractive hue-bend (blue+yellow→green, not muddy lerp) that makes scumbled/overlapped pastel layers read as real pigment. PATH: splice a `spectral.glsl`-style K-S mixer into the SHARED `procedural-color.glsl.ts` chunk (alongside the Ottosson matrices, so aurora.frag.ts AND metaball.frag.ts inherit it and `proof:single-color-core`/`proof:shader-shared-source` freeze it), then route `mediumCrayon`'s scumble `mix(paper,deposited,...)` and `mixPaletteOklchArc` through it behind a uniform/`brokenColor`-style knob. Cost is the hazard (see pitfalls) — gate it to the painterly mediums and consider a precomputed 7-primary reflectance LUT.", "ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA is ALREADY the staged AW.W7 WebGPU multi-pass headline in DESIGN.md (§2 inv.8, §10 Δ09) — this research confirms it is the correct, canonical choice and supplies the exact recipe: Papari 8-sector circular kernel + polynomial sector weights `max(0,(x+η)−λy²)²` (η=0.1,λ=0.5) for the real-time budget, structure-tensor eigen-ellipse for orientation, lowest-variance sector select. Our `painterly.wgsl.ts` already declares `PAINTERLY_KUWAHARA_SECTORS`/`PAINTERLY_TENSOR_FORMAT` as the consumer-owned N-pass seam (proof:webgpu-substrate-single) — the path is to fill that pass with the Papari/Kyprianidis recipe. The oil-pastel medium specifically benefits: Kuwahara AFTER deposition gives the 'blended from a distance, broken up close' look that scumbling is.", "STRUCTURE TENSOR — we already ship the single-tap closed-form `structureTensorField()` and force `tensor` orientation for painterly mediums (the keystone, landed). The SOTA delta is the GAUSSIAN-SMOOTHED multi-tap tensor + LIC smear — also correctly staged for WebGPU (DESIGN §7 painterly notes, Δ09). Our single-pass tap is honest as the orientation SOURCE; the WebGPU smoothing/LIC is the finish. No change to the verdict, but our DESIGN's principal-angle math matches the literature exactly (good — keep the `atan2(2Jxy,Jxx−Jyy)` robust form, it's the published one).", "DEPOSITION + SCUMBLE + BURNISH — our `mediumCrayon` (uMedium 4/6) ALREADY implements a credible version of all three (toothFloor pressure-deposition, scumbleCoverage<1 broken upper pass, broad wax sheen `pow(dot(N,H),6.0)` growing with build-up). This research VALIDATES the model against Murakami-Tsuruno + the artist-technique corpus and pinpoints concrete refinements: (a) make scumble OPTICAL — currently it `mix`es toward deposited color; per the broken-color principle it should let the genuinely-different LOWER palette color show through, which K-M mixing would amplify; (b) add a sgraffito/scratch axis (negative coverage) as a cheap high-value gesture; (c) the burnish sheen could key off an explicit per-pixel LAYER-COUNT accumulator rather than `deposit*scumbleMask`.", "GRAIN/DITHER — our post already does `col += (hash−0.5)·paperGrain`. The SOTA note is to make it band-limited/Nyquist-aware (or ordered-Bayer) so it doesn't alias under DPR changes and zoom, and to keep it as the anti-banding layer that masks the OKLCh→sRGB quantization the deep palettes expose. Low-effort, high-portability-safety.", "PLACEHOLDER/FALLBACK — the CSS-gradient placeholder (Aurora.vue, `paletteToCssGradient`) and the `renderMode:'css'` permanent surface get none of this. modern-web-guidance 'visually-texture-content' (CSS Masks) could add a static paper-tooth/scumble texture to the placeholder so the still fallback reads as pastel rather than a flat gradient — a cheap, no-GPU win that keeps the two-pole aesthetic intact when WebGL/WebGPU is unavailable."]
pitfalls: KUBELKA-MUNK COST in a single-pass WebGL2 fragment shader is the dominant hazard. A full 38-band spectral mix per pixel per stroke-layer is far too expensive for our budget (4 stroke layers × per-pixel mixing inside `profile:budget`). spectral.glsl's `spectral_mix` is already a reduced 7-primary form; even so it must be GATED to the painterly mediums (NOT the smooth/default wispy-sky path, which must stay cheap and identical on both backends) and ideally reduced to a 2-color mix or a precomputed reflectance LUT. Spectral.js's JS lib uses 64-bit + memoization — neither is available in a GLSL `highp` (mediump on some mobile GPUs) per-pixel context; precision loss in the R=1+(K/S)−√(...) recombine can produce NaN/black pixels. Validate against the existing `proof:aurora-space-gamma` / OETF seam.

MULTI-PASS BAN (invariant 8) — anisotropic Kuwahara, smoothed structure tensor, and LIC are FUNDAMENTALLY multi-pass and CANNOT land on the WebGL2 fallback. This is already correctly fenced (WebGPU-only, AW.W7). The portability hazard is regression: WebGPU is production-deployable in 2026 but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available (~95/5 split per DESIGN §7), and Safari/iOS only shipped it 2025-11. The WebGL2 single-pass path MUST stay the declared zero-regression fallback and render the wispy-sky default IDENTICALLY — do not let a K-M or Kuwahara enhancement silently change the default look (`proof:aurora-backend-fallback` + the DEFAULT-PRESERVING `resolveAtoms` roundtrip guard this).

KUWAHARA OVER-DENATURING — Heckel and the literature both warn large kernels erase too much structure ('boxy brush artifacts' from square kernels; over-smoothing from big radii). For an abstract gradient with no subject matter, an over-aggressive Kuwahara can flatten the nuclei field into mush and KILL the broken-color/scumble texture we deliberately add. Tune kernel radius small and apply AFTER deposition, not as a replacement for it.

K-M PALETTE DRIFT vs OKLCh — switching palette interpolation from OKLCh arc to Kubelka-Munk will VISIBLY change every preset's midtones (that's the point — but it's a breaking visual change). Per the no-backwards-compat memory rule this is acceptable as a clean break, but it will move all 11 authored presets' look; they live in the consumer (`demo/stories/aurora/presets.ts`) and would need re-tuning. Gate behind a knob and treat preset re-bake as part of the wave.

BROKEN-COLOR / SCUMBLE can read as NOISE not paint if jitter is in RGB or unbounded — our existing OKLCh-bounded jitter (±16°/±14%) is the correct discipline; do NOT widen it chasing 'more texture'. Same for paper grain: unbounded high-freq hash aliases under DPR/zoom and shimmers under motion (and our stroke texture is supposed to be STATIC material, not process — invariant 7). Keep grain band-limited and static.

DERIVATIVE-BASED RELIGHT (dFdx/dFdy on paper-height) for the burnish normal is screen-space and DPR/zoom-dependent; it can produce inconsistent sheen across devices and flicker at tile boundaries. It's already in use for impasto; extending it to the wax lobe inherits the same hazard. The WebGPU multi-pass path can compute a real smoothed height-gradient instead.

SPECTRAL.JS LICENSE/PORT — spectral.glsl is a community GLSL port (MIT-ish) but Mixbox is CC-BY-NC for the trained LUT (non-commercial) — do NOT pull Mixbox's lookup table into a shipped library. Spectral.js (rvanwijnen, Kubelka-Munk from first principles) is the safe open-source basis; hand-author the GLSL into the shared chunk (matches the zero-dep, no-Three.js/TSL posture the WGSL twin already follows).

notes.facet: Van Gogh brushstroke synthesis — atomic directional strokes, impasto ridges, energy-graded length (long in lights, dabs in darks), Starry-Night-class congruence WITHOUT subject matter
pitfalls: FLOAT TEXTURE PORTABILITY: the smoothed structure tensor MUST be RGBA16F (gradient magnitudes exceed [0,1]; an 8-bit LDR target clips to garbage). The engine's PAINTERLY_TENSOR_FORMAT='rgba16float' is correct — do NOT upgrade to rgba32float: float32-renderable RGBA is NOT universal on mobile GPUs/browsers (Chrome on many phones lacks 32-bit-float render targets). 16F is the portable HDR-intermediate.

MULTI-PASS IS WEBGPU-ONLY (invariant 8): the smoothed multi-tap tensor, LIC smear, and anisotropic Kuwahara are genuinely multi-pass (FBO ping-pong) operators a single WebGL2 fragment shader cannot express. The WebGL2 fallback stays the single-pass ETF approximation; the painterly finish degrades, it does not break. Keep the N-pass seam in the CONSUMER (aurora gpuRuntime), not the substrate.

KUWAHARA KILLS THE BRUSH: too-aggressive anisotropic Kuwahara (large radius, high q) FLATTENS everything and DESTROYS the atomic-stroke texture — the opposite of impasto. Kuwahara is an edge-preserving SMOOTHER; per-stroke ridge/streak texture must composite AFTER or the two fight. Energy-grade the Kuwahara radius DOWN in the lights to preserve long-stroke detail.

STRUCTURE-TENSOR NOISE IN FLAT ZONES: where the nuclei field is near-flat the tensor is noise-dominated and the minor eigenvector spins randomly — strokes read as jitter. The coherence-weighted mix(fallbackDir, tangent, A) is mandatory; without the Gaussian PRE-smoothing of J (the multi-pass step) the single-pass small-tap field is inherently noisier — manage expectations on the WebGL2 floor.
atan2 DEGENERACY: theta=0.5*atan2(2*Jxy,Jxx-Jyy) is robust, but the v=(lambda-Jyy,Jxy) eigenvector formula collapses to zero when Jxy~0 — the engine correctly uses atan2; keep it.

ENERGY-GRADING INVERSION RISK: long-in-lights/short-in-darks must key off PERCEPTUAL luma of the BASE field (not post-impasto color) or the relight feeds back and oscillates. Sample base luma BEFORE the medium overlay (sampleBase ordering does this).

BROKEN-COLOR OVERSHOOT: pushing complementary hues too hard reads as RGB noise not paint. Starry-Night congruence is BOUNDED variation around a palette anchor (the engine's ~+/-16deg hue / +/-12% chroma cap is the right register); divisionism is juxtaposition of NEARBY hues, not random color.

WEBGPU DEPLOYABLE BUT NOT 'BASELINE WIDELY AVAILABLE' (Safari 26 default-on was late-2025; ~5% of sessions still WebGL2-only): never make the painterly headline a hard requirement. The wispy-sky default must render identically on both paths; multi-pass is a capability-gated enhancement only.

PERFORMANCE: best-of-9-neighbor placement is already 9x base-field samples/pixel; a 3-radius coarse-to-fine pass triples that. Stay inside profile:budget — the multi-scale cascade is best ONLY on the WebGPU multi-pass branch (render each scale to an FBO) rather than unrolled in the single WebGL2 fragment program.

LIC COST: per-pixel streamline integration (Runge-Kutta) is expensive; use a short fixed step count and the LIC-R fast formulation, gated behind the WebGPU park machinery (skip when offscreen/PRM-reduced/paused like every other pass).
sotaTechniques: STRUCTURE-TENSOR / EDGE-TANGENT-FLOW (ETF) ORIENTATION (Kang/Lee/Chui 2007; Kyprianidis 2011). Build J=[[Gx^2,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy^2]] from Sobel-luma gradients, Gaussian-SMOOTH J, take the MINOR-eigenvector (edge tangent) as stroke direction with coherence A=(L1-L2)/(L1+L2). Strokes hug painted iso-bands not a global angle; smoothing is the load-bearing step the single-pass form skips. ENGINE already ships single-pass (structureTensorField, 3x3); reference eigen-math (tfm.glsl) confirmed correct.

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA + POLYNOMIAL WEIGHTING (Kyprianidis/Semmo NPAR 2010) — the canonical make-a-gradient-read-as-oil-paint operator. 8 polynomial-weighted sectors of an ELLIPTICAL kernel squeezed along the ETF: a=radius*clamp((alpha+A)/alpha,0.1,2.0), b=radius*clamp(alpha/(alpha+A),0.1,2.0), alpha=1.0; sector weights z=max(0,v.y+(0.33-3.77*v.x^2))^2 (zeta~0.33 eta~3.77), Gaussian g=exp(-3.125*dot_v)/sum; final SOFT blend w=1/(1+(255*sigma)^q), q~8 (NOT hard lowest-variance winner). Edges crisp, flats flatten to paint.

MULTI-SCALE COARSE-TO-FINE SBR (Hertzmann SIGGRAPH 1998). Paint in layers of DECREASING brush radius: large-brush sketch first, smaller brushes ONLY where canvas differs from a blurred reference (the residual field). Long curved strokes follow near-constant-color curves. The principled engine for long-in-lights/dabs-in-darks as a SCALE cascade, not a single-pass length lerp.

HEIGHT-FIELD IMPASTO + GGX RELIGHT (Differentiable Stroke Planning arXiv 2024). Canvas weave C=C0+dC[fbm(x)+w*sin(20 x.dx)sin(20 x.dy)]; per-stroke ridge h~=h+A*SUM wk*sin(kk*f0*r^-1*l+phi_k), freq ratios (1.0,1.8), random phases for bristle grooves; thickness-aware canvas-vs-paint inverse blend. Normals n=normalize([-s*grad H,1]); shade GGX roughness 0.3, F0=0.08 — physically grounded vs Blinn-Phong.

STARRY-NIGHT TURBULENCE SCALING (Aragon 2006; Hidden Turbulence in The Starry Night, Physics of Fluids 2024). Luminance Fourier power spectrum follows -5/3 Kolmogorov across the visible-eddy band and -1 Batchelor below the smallest eddies; brushstroke BRIGHTNESS stands in for kinetic energy. Generator prior: stroke size/brightness/spacing power-law-distributed across scale, brightness coupled to local energy — the long+bright-in-lights/dab+dark-in-darks grading with named exponents.

BROKEN COLOR / DIVISIONISM (Van Gogh technique; optical mixing + simultaneous contrast). Adjacent strokes carry DIFFERENT pure hues (complementary pairs blue/orange, red/green) that fuse optically into luminosity/shimmer; opposed directions create moire movement. SOTA refinement over symmetric jitter: push neighboring cells toward OPPOSITE OKLCh hue/temperature poles (directional complementary dab), not i.i.d. symmetric +/-16deg jitter.

LINE-INTEGRAL-CONVOLUTION (LIC) FLOW SMEAR (Cabral-Leedom; Kyprianidis coherence-enhancing 2011; LIC-R SCITEPRESS 2025). Convolve ALONG the ETF: trace a short streamline fwd/back per pixel (Runge-Kutta), box-average — output correlates along field lines, decorrelates orthogonally, giving smeared directional paint coherence. LIC-R (2025) is the fast formulation. The WebGPU multi-pass finish the single-pass WebGL2 path cannot afford.

GAUSSIAN-SPLAT-SEEDED / NEURAL SBR (Differentiable Stroke Planning dual-parameterization 2024; MambaPainter, BrushGaussian 2024/2025). Seed strokes by image FEATURE DENSITY (high-residual regions, non-max suppression) not a uniform grid, grow polylines by gradient-ascent on the error field (momentum d=0.8*grad+0.2*d_prev), couple polyline<->Bezier; cuts stroke count 30-50%. Informs a density/saliency cell-jitter prior over the uniform bestOil grid.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for glass-ui aurora — the source image is the procedural nuclei field (no subject matter), exactly congruent since every operator reads a generated luma/color field not a photo. The engine ALREADY ships the keystones: single-pass ETF orientation (structureTensorField), energy-graded length via luma*coherence (bestOil uMedium==5), real height->normal->Blinn impasto relight (relightImpasto), OKLCh broken-color jitter, and a STAGED WebGPU anisotropic-Kuwahara pass (painterly.wgsl.ts). AX-wave deltas: (1) MULTI-SCALE bestOil — 2-3 brush radii coarse-to-fine, fine dabs only where the coarse layer's luma differs from a blurred base (Hertzmann), turning the single-scale length-lerp into a true Starry-Night scale cascade; cite -5/3 / -1 as the cell-size-vs-scale distribution prior. (2) WebGPU Kuwahara from HARD lowest-variance-winner to SOFT polynomial blend w=1/(1+(255*sigma)^q), q~8, with canonical eccentricity a/b=radius*clamp((alpha+/-A)/alpha,0.1,2.0), alpha=1.0 — matches the Kyprianidis reference and removes sector-boundary banding. (3) DIRECTIONAL complementary broken color — brokenColorJitter pushes neighboring cells toward opposite OKLCh hue poles (divisionism) for optical-mixing shimmer. (5) On WebGPU add the LIC smear along the smoothed ETF before/with Kuwahara — DESIGN.md already names it; target LIC-R (2025). (6) Optionally seed bestOil cells by feature density (luma residual) over the uniform grid for fewer, better strokes. All read existing seams (nuclei field, shared OKLCh, structure tensor) — no new substrate; the wispy-sky default stays untouched (energy-grading fires only under uMedium==5).

notes.facet: Impasto height-field → normal → relight (Blinn-Phong) for view/light-dependent paint relief; catch-light vs baked rim
sotaTechniques: GGX/Cook-Torrance microfacet relight (the 2026 SOTA replacement for Blinn-Phong). The current state of the art for impasto relighting (Liu et al. 2026, 'Differentiable Stroke Planning', CVPR-track) does NOT use Blinn-Phong: it shades the height field with a GGX microfacet BRDF L = (rho/pi)*Ld + (D*F*G)/(4*(n.v)*(n.l))*Ls, using Trowbridge-Reitz GGX for D, Smith-Schlick-GGX for the geometry term G, and Fresnel-Schlick for F, with the published paint constants roughness alpha_r=0.3, Fresnel base reflectance F0=0.08 (the canonical non-metallic-pigment value), and light intensities (Ld,Ls)=(1.0,0.8). This 'accentuates both canvas microstructure and impasto depth under directional illumination' far better than a fixed-shininess Blinn lobe.

Height-to-slope normal with an explicit slope-scale s (the universal normal-from-height formula). n(x) = normalize([-s * grad H(x), 1]). The single tuning knob is the scalar slope-scale 's' (= our heightScale x the dFdx multiplier collapsed into one named constant) that converts pixel-level height delta into a shading-consistent slope; the whole relief-depth-vs-flatness tradeoff lives in that one number.

Schlick-Fresnel rim as the TRUE view-dependent term (the principled 'catch-light vs baked rim' resolution). Fresnel = pow(clamp(1 - dot(N,V), 0, 1), p) with the exponent p as the rim-falloff knob (p=5 thin rim, p~0.5 broad sheen). For a backdrop with V fixed at (0,0,1), the N.V Fresnel reads as a grazing-angle sheen on the steep flanks of impasto ridges — this is the physically-correct, normal-derived rim that the DESIGN.md 'baked-rim RETIRED' arc was reaching for. The old vec3(0.18,0.15,0.11) constant rim was screen-space-fixed (a phantom UL light); a Fresnel term is height-derived and therefore moves correctly with the relief.

Two-component structure-texture height field (Liu et al. 2026 §6). The target relief is built as H = fuse(H_depth, H_texture): a coarse depth-ordering field (from the scene/nuclei field) PLUS a high-frequency texture field extracted from the CIELAB luminance high-pass. For us this maps cleanly onto: nuclei/iso-band field = the macro 'depth' term, canvas tooth + bristle fbm = the micro 'texture' term — already the two ingredients our relightImpasto sums (height + canvasBase), but the paper formalizes blending them with a luminance high-pass rather than ad-hoc weights.

Procedural impasto ridge model (Liu et al. 2026 Eq. 13). Per-stroke height is perturbed h~ = h + A(r) * sum_k w_k * sin(kappa_k * f0 / r * l(x) + phi_k) — a small sum of sinusoids along the stroke arclength l(x), amplitude A scaled by stroke radius r, with the paper's blend alpha=0.8 so thin strokes inherit canvas roughness and thick strokes (gamma->1) override it. This is a principled, controllable version of our fbm-perturbed ridge term and gives explicit bristle-frequency control.

Geometric specular anti-aliasing / Toksvig roughness widening (Kaplanyan, NVIDIA GDC 2016; Hill SIGGRAPH 2012). When relighting a NOISY procedural height field, the sub-pixel normal variance must be folded into roughness: roughness'^2 = roughness^2 + k * (|dFdx(N)|^2 + |dFdy(N)|^2) (or the Toksvig shortened-averaged-normal measure). This is the canonical cure for specular shimmer/strobing on high-frequency relief — directly applicable because our height field is fbm-driven and our shininess is currently un-filtered.

Higher-quality normals than raw dFdx (cross/Sobel central differences via explicit taps). Raw dFdx/dFdy on a height computes the gradient over a 2x2 pixel QUAD, producing blocky, faceted normals (enkisoftware, GameDev.net). The SOTA-for-quality alternative is an explicit 4-tap (or Sobel 3x3) central difference: sample height at +/-delta in x and y and form grad = ((h(+x)-h(-x)), (h(+y)-h(-y)))/(2*delta). Sobel's Gaussian-weighted 3x3 is smoother (noise-robust) at higher cost. Trades a re-evaluation of the height function for quad-free, smooth relief.

Self-shadowing / relief depth cues (Baxter IMPaSTo 2004; de Carpentier-Bidarra 2009). The foundational interactive paint model (Baxter, Wendt & Lin, NPAR 2004) stores paint as a height-field + spatially-varying BRDF and relights under any illuminant; de Carpentier's GPU heightfield brushes (FDG 2009) add cheap screen-space soft-shadow / occlusion from the height gradient. A 1-2 tap height-march toward uLightDir yields a soft contact-shadow in the grooves between ridges — the strongest non-specular depth cue, and single-pass-cheap.

Cursor/device-orientation as the virtual light (the correct view-dependence model for a camera-less backdrop). A backdrop has no real camera, so view-dependent relief must be DRIVEN: the SOTA pattern (parallax.js, DeviceMotion gyro parallax) is to bind the light/view proxy to pointer position or DeviceOrientationEvent so tilting the device or moving the cursor sweeps the catch-light across the relief. This is exactly the 'cursor-as-light drives uLightDir' axis already specced for AW.W8 — the research validates it as THE idiomatic substitute for a non-existent camera.
notes.applicability: OUR ENGINE TODAY (brush.glsl.ts relightImpasto + mediums.glsl.ts mediumOilPastel waxBurnish): height -> normal via normalize(vec3(-dFdx(h)*40, -dFdy(h)*40, 1/heightScale)) -> Blinn-Phong (H=normalize(L+V), spec=pow(max(dot(N,H),0),shininess), shininess=mix(8,64,height*2)) from a movable uLightDir, in LINEAR before aces(). This is already a real height->normal->relight with a catch-light (the baked vec3 rim is correctly retired), so we are NOT behind on the architecture — only on the BRDF and the normal/AA quality. PATH FORWARD, in priority order: (1) Swap the Blinn-Phong lobe for a compact GGX+Smith+Schlick-Fresnel lobe with the paper's paint constants (alpha_r=0.3, F0=0.08); cost over Blinn is small (per Filmic Worlds/UE4) and it is the single biggest fidelity lever — it gives energy-conserving glints that sharpen with impasto thickness for free (drive alpha_r DOWN with height instead of shininess UP). (2) Add a Schlick-Fresnel N.V rim term as the principled view-dependent sheen on ridge flanks (exponent as a uniform) — this is the 'catch-light vs baked-rim' resolution: a height-derived rim that moves with relief, not a fixed RGB constant. (3) Fold screen-space normal variance into roughness (geometric specular AA / Toksvig) to kill shimmer on the fbm height — mandatory once GGX sharpens the lobe, because a sharp lobe on a noisy normal strobes. (4) Replace raw dFdx/dFdy on height with a 4-tap central difference (or Sobel) so the relief stops reading as 2x2-quad facets; this also collapses the magic *40 and 1/heightScale into one named slope-scale 's' per the canonical n=normalize([-s*gradH,1]). (5) Collapse the duplicated normal-from-height + Blinn lobe in relightImpasto (brush) and waxBurnish (mediums) into ONE shared relight(height, normal, lightDir, roughness, F0) helper in the shared procedural-color chunk — both call sites currently hand-roll the same N/L/H/spec, a single-source opportunity matching the AW.W5 OKLCh-share discipline. (6) For WebGPU (AW.W7), the structure-texture height fusion (depth term + LIC-smeared texture term) and a 1-2 tap self-shadow march toward uLightDir are the multi-pass enhancements that lift it from 'lit relief' to 'volumetric impasto'. (7) Bind uLightDir to pointer AND DeviceOrientation (AW.W8) — the camera-less-backdrop SOTA is to make the user the light.
pitfalls: Specular shimmer / strobing on the noisy procedural height field. A sharp GGX (or high-shininess Blinn) lobe over an fbm-perturbed normal aliases violently under motion — the single biggest hazard. MUST add geometric specular AA (widen roughness by screen-space normal variance, Kaplanyan/Toksvig) the moment you sharpen the lobe. Our current shininess=mix(8,64,...) is already at risk on the thick-impasto end.

dFdx/dFdy on height = 2x2-quad faceting + float precision. Raw screen-space derivatives compute the gradient over a 2x2 pixel quad, so the relief reads blocky/faceted and is half-resolution; the *40 magic multiplier is also DPR/zoom-dependent (a derivative of a 0..1 field scales with pixel size). Prefer explicit central-difference taps; if keeping dFdx, the relief depth silently changes with DPR — a portability hazard for the same config across screens.

No real camera = no free view-dependence. Fresnel/rim with V fixed at (0,0,1) only varies with N (the relief flanks), which is correct but STATIC — the relief looks lit but inert until uLightDir (or a tilted V) is animated/driven. Without the cursor/device-orientation drive (AW.W8) the 'view/light-dependent' promise is unfulfilled; the relief is a still-life. Budget the light-drive as part of the impasto deliverable, not a separate nicety.

WebGL2 dFdx requires the right context/precision; GLSL ES 3.00 has dFdx natively but fwidth/derivative quality is 'coarse' vs 'fine' is undefined by default — relief can differ between GPUs. Cross-check on Apple/Intel/NVIDIA; consider GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER_DERIVATIVE_HINT if available, or explicit taps to be hint-independent.

Energy / tonemap ordering. GGX is energy-conserving ONLY if you do NOT then double-tonemap or add it after aces(); the spec lock (proof:aurora-space-gamma) keeps relight in linear before aces — preserve that. A naive GGX port that forgets the 1/(4*(n.v)*(n.l)) denominator or clamps n.l to a tiny epsilon will spark fireflies on near-grazing ridges (the classic GGX hot-pixel); clamp the denominator, not just the dots.

Over-relief on the smooth/atmospheric pole. The impasto relight must be GATED by uImpasto*relief (it already is) — but with GGX's stronger response, a non-zero impasto on a 'smooth' medium preset will suddenly read as plastic/CGI sheen. Re-baseline the default impasto for the wispy-sky preset after the BRDF swap or the DEFAULT-PRESERVING roundtrip (proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip) breaks visually even if numerically intact.

Baked-rim regression temptation. The fixed RGB rim is cheap and deterministic; under perf pressure someone may re-add it 'just for the still default'. That reintroduces the screen-space-fixed phantom light the W4.2 arc retired. The principled cheap fallback is a Fresnel N.V term (still height-derived), not a constant — keep the rim on the cascade of the normal, never a constant.

The optimization machinery is irrelevant to us.

notes.facet: Stroke-based rendering (SBR) literature — greedy stroke placement, curved spines, layered strokes, bristle texture
sotaTechniques: GREEDY STROKE PLACEMENT (Litwinowicz 1997 / Hertzmann 1998). Classical SBR seeds strokes greedily where the current canvas most disagrees with a blurred reference: tile the image into a grid of size fg*R (grid factor fg~1.0, brush radius R), sum the per-cell area error E=sum|canvas-ref| over each cell, and if E>T (approximation threshold) deposit a new stroke at the cell's single MAX-error pixel. This 'paint where it's worst' loop is the canonical algorithm. OUR engine's bestOil() does a structurally identical but PROCEDURAL inversion: it scans a 3x3 cell neighborhood and keeps the stroke of MAX coverage (best.coverage), with a density-gated hash threshold for sparsity — the same greedy 'best-of-neighborhood' selection, but coverage-driven rather than error-driven since there is no target image.

LAYERED COARSE-TO-FINE PAINTING (Hertzmann 1998, the defining contribution). Build the painting as an ordered stack of layers, largest brush first: for each radius R in a descending list (canonical {8,4,2} or {R, R/2, R/4}), Gaussian-blur the reference by sigma=fs*R (blur factor fs~0.5), paint a full greedy layer, then move to the smaller brush which only repaints where the coarse layer still differs from the (less-blurred) reference by >T. Big brushes lay the tonal field; small brushes add detail only at edges. This is the single most important quality lever and it is NOT yet in our engine — our oil path is single-scale (one cellSize, optional strokeLayers:1|2 crosshatch). A coarse-to-fine multi-radius cascade (2-3 descending cellSizes, each gated by the residual of the previous) is the highest-value port.

CURVED-SPLINE STROKES VIA GRADIENT-NORMAL INTEGRATION (Hertzmann 1998). A long curved stroke is grown by stepping along the EDGE TANGENT (the gradient NORMAL, perpendicular to luminance gradient): from the seed, step a distance R, set new direction = gradient-normal at the new point, then apply a curvature filter dir = fc*newDir + (1-fc)*lastDir (fc~1.0 = follow edges tightly, fc~0 = straight strokes) and flip if it would double back (dot<0); stop at maxStrokeLength (~16) or when stroke color diverges from canvas. Control points become a Catmull-Rom/B-spline. OUR engine uses a fixed quadratic-bulge spine (bend = 4*K*t*(1-t)) — a single parabola, not a multi-segment integrated spline. The path forward: replace the fixed bulge with a SHORT multi-step integration along the structureTensorField minor-eigenvector (2-4 segments), giving genuinely meandering strokes that hug iso-bands instead of one symmetric arc.

STRUCTURE-TENSOR + EDGE-TANGENT-FLOW ORIENTATION (Kyprianidis/Kang). Orientation is derived from the image's own structure: form J=[[Gx^2,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy^2]] (smoothed), eigen-decompose closed-form via theta=0.5*atan2(2*Jxy,Jxx-Jyy); the MINOR eigenvector (-sin,cos) is the edge tangent = stroke direction, coherence A=(l1-l2)/(l1+l2) gates tangent-vs-fallback. OUR engine ALREADY DOES THIS (structureTensorField in mediums.glsl.ts, strokeOrient:'tensor'). The SOTA upgrade is KANG'S ETF refinement: iteratively smooth the tangent field (3 iterations) with a nonlinear kernel weighting neighbors by spatial ws (box radius), magnitude wm=0.5*(1+tanh(g(y)-g(x))) (let strong gradients dominate), and direction wd=|t(x).t(y)| (align same-direction, suppress orthogonal). ETF yields globally coherent, flicker-resistant flow that a single Sobel tensor cannot — this is the keystone for the multi-pass WebGPU branch (AW.W7).

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA FILTER (Papari 2007 / Kyprianidis 2009 / Acerola). The canonical 'make a gradient read as oil paint' operator and the explicit AW.W7 WebGPU finish. N=8 overlapping sectors over a circular kernel WARPED into an ellipse by the structure tensor (axes set by anisotropy A: major=(A+zeta)/zeta along tangent, minor=zeta/(A+zeta)); per sector compute weighted mean m_k and variance s_k via a polynomial sector mask (charPoly with zeta~0.1, eta/zeroCrossing~0.58); output = sum(m_k*w_k)/sum(w_k) with w_k=1/(1+(hardness*1000*s_k)^(sharpness/2)) — low-variance sectors win, so color flattens into oriented brush-shaped patches while edges sharpen. Multi-pass (tensor pass -> smooth pass -> filter pass), correctly scoped to WebGPU in the design. Stacking 2-3 radii (multi-scale AKF, Kyprianidis 2009) simulates different brush sizes — the Kuwahara analogue of Hertzmann's layering.

REAL-TIME PAINTERLY-SHADER PIPELINE (Maxime Heckel 2024, the closest portable reference). The production WebGL/WebGPU recipe: Pass1 structure tensor (Sobel) -> Pass2 anisotropic Kuwahara (8 sectors, polynomial weights swapped in for exp() Gaussian to hold 60fps) -> Pass3 final look (tonemap + paper grain + optional brushstroke overlay). Key real-time tricks: the polynomial sector weight [(x+eta)-lambda*y^2]^2 (eta~0.1,lambda~0.5) replaces per-sample exp(); kernel radius is the dominant cost knob; the structure tensor pass can be downsampled/cached. Directly validates our AW.W7 staging and supplies the exact constants. Heckel also notes a Voronoi-normal-smudge + brush-texture material approach was tried and ABANDONED for post-processing — a portability warning for over-engineering the bristle layer.

BRISTLE / IMPASTO HEIGHT-FIELD MODELING (Fast Paint Texture; dual-parameterization 2024/2026). Tactile oil-paint look = a height field combining canvas substrate + per-stroke impasto accumulation: each stroke deposits a procedurally-perturbed per-pixel height (bristle ridges/grooves via harmonic weights + frequency ratios), with THICKNESS-AWARE modulation — thin strokes inherit canvas roughness, thick impasto overrides it. Then normal = gradient(height), relit with diffuse+Blinn-specular (thick ridges = high shininess sharp glint, thin = broad soft sheen). OUR engine ALREADY implements exactly this (paintOver accumulates height, relightImpasto does dFdx/dFdy normal + movable uLightDir + height-graded shininess). This is genuine SOTA-parity; the only refinement available is layered multi-frequency bristle harmonics (2+ frequency ratios) and a separate waxy-burnish lobe (already present in oil-pastel).

NEURAL / DIFFERENTIABLE SBR (Paint Transformer 2021, Stylized Neural Painting 2020, MambaPainter 2024, dual-parameterization 2024-2026). The modern image->painting branch: strokes are an 8-vector {x,y,h,w,theta,r,g,b} (Bezier control pts + width + color + opacity for SDF rasterization), predicted feed-forward (Transformer/Mamba/SSM) or optimized by differentiable rendering with a 'transportation' loss to dodge the zero-gradient trap; coarse-to-fine over 2^k x 2^k patches; sequential alpha-blend I=alpha*Ib+(1-alpha)*I_prev. PORTABLE IDEAS (NOT the networks, which target a source image our procedural engine lacks): the SDF stroke primitive + opacity-blend ordering (we use this), the dual coarse/fine parameter split (validates a coarse-to-fine port), and the explicit acknowledgement that stroke ORDER is load-bearing (deterministic painter's-order matters for our overlaps).

TEMPORAL COHERENCE FOR ANIMATED STROKES (Meier motion-maps; constraint-based stroke ordering; Barroso 2025). Because the aurora DRIFTS, the relevant failure modes are 'shower-door' (strokes glued to screen not content) and 'popping' (strokes reorder between frames). SOTA fixes: ADVECT stroke anchors along the flow/optical-flow field so texture moves with the content, keep stroke ORDER stable across frames (constraint-based ordering), and accept that some hand-made looseness is desirable (Barroso 2025 deliberately does NOT over-stabilize). OUR engine sidesteps this elegantly — DESIGN.md invariant 7 freezes the stroke MATERIAL static (deterministic per-cell hashes, breath only wobbles luminance), so there is no per-frame stroke churn to flicker. The lesson: if any future wave ADVECTS strokes with the warp/cursor-wake, it must advect anchors continuously (not reseed per frame) or it will reintroduce popping.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for glass-ui's aurora — see facet-level synthesis above; ranked highest-to-lowest value: (1) coarse-to-fine multi-radius stroke layering (Hertzmann; currently ABSENT, single-pass-compatible, biggest quality lever); (2) multi-segment integrated curved spines replacing the fixed quadratic bulge (tensor field already computed); (3) keep + document the already-SOTA structure-tensor/ETF orientation, height-field impasto relight, OKLCh broken color, greedy best-of-neighborhood selection; (4) Kang ETF iterative smoothing + multi-scale anisotropic Kuwahara correctly staged to the WebGPU branch (AW.W7) with the polynomial-weight constants from Heckel/Acerola; (5) park the neural branch (no source image, pulls a dependency).
pitfalls: MULTI-PASS IS BANNED ON WebGL2 (DESIGN.md invariant 8). True ETF iterative smoothing and the anisotropic Kuwahara finish are inherently multi-pass (need a populated neighborhood buffer) and MUST stay on the WebGPU branch. Do not attempt them as a single fragment pass — a fixed small-tap approximation is the honest WebGL2 ceiling (the design already states this).

COARSE-TO-FINE WITHOUT A TARGET IMAGE: Hertzmann's layering is gated by error-vs-reference; the aurora has no reference. The port must redefine the gate as color-divergence between the coarse stroke layer and the procedural nuclei field (sampleBase), or as a coverage residual — a naive 'just stack more strokes' loses the algorithm's whole point (detail only where needed) and just darkens everything.

PER-FRAME GREEDY COST: classical greedy placement visits every cell every frame. Our 3x3 best-of-neighborhood is already O(9) taps per pixel; a 3-level coarse-to-fine cascade triples that to ~27 strokeShape evaluations per pixel. Must stay inside profile:budget — measure against the bundle/perf gate, and gate stroke count by cellSize so coarse levels stay cheap.

TEMPORAL POPPING IF STROKES ARE EVER ADVECTED: the engine's safety today is that strokes are STATIC material (deterministic hashes, breath only wobbles luma). Any future wave that advects stroke anchors with the warp drift or cursor wake (AW.W8) must move anchors CONTINUOUSLY along the flow and keep stroke ORDER stable — reseeding per frame reintroduces shower-door + popping flicker the NPR temporal-coherence literature spends entire papers fighting.

KUWAHARA exp()->POLYNOMIAL IS MANDATORY FOR 60FPS: Heckel and the shader-art community are explicit that the textbook Gaussian sector weight (exp()) is too slow; the polynomial sector mask [(x+eta)-lambda*y^2]^2 (eta~0.1,lambda~0.5,zeta~0.1,zeroCrossing~0.58) is the production form. Porting the naive math will tank the WebGPU finish framerate.

ETF ELLIPSE / TENSOR DEGENERACY: at Jxy~0 the (lambda-Jyy,Jxy) eigenvector formula collapses to a zero vector — the atan2 closed form (theta=0.5*atan2(2*Jxy,Jxx-Jyy)) is the robust one (the engine already uses it; any new tensor code must NOT regress to the naive eigenvector form). In flat/low-coherence zones strokes must relax to the fallback flow (mix by coherence A) or the tensor reads as noise.

OVER-ENGINEERING THE BRISTLE LAYER: Heckel explicitly tried a Voronoi-normal-smudge + brush-texture MATERIAL model and ABANDONED it for cheaper post-processing. The engine's procedural height-field bristle is already the right altitude; do not add a sampled brush-texture atlas or a per-bristle physical sim (Industrial-strength/Fast-Paint-Texture) — that is film-pipeline cost with no UI-backdrop payoff and breaks the zero-dep posture.

PORTABILITY OF MULTI-RADIUS BLUR: Hertzmann blurs the reference by fs*R per layer. On GPU per-pixel there is no cheap large-radius blur in one pass; approximate via fBm-octave selection or mip sampling of the nuclei field, not a real separable Gaussian (which is itself multi-pass and would re-trip invariant 8 on WebGL2).

notes.facet: Watercolor simulation — wet-edge darkening, granulation, pigment dispersion, edge bleed
sotaTechniques: KUBELKA-MUNK SPECTRAL PIGMENT MIXING (Curtis 1997 → spectral.js, MIT, 2025). The canonical watercolor optical model: each pigment carries absorption K + scattering S coefficients; superimposed glazes composite via the KM equations, NOT alpha-over. spectral.js's spectral.glsl ports this single-constant variant to GLSL: srgb→linear→7-primary-weighted 38-band reflectance R (Burns LHTSS), K/S = (1-R)²/2R per band, concentration-weighted KS mix (C = factor²·tintingStrength²·luminance), inverse KM R = 1+KS-sqrt(KS²+2KS), then 38-tap reflectance→CIE-XYZ→sRGB. This is WHY mixing yellow+blue gives green (subtractive) instead of the muddy grey alpha-blend / even an OKLab-arc lerp produces. Pure-ALU, no textures, single-pass-capable.

WET-EDGE DARKENING VIA POWER-CURVE ON EDGE PROXIMITY (Curtis 1997 surface-tension model; CS184/gracelgilbert single-pass form). Physics: as a wash dries, water carries pigment from the pool center to its perimeter, depositing a darker rim. Single-pass trick: compute an edge/boundary proximity e∈[0,1] (luma-gradient magnitude OR distance to a region boundary), then RAISE the color to a power that grows with e: col = pow(col, 1 + k·e). Because 0<col<1, a higher exponent darkens, and the rim darkens MORE than the interior — a free, multiply-free, monotone edge stamp. Equivalent dual form is the inverted-Gaussian / unsharp-mask: subtract a blurred copy so only the high-gradient ring survives.

PIGMENT-DENSITY / TURBULENCE MODULATION (Bousseau 2006, the real-time keystone). Every wash carries within-region value mottling driven by a turbulence field τ(x) (an fBm/Perlin noise): color *= (1 - density·(τ(x) - 0.5)). density is the per-pigment art-direction knob; τ is a static 'pigment density texture'. This is exactly the no-flat-fills law — it is single-pass, one noise eval, and is the dominant 'reads as a real wash' lever after edge darkening.

GRANULATION AS PIGMENT SEPARATION + PAPER-TOOTH SEDIMENTATION (Curtis granularity term; Bousseau substrate granulation). Heavy/irregular pigment particles settle into the paper's tooth (height field) where the wash pools. SOTA refinement over a single grey-noise multiply: (a) modulate deposition by a multi-octave PAPER HEIGHT field h(x) so pigment collects in valleys (granulate = mix(1, h, granulation·pigmentLoad)); (b) the TWO-PIGMENT SEPARATION effect — when a granulating mix dries, the denser pigment settles first and the lighter floats further, so the two pigments visibly SEPARATE in OKLab chroma/hue: split the local color into two OKLab endpoints and let h(x) bias which one deposits per-pixel (heavy → low tooth, light → high tooth). This is the 'mottled two-tone grain' real granulating paints show, not uniform noise.

BOUNDARY WOBBLE / HAND-TREMOR DOMAIN WARP (Bousseau hand-tremor; Montesdeoca substrate distortion). The wet edge is never a clean iso-line — wobble the SAMPLE COORDINATE by a low-frequency noise before evaluating the region field: p_wob = p + amp·(noise2(p·f) - 0.5), amp≈0.01, f≈3-8. Applied to the edge-mask/region-boundary sample only, it gives the organic cauliflower/feathered boundary. This is domain warping (Quilez) repurposed as a per-medium edge perturbation — aurora already owns the fBm + domainWarp machinery to do it for ~free.

BACKRUNS / BLOOMS (Curtis backrun model). When fresh water hits a damp region, it pushes pigment outward into branching, hard-edged 'cauliflower' fronts with darkened perimeters. Faithful backruns need the fluid sim (multi-pass), but a convincing STATIC approximation is a thresholded, edge-darkened secondary noise mask: bloom = smoothstep(t, t+w, fbm(p·s)); apply edge darkening to bloom's own gradient. Maps to the WebGPU branch for the animated version (a Gaussian splat + self-advect in the ping-pong velocity texture already specced for AW.W8 'wake').

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA AS THE WET-MEDIA SETTLING FINISH (Kyprianidis; Heckel 2024). The edge-preserving smoothing that makes a field 'read as settled pigment': 8-sector circular kernel, per-sector mean μ and variance σ², output the lowest-variance sector's mean — flattens interiors into watercolor-flat washes while preserving the wet-edge boundary. The polynomial sector weight max(0,(x+η-λy²))² is the cheap single-pass approximation; the Gaussian-smoothed structure-tensor-steered ANISOTROPIC version is multi-pass (the AW.W7 WebGPU finish already in DESIGN.md §10 Δ09). For watercolor specifically it is the 'settle the wash' operator, complementary to the oil/vangogh use.

WET-ON-WET FLUID ADVECTION (Curtis shallow-water sim; WebGPU ping-pong, 2024-2025). True bleed/diffusion is a shallow-water fluid sim: a wet-area mask gates a velocity field; pigment advects along velocity, diffuses, and deposits on evaporation. Two-texture ping-pong (quantity + velocity) on the GPU runs interactively. This is inherently multi-pass and belongs on aurora's already-specced WebGPU branch (the createGPUCanvas substrate + the stateful pointer-wake velocity texture) — NOT the WebGL2 single-pass fallback.
notes.applicability:
"GROUNDED IN OUR ENGINE — current state: aurora's mediumWatercolor (mediums.glsl.ts lines 83-105) is a 3-line single-pass approximation: (1) wet-edge = a luma-gradient-magnitude smoothstep mask × a fixed 0.78 multiply; (2) granulation = a 2-octave value-noise (160/360) multiplied by pigmentLoad (1-luma); (3) a faint fbm wash band. It is honest and cheap but lacks the actual watercolor physics. The shared color core ALREADY ships the Ottosson OKLab/OKLCh matrices (procedural-color.glsl.ts) and the runtime already wires uWetEdge + uGranulation uniforms — so the upgrades below are mostly shader-internal, no new uniform plumbing.

PATH FORWARD, ranked by impact/cost on the WebGL2 single-pass path (invariant 8 holds — all four below are single-pass, pure-ALU, no FBO):
1. WET-EDGE POWER CURVE (cheapest, biggest win): replace the flat `mix(1, 0.78, mask·uWetEdge)` multiply with `col = pow(col, 1 + uWetEdge·k·edge)`. Monotone, rim-stronger-than-interior, and (being in linear pre-ACES) tonemaps correctly. Keeps the existing edge variable; ~2 extra ALU ops.
2. KUBELKA-MUNK PALETTE MIX (the headline fidelity lever): the in-shader palette interpolation (mixPaletteOklchArc) and brokenColorJitter currently mix in OKLCh. Splicing a SMALL KM mix (the spectral.glsl single-constant model) for the palette-stop interpolation makes overlapping color zones composite SUBTRACTIVELY — yellow over blue → green — which is the single biggest 'reads as real pigment glaze' move and is congruent with the existing shared-color-core discipline (one more spliced chunk alongside OKLCH_MATRICES_GLSL, with a WGSL twin for the WebGPU branch). Cost is real (38-band loop) — gate it behind a `pigmentMix` flag or precompute the LUT on the CPU bake (color.ts already bakes the palette) so the per-pixel shader stays cheap: bake a KM-mixed LUT instead of a linear-sRGB one, zero per-pixel cost.
3. GRANULATION 2.0 — paper-height sedimentation + OKLab two-pigment split: aurora already computes a paper-tooth height in mediumCrayon (the t1/t2/t3 field) and has OKLab in-shader; lift that height field into mediumWatercolor and bias deposition by it, then split the local color into two OKLab endpoints (denser→valley, lighter→peak) for the mottled two-tone grain. Reuses existing noise + OKLab; no new uniforms.
4. BOUNDARY WOBBLE: wobble the sampleBase coordinate inside mediumWatercolor's edge sampling with the existing fBm (`p + 0.01·(fbm(p·6)-0.5)`) so the wet edge feathers organically. One noise eval; reuses domainWarp's machinery.

WebGPU branch (AW.W7, already specced): wet-on-wet fluid advection + animated backruns ride the ping-pong velocity texture the 'wake' interactivity axis already introduces — pigment self-advects/diffuses for a true bleed, and the anisotropic-Kuwahara finish settles the wash. These are the capability-gated enhancement, NOT the fallback. The default wispy-sky must render identically on both paths.

The two-tier atoms door (resolveAtoms) maps cleanly: `textureAmount` already fans to wetEdge for the watercolor medium; a `pigmentMix`/granulation-style atom can ride the same fan-out without widening the consumer surface."
pitfalls: KUBELKA-MUNK PER-PIXEL COST: spectral.glsl is SPECTRAL_SIZE=38 — two+ 38-element float arrays per mix, a 38-iteration loop with pow()+sqrt() per band, plus a 38-tap reflectance→XYZ integration. That is hundreds of ALU ops + dynamic-length array indexing per pixel per mix. Running it raw in the per-pixel aurora path will blow profile:budget on low-tier GPUs and risks GLSL array-unroll compile blowups. MITIGATION: bake the KM mix into the CPU palette LUT (color.ts already bakes), or splice a reduced-band (e.g. 8-10 primary) variant — do NOT call full 38-band spectral_mix per fragment.

GAMMA/LINEAR SEAM IS LOAD-BEARING: aurora bakes the palette to LINEAR sRGB and applies the sRGB OETF once at main() (the AV.W1 'too-dark' fix, locked by proof:aurora-space-gamma). spectral.glsl does its OWN srgb↔linear (its spectral_uncompand uses gamma 2.4, not the piecewise-accurate transform aurora's shared OETF uses) and finishes in sRGB. Splicing it naively double-applies gamma and re-introduces the 2.2× too-dark class. Any KM splice MUST operate in aurora's linear space and let the single shared OETF close — strip spectral.glsl's companding.

EDGE-DARKENING POWER CURVE MUST STAY PRE-TONEMAP + AVOID BLACK CRUSH: pow(col, 1+k·e) in linear before ACES is correct; doing it post-OETF compounds with the tonemap. Also clamp k so the rim doesn't crush to the §4 'never pure black' floor (col·0.985+0.008). Watch that the existing edge variable is a raw gradient magnitude (unbounded) — normalize/smoothstep it before feeding the exponent or sharp zones spike.

GRANULATION TEMPORAL SHIMMER: granulation/paper texture is MATERIAL, not process (DESIGN.md invariant 7 — stroke texture stays static). The height/tooth field and the two-pigment split must be a function of static p only, never t — otherwise the grain crawls and breaks the 'settled pigment' read. The current granulation is already static; keep any new height field static too.

KUWAHARA + TRUE BLEED ARE MULTI-PASS — DO NOT SMUGGLE THEM ONTO WEBGL2: the anisotropic-Kuwahara finish and the wet-on-wet fluid advection are genuinely multi-pass (structure-tensor smoothing pass + the Kuwahara pass; ping-pong velocity/quantity for the fluid). Invariant 8 bans multi-pass on the WebGL2 fallback. These belong ONLY on the AW.W7 WebGPU branch; the single-pass form (power-curve edge, noise granulation, coord wobble, static backrun mask) is the WebGL2 contract.

BACKRUN STATIC-APPROXIMATION CAN READ AS 'NOISE BLOBS' NOT BLOOMS: a thresholded fbm mask without the directional outward push + darkened front looks like random splotches, not the characteristic branching cauliflower. If shipping a static backrun on WebGL2, it must carry its OWN edge-darkening on the bloom gradient and be sparse — otherwise skip it and reserve real backruns for the WebGPU fluid pass.

OKLab TWO-PIGMENT SPLIT CAN OVER-SATURATE / GO OFF-GAMUT: splitting a wash color into two OKLab chroma endpoints and depositing them separately can push chroma past sRGB gamut (the classic OKLCh-gamut-clip problem). notes.facet: Canvas/paper texture synthesis + how grain interacts with pigment opacity
sotaTechniques: LUMINANCE-ADAPTIVE GRAIN RESPONSE (mattdesl glsl-film-grain): grain amplitude is gated by a smoothstep over local brightness — response = smoothstep(0.05, 0.5, luminance); color = mix(grainedColor, base, pow(response, 2.0)) — so grain is STRONGEST in the darks/shadows and suppressed in the highlights, matching how real film/paper grain reads (the eye sees grain in mid-shadows, not in bright washes). This is the canonical 'grain interacts with pigment opacity' law.

SOFT-LIGHT (NOT ADDITIVE) GRAIN COMPOSITING: SOTA grain is blended via a soft-light/overlay operator against a DESATURATED copy of the image rather than added — softLight(base, grain) preserves local contrast and rides the underlying value, where naive `col += (n-0.5)*amp` washes shadows to grey and blows highlights. Soft-light grain is multiplicative-near-mid-grey and self-attenuating at the value extremes.

KUBELKA-MUNK PIGMENT COMPOSITING (Curtis et al. 'Computer-Generated Watercolor'): a layer's reflectance R=sinh(b·S·x/c), transmittance T=b/c with c=a·sinh(b·S·x)+b·cosh(b·S·x), composited over substrate via R = R1 + T1²·R2/(1−R1·R2). Pigment THICKNESS x is the opacity axis — modulating x by a paper-tooth height field IS the physically-correct grain-meets-opacity coupling (thin pigment over tooth valleys shows substrate; thick pigment buries the tooth).

PHYSICALLY-BASED GRANULATION = PIGMENT SETTLES IN THE VALLEYS: heavy pigment particles sink into the paper-tooth crevices (darkening lows), fine particles float on the hills (lighter) — the mottle is a height-field-driven darkening keyed to pigment LOAD (darker/denser zones granulate more). Modern shaders model it as a value-noise (or worley) height field × pigment-load weight, NOT a uniform multiply.

MULTI-OCTAVE COMPOSITE PAPER/CANVAS SYNTHESIS (Paper Shaders 'paper-texture', paper.design — the Stripe-gradient design-system lineage): paper = weighted sum of independently-scaled noise primitives — curly FIBER noise + cell-based CRUMPLE + fine ROUGHNESS speckle + a big-scale FADE mask — each seeded, blended between colorBack/colorFront by a contrast knob. Canvas weave = fbm + anisotropic sinusoidal warp (weave-weight ~0.45 balances stochastic fiber vs regular thread).

TRIANGULAR (TPDF) BLUE-NOISE DITHER IN THE QUANTIZATION/DISPLAY SPACE (Gjoel/Jimenez IGN, Wronski): dither must be applied AFTER the OETF (in the space where 8-bit quantization happens), use a triangular PDF (sum of two uniforms → no banding at gradient centers without over-noising), and prefer blue/IGN spatial spectrum (no low-frequency clumps the eye catches) over white noise. ~1 LSB (1/255) amplitude breaks mid-tone banding invisibly.

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA + STRUCTURE-TENSOR PAINTERLY FLATTENING (Kyprianidis/Kang; Acerola 2024 implementations): the structure tensor's smoothed eigenvectors steer an elliptical Kuwahara kernel along edge-tangent flow, flattening color into painterly cells WHILE PRESERVING the canvas/brush grain as a separate high-frequency overlay — the SOTA way a smooth gradient reads as oil paint without the grain being smeared away (a multi-pass operator).

SVG feTurbulence / RASTER GRAIN OVERLAY as the design-system backdrop fallback (CSS-Tricks 'Grainy Gradients', fffuel gggrain): Perlin feTurbulence (type/baseFrequency/numOctaves) tuned with feComponentTransfer, composited over a CSS gradient via mix-blend-mode (soft-light/overlay) — the cheap, GPU-free grain-on-gradient pattern; bake to AVIF/WebP when the live SVG filter is too CPU-heavy.
notes.applicability: "OUR ENGINE TODAY (grounded read of tonemap.glsl.ts + aurora.frag.ts + mediums.glsl.ts): the `uPaperGrain` term is `col += (hash21(gl_FragCoord.xy + t*17.0) - 0.5) * uPaperGrain` — WHITE noise, ADDITIVE, VALUE-INDEPENDENT, applied in LINEAR space AFTER aces() but BEFORE linearToSrgb (aurora.frag.ts:414-415), and TIME-ANIMATED so it crawls every frame. A separate 1-LSB IGN triangular dither already runs CORRECTLY in display space after the OETF (line 426) — so the dither story is SOTA; the PAPER-GRAIN story is the gap. PATH FORWARD, four concrete waves: (1) GAIN-STAGE THE GRAIN BY LUMINANCE — replace the flat `*uPaperGrain` with `*uPaperGrain*mix(1.0, k, smoothstep(0.05,0.5,luma(col)))` (Acerola/mattdesl response curve) so grain lives in the shadow/mid pigment and recedes in the bright washes — this is the single highest-fidelity, lowest-cost change and directly answers 'grain interacts with pigment opacity'; gate it on the existing uPaperGrain uniform so the default-config look is preserved. (2) MOVE GRAIN INTO DISPLAY SPACE next to the IGN dither (after linearToSrgb) OR keep it linear but document the choice — linear-space additive grain is perceptually non-uniform (crushes shadows), and the design wants paper, which is a display-space material; fold paperGrain + IGN into one display-space grain stage. (3) SWITCH ADDITIVE→SOFT-LIGHT for the paper-grain term (softLight(col, vec3(grain))) so the grain rides value instead of greying it. (4) UNIFY THE THREE GRAIN FIELDS ON ONE PAPER-HEIGHT SOURCE — today watercolor `granulation` (mediums.glsl.ts:97, value noise 160/360, the ONLY pigment-load-coupled term via `pigLoad=1-luma`), oil `canvas tooth` (linen weave, line 311), pastel `tooth` (vnoise*800), oil-pastel `paperHeight` (3-octave, line 157), and the post `uPaperGrain` are FIVE unrelated noise fields. Derive them from ONE shared `paperHeight(p)` chunk (mirror the AW.W5 shared-color-source discipline → a `paper.glsl.ts` shared chunk the blob could reuse) so the canvas identity is coherent and tunable from one place. (5) FIX THE GRANULATION POLARITY against the physical reference: real granulation settles pigment into the VALLEYS (darkens lows), while oil-pastel deposition correctly lands on PEAKS — these are physically opposite and the shared paper-height chunk should expose both a `settleInValleys` (watercolor) and `depositOnPeaks` (dry media) read so each medium is physically right. (6) WebGPU branch (AW.W7) is the home for the multi-tap smoothed structure tensor + anisotropic Kuwahara that lets the gradient read as oil WITHOUT smearing the grain — grain stays a final display-space overlay AFTER the Kuwahara flatten, not before."
pitfalls: COLOR-SPACE PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING: the current paper-grain is added in LINEAR before the OETF, so equal grain amplitude reads ~5x stronger in shadows than highlights after the gamma curve compresses lows — this accidentally gives SOME value-coupling but in the wrong, uncontrolled way (and it interacts with ACES roll-off). Any grain rework MUST decide linear-vs-display explicitly; the IGN dither is already display-space (correct) and the proof:aurora-space-gamma gate locks the OETF seam — do not move grain across that seam without re-baselining the gate.

ANIMATED WHITE-NOISE GRAIN CRAWLS AND FIGHTS prefers-reduced-motion: `t*17.0` reseeds the grain every frame, so the paper 'boils' — paper is a MATERIAL (static), not a process (DESIGN.md invariant 7 says stroke texture stays static). A live boiling grain is both an aesthetic error and a PRM/seizure-adjacent motion concern that the masterTempo/PRM freeze does NOT currently zero (it's post-tonemap, outside the flow stack). Static or very-slow grain is the reference-correct choice.

WHITE NOISE BANDS AND CLUMPS: hash21 white noise has full low-frequency content — on the soft aurora gradients it reads as visible clumping and does not melt away the way blue/IGN noise does (Wronski). The dither already uses IGN; the paper-grain should too (or a blue-noise tile), else the two grain layers have different spectra and the white-noise layer dominates visually.

PORTABILITY — dFdx/dFdy IN THE GRAIN/RELIGHT PATH: the oil-pastel burnish and impasto relight derive normals from dFdx/dFdy(paperHeight) (mediums.glsl.ts:185, brush.glsl.ts). Screen-space derivatives are correct on WebGL2 but the WGSL twin must use dpdx/dpdy and the multi-pass Kuwahara tensor changes the neighborhood — the grain-relight will NOT match 1e-6 between backends the way the color core does; the proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence harness only certifies the COLOR/noise math, not the derivative-driven relight, so a backend grain divergence can slip the gate.

GRAIN BEFORE TONEMAP vs AFTER changes its character: grain added before aces() gets compressed by the tonemap roll-off (highlights eat it); grain after aces() but before OETF (current) is in linear display-ish space; grain after OETF (the dither's home) is in true perceptual space. These three are visibly different and NOT interchangeable — pick one rationale and document it, because a future contributor will 'simplify' by merging the paperGrain and IGN stages and silently shift the look.

DON'T DOUBLE-COUNT PIGMENT-LOAD: watercolor granulation already weights by pigLoad=1-luma; if you ALSO add a global luminance-adaptive grain response on top, the watercolor darks get grain^2. The shared paper chunk must make the per-medium coupling explicit so the post-stage global grain doesn't re-apply a coupling the medium already did.

PERFORMANCE/BUDGET: a shared multi-octave paperHeight evaluated per-pixel for every medium plus a soft-light blend is more ALU than the current single hash21 — it must stay inside profile:budget (the AW.W4 painterly arc is already budget-pressured on the single-pass WebGL2 path). Multi-tap smoothed tensor + Kuwahara are explicitly WebGPU-only (invariant 8) for exactly this reason.

RASTER/SVG FALLBACK MISMATCH: if a CSS-mode (renderMode:'css') or SVG-feTurbulence backdrop ever ships as the no-WebGL fallback, its Perlin grain spectrum and blend mode will not match the shader's IGN/soft-light grain — the placeholder-to-canvas crossfade (Aurora.vue) would show a grain 'pop'. Match the fallback grain spectrum or crossfade through a grain-free frame.

notes.facet: Skyscape/landscape photography palette characteristics — gradient anatomy of golden-hour/dusk/aurora-borealis skies
sotaTechniques: Twilight-wedge vertical gradient anatomy (the physically-correct stop ORDER). A real dusk/dawn sky is a VERTICAL stack of named bands, not a free 2D blob field: horizon→zenith runs (sunset side) deep orange/gold (long-path Mie+Rayleigh reddening, ~590-620nm) → a thin yellow-green transition → desaturating peach/salmon → the Chappuis-band cyan/steely-blue mid-sky → indigo zenith; on the ANTI-sunset (eastern) side the stack is Earth's-shadow blue-gray hugging the horizon (~0-6 deg) → the Belt-of-Venus pink/magenta arch above it (~6-20 deg, backscattered reddened light, pale-pink low → deeper magenta high) → blue zenith. The transitions are SOFT (degrees-wide) and the band order is invariant — encode it as a monotonic L ramp keyed to the screen Y axis, not isotropic radial nuclei.

Chappuis-band cyan as the twilight 'secret' stop. The steely blue/cyan of twilight is NOT Rayleigh — it is ozone ABSORPTION in the Chappuis band (continuum 400-650nm, max absorption ~603nm). Ozone removes red/orange from the long twilight path, leaving a pale-blue cast; WITHOUT ozone the twilight sky would read straw-yellow/pale-green. Algorithm: inject one cool desaturated-cyan stop (OKLCh roughly L0.72 C0.05 h ~215-230) between the warm horizon and the indigo zenith — it is the perceptual hinge that makes a dusk gradient read as 'real sky' rather than a generic warm-to-cool ramp.

Aurora emission-line palette (discrete spectral stops, not a continuum). Aurora color is QUANTIZED by atomic emission lines, so the palette is a small set of fixed hues, NOT a smooth spectrum: oxygen green 557.7nm (the dominant band, OKLCh ~L0.86 C0.21 h150, scotopic-boosted so it dominates), oxygen red 630.0nm (high-altitude crown, h ~25-35), nitrogen blue/violet 427.8nm + the magenta-pink 'curtain base' (N2 first-positive, h ~330-340), over a night-sky indigo/navy base. The signature look = high-chroma neon ribbons over a near-black low-chroma base (high local contrast), green-bottom/red-top vertical layering matching the altitude bands (100-300km green, >300km red).

Camera-vs-eye luminance asymmetry as a deliberate authoring axis. Long-exposure aurora/twilight photos accumulate faint photons the dark-adapted eye misses, so PHOTOGRAPHIC palettes are higher-chroma and reveal red/violet layers the eye barely sees. Two authored looks from one phenomenon: an 'observed' low-chroma desaturated variant and a 'photographic' high-chroma saturated variant — a single mood/exposure scalar that scales OKLCh C and the value-variance, congruent with the engine's existing calm<->vivid mood atom.

IQ cosine-palette parameterization (a + b*cos(2pi*(c*t+d))) as a compact natural-gradient generator. Four vec3s encode a whole atmospheric ramp on the GPU with no LUT: a=bias/brightness midpoint, b=per-channel contrast, c=oscillation count (use 0.5/1.0 for one sweep over 0..1), d=per-channel phase = the hue separation. Authoring a dusk ramp = phase-offset the R/G/B cosines so red peaks at the horizon end and blue at the zenith end. Cheaper than an 8-stop LUT and trivially animatable (drift d over time).

OKLab/OKLCh perceptual interpolation with an explicit hue PATH (shorter vs increasing/decreasing arc). Interpolating sky stops in sRGB drives orange->blue through a desaturated gray 'mud' midpoint; OKLCh keeps chroma up across the transition (orange->blue passes through cyan/green, not gray). For atmospheric ramps the muddy-midtone-free 'shorter' OKLab-rectangular path is correct for the warm->cool sweep, while 'increasing' gives a deliberate rainbow sweep for an aurora multi-emission ribbon. Warm-light/cool-shadow temperature coupling (warm the lights ~70deg, cool the shadows ~250deg) is the single most-cited painting rule and matches real atmospheric warm-low/cool-high.

Pre-quantization dithering with Interleaved Gradient Noise (IGN) to kill 8-bit banding. Smooth low-chroma sky ramps band hard at 8-bit/channel; the fix is to add screen-space IGN noise = fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(gl_FragCoord.xy, vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715)))) scaled to (1.0/255.0) and centered by -(0.5/255.0), applied AFTER tonemap but in the shader BEFORE the framebuffer's 8-bit quantization (a post-process dither over a 24-bit buffer is too late). IGN beats a plain sin-hash (which has visible structure) and a Bayer matrix (visible at low amplitude) and needs no texture sample.

Display-P3 wide-gamut progressive enhancement for neon aurora greens. The aurora's 557.7nm green and electric magenta are OUTSIDE sRGB; on sRGB they get gamut-clamped (and the clamp algorithm is unstandardized, so it varies per platform). SOTA: author the vivid stops in P3/OKLCh, gate the punchier palette behind @media (color-gamut: p3) (greens expand most in P3, exactly the aurora case) with an sRGB-clamped fallback ramp — the same dual-ramp/@supports pattern the design-system aurora-backdrop tools use.

Reference analytic sky models (Preetham, Hosek-Wilkie, Bruneton) as the gradient-anatomy ORACLE, not the runtime. Full Rayleigh+Mie ray-marched scattering (Hosek-Wilkie improves Preetham's fit with more DOF for turbidity/albedo) is the ground truth for which colors sit where in a real sky — but it is multi-sample and overkill for a backdrop. Use it offline to derive the canonical horizon->zenith stop set per phase (golden-hour, civil-twilight, blue-hour), then bake those stops into authored presets; the cheap single-pass nuclei/ramp shader reproduces the look at zero ray-march cost.
notes.applicability: "OUR ENGINE TODAY: deriveAurora() already does a perceptual OKLCh L-ramp with a bell-shaped chroma curve (saturated body, calm extremes), a huePath axis (shorter/increasing/decreasing), and a temperatureShift (warm-light/cool-shadow). deriveScene() maps mood words to harmony+medium+motion. The DESIGN.md is deep on painterly NPR (structure tensor, impasto, OKLCh jitter) but the COLOR-SCIENCE of specific sky phenomena is under-encoded: palettes are free analogous/triad ramps, not the physically-correct band stacks. THE PATH FORWARD, mapped to the existing surface: (1) Add a SKY-PHASE preset family in demo/stories/aurora/presets.ts (presets-in-consumers rule) encoding the canonical horizon->zenith stop sets: golden-hour (gold/peach->Chappuis-cyan->indigo), civil-twilight + Belt-of-Venus (blue-gray->magenta->blue), aurora (night-indigo base + 557.7nm green + 630nm red crown + N2 magenta). pitfalls: sRGB gamut clipping of neon aurora green/magenta: 557.7nm green and electric magenta fall outside sRGB; the engine bakes palettes to LINEAR sRGB for the LUT (color.ts flattenPalette via oklchToLinear), so a vivid aurora stop silently clamps and reads duller than authored. The existing gamutMapStop() in deriveAurora protects derived stops, but hand-authored consumer presets must run through it too, or accept the desaturation. P3 enhancement needs a real P3 canvas context, not just P3 CSS.

Banding on the smooth/atmospheric pole: low-chroma horizon->zenith ramps are exactly the case that bands at 8-bit. The current shader has NO dither (DESIGN.md §4 post chain ends at clamp). Adding IGN must happen in-shader before quantization and AFTER the sRGB OETF would be wrong — it goes between tonemap and the implicit 8-bit framebuffer write; getting the linear-vs-gamma timing wrong (the AV.W1 '2.2x too dark' class) re-band or shift brightness.

Don't ray-march: full Rayleigh/Mie atmospheric scattering (Preetham/Hosek-Wilkie/Bruneton) is multi-sample and violates the single-pass-WebGL2 invariant 8. Use it offline as the stop oracle only; baking a runtime scattering integral into the fallback path is the wrong altitude for a UI backdrop.

The vertical band ORDER is load-bearing and easy to lose: real skies are vertically stratified (gold low, blue high; Earth's-shadow low, Belt-of-Venus above). The engine's isotropic radial nuclei naturally produce blobs, not bands — a naive multi-nuclei aurora reads as a lava-lamp, not a sky. Must couple paletteBias to nucleus Y and/or use elongation to get the horizontal stratification; otherwise the physically-correct stops still look wrong.

Hue-path mud on warm->cool sweeps: a golden-hour gold->indigo ramp interpolated on the 'increasing' OKLCh arc sweeps through green (wrong for a clean dusk); the 'shorter'/OKLab-rectangular path is correct there, while aurora multi-emission ribbons WANT the long arc. The huePath axis must be set per-phase, not globally — a single default will be wrong for one of the two families.

Web color-palette sources (schemecolor/color-hex aurora hex sets) are decorative, not physical: many 'aurora borealis palette' hex sets are stylized and include colors aurora never emits (e.g. saturated teal/purple gradients). Ground the emission stops in the 557.7/630.0/427.8nm lines, not the decorative palettes, or the result is generic-neon rather than congruent.

Camera vs eye is a CHOICE, not a default: authoring everything at photographic high-chroma makes the backdrop overwhelming behind content (the engine already ships opacity-ceiling for exactly this content-over-aurora problem). The 'observed' low-chroma variant is the right default for content routes; reserve the vivid photographic palette for hero surfaces.

Dithering and reduced-motion/static frames: IGN keyed to gl_FragCoord is static (good — it won't shimmer frame-to-frame), but if ever keyed to uTime it would crawl and violate the prefers-reduced-motion freeze the substrate enforces. Keep the dither time-independent.
