notes.facet: OpenAI / Stripe / Linear gradient-backdrop techniques: mesh gradients, animated noise, and the math to push the procedural aurora look further
pitfalls: Dither must be added in DISPLAY space after the OETF, not in linear before ACES, or banding returns; keep IGN dither and film grain as two separate adds.
Double-dither beat patterns can appear on 6-bit panels that do their own temporal dithering; freezing a static IGN frame under reduced-motion can make the pattern faintly visible.
AgX is not a drop-in for ACES; its initial desaturation means ACES-tuned presets look flat until chroma is pushed back, so gate it behind a uniform and re-bake thumbnails.
Curl noise needs a well-tuned gradient epsilon and changes flow character; it is an additive fluid pattern, not a 1:1 replacement for the authored radial/swirl/diagonal patterns.
Anisotropic Kuwahara and LIC are genuinely multi-pass and correctly banned on the WebGL2 single-pass path; keep the painterly finish WebGPU-only and do not fake it single-pass.
Do not vendor reverse-engineered Stripe MiniGL libraries or Three.js TSL node materials; both break the zero-dependency hand-written-shader posture.
CSS Paint API is Chromium-only, so it is progressive enhancement only; the portable static fallback is native linear-gradient in oklch or a baked poster.
Progressive-blur stacks of backdrop-filter plus mask plus overflow-hidden render incorrectly on rounded wrappers in Chrome; test that case specifically.
Adding curl, AgX, and adaptive grain as new uniform-selected branches risks shader complexity that trips profile:budget; keep them branchless and budget-gated.
About 5 percent of sessions still fall back to WebGL2, so every painterly headline must render acceptably single-pass and never assume the Kuwahara finish is present.
sotaTechniques: Domain-warped fBm f(p+g(p)): distort the sample coordinate by a second fBm field before evaluating, so color bands curl organically; nested warp q=fbm(p+fbm(p)) buys another fidelity rung. The canonical OpenAI/Stripe wispy-gas generator; already the engine's composition core.

Stripe mesh-gradient model: a ~10KB WebGL program bilinear-interpolates a low-res vertex mesh of control colors, then a sin/cos UV ripple plus fBm Simplex octaves animate it; the diagonal Stripe look is a CSS skewY(-12deg)+overflow:hidden frame, not a shader effect.

Alex-Harri layered-noise gradient: one branchless per-pixel color(position,time); stack 2-4 Simplex octaves at L/1.0 and L/1.3 with per-layer speed and decaying amplitude, add F*time drift, map scalar to color through a 1D gradient texture, soften edges with quintic smoothstep and noise-driven per-pixel blur raised to ~3.5 power.

Curl noise (divergence-free flow): take the perp-gradient of a potential fBm field, v=(dN/dy, -dN/dx), giving zero divergence; strokes and UV-advection swirl in incompressible fluid-looking streams with no clumping or sinks. SOTA replacement for a hand-authored swirl/radial flow.

Interleaved Gradient Noise dither (Jimenez): fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(coord,vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715)))) gives texture-free near-blue-noise; add +/-0.5 LSB in display space after the OETF, ideally TPDF-shaped, to dissolve 8-bit banding. Highest-ROI move for flat gradients; engine already lands it.

Anisotropic Kuwahara / structure-tensor finish: build J from Sobel, Gaussian-smooth, eigen-decompose for orientation and anisotropy A=(l1-l2)/(l1+l2); run Papari 8-sector circular Kuwahara with an elliptical kernel rotated along the tensor, output the lowest-variance sector. Polynomial sector weights for real-time. Engine stages this on WebGPU.

OKLCh/OKLab perceptual interpolation: interpolate palette stops and per-stroke jitter in OKLab/OKLCh so midpoints keep chroma instead of muddy gray; CSS mirrors this with linear-gradient(in oklch,...), and Tailwind v4 / Radix / Material You standardized on it. Engine already interpolates in-shader OKLCh.

Tonemap choice: ACES Narkowicz (the engine's curve) skews hot saturated pixels toward white; AgX (now Blender/three.js default) emulates film-stock desaturation with a gentler hue-preserving rolloff that holds vibrant colored highlights. PBR-Neutral preserves saturation harder. AgX is the SOTA default for press-imagery color.

Luminance-adaptive film grain: modulate grain amplitude by luma via smoothstep and composite soft-light/overlay rather than flat additive, with per-octave coordinate rotation to kill directional artifacts; matches the Sora grainy-gas surface. Engine's grain is currently flat-additive pre-OETF.

OpenAI-brand random-gradient lineage (Wang/Barry): 4-corner random pick + interpolate, a Perlin heightmap with a color scale, then 5-6 layered SVG radialGradients with randomized focal point plus scale/rotate/skew/translate, unique per page load. Takeaway: per-load seed variation as the freshness lever.

Progressive (gradient) blur backdrop: stack divs with increasing backdrop-filter blur and linear-gradient masks so blur ramps across the surface (Apple visionOS look); a compositing layer over the canvas for content legibility that complements the opacity-ceiling envelope.

Native CSS / Houdini fallback tier: linear-gradient(in oklch,...) is Baseline 2025; CSS Paint API renders resolution-independent themable gradients off the main thread. The zero-WebGL tier below css render-mode for low-power devices and a static-poster first paint.
notes.applicability: The engine is already near-SOTA; most headline techniques are landed or staged. Grounding against code: domain-warped fBm (composition.glsl.ts), in-shader OKLCh interpolation (AW.W5), structure-tensor/ETF orientation + anisotropic Kuwahara (AW.W4 single-pass approx then AW.W7 WebGPU multi-pass), ACES tonemap, and the Jimenez IGN 1-LSB triangular dither in DISPLAY space post-OETF (aurora.frag.ts line 426) are ALL present. The path forward is incremental frontier, not catch-up. Additive wins for AX aurora waves, ranked by ROI: (1) CURL NOISE flow field, augment the hand-authored FlowPattern swirl/radial with a divergence-free curl-of-fBm field v=perp(grad N); strictly more fluid than the current angle+curl model and couples to the existing warpDrift breath. (2) TONEMAP AUDIT, the DESIGN.md cites OpenAI/Sora press imagery whose hot saturated highlights are exactly what ACES Narkowicz skews toward white; add an AgX option or AgX-default for vivid presets, a single tonemap.glsl.ts swap behind a uniform; three.js and Blender both moved their default off ACES to AgX for this reason. (3) LUMINANCE-ADAPTIVE GRAIN, current grain is flat-additive in LINEAR before ACES (aurora.frag.ts ~line 414); modulate amplitude by luma and move the grain (distinct from the IGN dither) to a soft-light composite so it reads as film. (4) NESTED domain warp as an opt-in knob for the atmospheric/smooth pole, cheap single-pass, more Quilez-organic boundaries. (5) GRADIENT-TEXTURE LUT, Alex Harri's texture2D(uGrad,t) palette LUT is the same shape as the engine's baked linear-sRGB LUT sampled through the OKLCh arc, already done, validates the choice. (6) PER-LOAD SEED variation, deriveScene(seed,mood) already exposes the OpenAI freshness lever; the README/AX wave should surface seed-rotation as the canonical never-the-same-twice consumer pattern. (7) CSS-tier fallback, the existing css render-mode can adopt native linear-gradient(in oklch,...) plus a Paint-API mesh worklet so the no-GPU tier is a static OKLCh mesh poster, not a flat color. Progressive-blur is a compositing concern for content-over-aurora routes, pairs with opacity-ceiling, not a shader change.

notes.facet: Gradient-mesh / multi-nuclei composition art — how designers build depth + zones
sotaTechniques: Quilez recursive domain warping (fBm-of-fBm): replace f(p) with f(p+4r) where r=fbm(p+4q+offsets) and q=fbm(p+offsets) — two nesting levels of an fBm-built 2D displacement vector produce organic, non-repeating zone boundaries. The KEY underused payload: the intermediate q and r vectors are themselves usable as extra color/value channels (Quilez maps separate ramps to |final|, q.xy and r.xy) — free depth and sub-zone structure with no extra noise calls.

Polynomial smooth-minimum (Quilez smin): smin(a,b,k){h=clamp(0.5+0.5*(a-b)/k,0,1); return mix(a,b,h) - k*h*(1-h);} — the canonical SOFT blob-merge operator. Where the current engine sums softmax-Gaussian weights (which only ever ADDS influence and can never carve), smin lets nuclei UNION/SUBTRACT as signed fields so two zones merge with a fattened seam (a real paint-pool meniscus) rather than a linear crossfade. Quilez's 2024 rewrite adds normalized/kernel/circular variants and per-blend analysis.

Smooth Voronoi (Quilez): res += exp2(-k*d) over the 3x3 neighbor cells, then dist = -(1/k)*log2(res) — a continuous, derivative-friendly cellular field where k tunes softness (low k = blurry blocks, high k = hard cells). The cell ID drives per-zone palette/value, giving the 'almost-rectangular territories' (the Meadow look) that pure fBm cannot make. The engine already declares warpMode cellular/hybrid; smooth-Voronoi is the correct primitive behind it.

Atmospheric perspective as an explicit DEPTH axis (the art-theory keystone, not yet in the engine): assign each nucleus a depth/z rank, then for 'far' zones DESATURATE, LOWER contrast, LIFT toward the sky/atmosphere tint, and SOFTEN edges; reserve highest saturation + sharpest boundaries + strongest value contrast for the 'near' focal zone. This is how painters and concept artists build readable depth+hierarchy in a flat field — a single per-nucleus depth scalar fanning to (saturation, contrast, edge-softness, atmosphere-mix).

Progressive/depth-coupled blur + film-grain texture (the 2025 mesh-gradient-tool vocabulary: Colorffy, ColorFlow, Learn UI): designers add depth by blurring background zones more than foreground and overlaying a grain texture via a BLEND MODE (overlay = grittiest, soft-light = smoother, luminosity = fine). The depth-coupled blur is the digital atmospheric-perspective lever; the blend-mode grain is what separates 'premium' mesh gradients from flat CSS radial-gradient stacks.

Professional blend-mode zone compositing (Stripe/Harri lineage): instead of a chain of mix() crossfades, composite color zones with Multiply/Screen/Overlay in the fragment shader. Multiply deepens overlaps (pigment glazing — wet-on-wet), Screen lightens (additive light), Overlay does both by luminance. This is how two overlapping color fields read as PAINT layered over paint rather than two regions alpha-blended.

Per-layer temporal-offset + depth parallax (Alex Harri flowing-gradient): each zone gets a distinct time phase derived from its position so motion never synchronizes, and depth reads via differential motion (slower = farther). The engine has per-nucleus driftPhase already; the missing piece is COUPLING drift speed/amplitude to the depth rank so far zones move slower (motion parallax = depth cue).

Curl noise (divergence-free) for the flow/drift field: velocity = curl of a noise potential (cross of noise gradient with normal) is mathematically divergence-free, so zones swirl in incompressible streams that never clump or tear — the organic 'colored gas' motion. The engine's flow.glsl already does curl-noise perturbation; the SOTA extension is driving the NUCLEI DRIFT itself off a shared curl field (not independent per-nucleus circles) so the whole composition moves as one coherent fluid.

Anisotropic Kuwahara finish via the smoothed structure tensor (Kyprianidis & Kang 2009; the canonical 'make a gradient read as oil paint' operator): build J=[[Gx²,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy²]] from Sobel, GAUSSIAN-SMOOTH J (the multi-tap step the single-pass path cannot do), eigen-decompose for orientation+coherence, then run elliptical Kuwahara sectors squeezed/rotated along the edge-tangent. Flattens the field into directional paint planes while preserving zone boundaries — exactly the engine's staged AW.W7 WebGPU multi-pass scope.

Interleaved Gradient Noise (IGN) anti-banding dither (Jimenez/CoD): bg += (1/255)*ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5/255 with ign(p)=fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(p,vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715)))) — one quantization-step of patterned dither breaks the 8-bit contour banding that ALWAYS appears on large low-contrast gradient backdrops (banding is a quantization artifact, independent of color space). Apply at output bit-depth (after the OETF) for the cleanest result.

OKLab/OKLCh perceptual interpolation + hue-path control (now CSS/Tailwind default as of 2024-2026): interpolate between stops in OKLab to avoid the grey/muddy midpoint, with an explicit increasing/decreasing hue-arc option for deliberate rainbow travel. The engine already does this (mixPaletteOklab / mixPaletteOklchArc) — it is at SOTA here; the forward note is to ALSO interpolate the per-zone value/atmosphere mix in OKLab so depth-desaturation stays perceptually even.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for glass-ui's engine (current state: softmax-weighted anisotropic-Gaussian metaballs in composition.glsl.ts, Quilez double-fBm warp, OKLab/OKLCh palette interp, per-zone value mottling, curl-noise in flow.glsl, ACES+sRGB OETF). HIGH-VALUE GAPS, ordered: (1) DEPTH AXIS — add a per-nucleus depth/z scalar to AuroraNucleus that fans to (saturation down, contrast down, edge-softness up, atmosphere-tint mix) for far zones; this is the single biggest missing lever — the engine builds zones but has NO depth ordering, so all nuclei read as one flat plane. Pure art-theory atmospheric perspective, ~10 lines in nucleiField + post. (2) IGN DITHER — one line at the end of main() after the OETF kills the 8-bit banding guaranteed-visible on full-viewport low-contrast aurora backdrops; cheapest highest-ROI win, zero new uniforms. (3) smin BLOB MERGE — offer a mergeMode 'softmax'|'smin' so adjacent nuclei pool with a real meniscus seam instead of a linear weight-sum crossfade; signed-field union is what makes two zones read as merged paint pools. (4) INTERMEDIATE-WARP CHANNELS — the engine already computes the double-fBm warp but throws away the intermediate q/r vectors; feeding q/r into a secondary value/chroma modulation gives free within-zone depth structure at zero extra noise cost (Quilez's own recommendation). (5) DEPTH-COUPLED DRIFT — couple nucleiDrift speed/amplitude to the new depth scalar (far = slower) for motion parallax, and optionally drive all nuclei drift off ONE shared curl-noise potential so the composition moves as a coherent fluid rather than independent orbits. (6) BLEND-MODE / GRAIN — the design-tool vocabulary (overlay/soft-light grain, depth-coupled progressive blur) maps onto the existing paperGrain/canvasGrain knobs and the staged WebGPU Kuwahara. Most of (1)-(5) fit the WebGL2 single-pass invariant 8; only the smoothed-tensor Kuwahara finish (technique 9) needs the staged WebGPU multi-pass branch (AW.W7), which the design already scopes correctly.
pitfalls: smin is NOT free: it needs SIGNED fields (SDF-like), but the current nucleiField accumulates POSITIVE Gaussian weights. A naive smin over Gaussians inverts/misbehaves — the merge operator must run on a distance-like quantity (e.g. -log of the weight, or an SDF per nucleus), not on the weight itself. Adopting smin means reframing the field as signed, which is a real architectural change, not a drop-in.

IGN dither must be applied at the OUTPUT bit-depth — AFTER the sRGB OETF, sized to 1/255. The frost.kiwi article's 'apply in linear before tonemap' framing is misleading for an 8-bit display target; dithering in linear under-corrects because the quantization happens post-OETF. Place it as the final op in main() before writing fragColor, and account for the engine's premultiply (the dither goes just before the after-OETF premul).

Atmospheric-perspective desaturation must run in a PERCEPTUAL space (OKLab chroma reduction), not an RGB lerp-toward-grey, or far zones go muddy — the exact muddy-midpoint failure the engine already fixed for palette interp. Reuse the existing OKLab seam; do not desaturate in linear sRGB.

Anisotropic Kuwahara is FUNDAMENTALLY multi-pass (Gaussian-smoothed tensor + per-pixel elliptical sector sampling = many taps). It CANNOT go on the WebGL2 single-pass path without violating invariant 8 — it correctly belongs only on the staged WebGPU branch. A single-pass small-tap approximation (already shipped as the ETF orientation field) is honest; do not claim the Kuwahara FINISH on WebGL2.

Blend-mode zone compositing (multiply/screen/overlay) must operate in LINEAR light to be physically correct; doing it in gamma-sRGB (the common copy-paste mistake) shifts hues and crushes the overlaps. This collides with the engine's 'ACES in linear, then OETF' discipline — blend zones BEFORE the tonemap/OETF seam.

Curl-noise driving ALL nuclei from one shared potential trades per-nucleus authorial control (driftRadius/driftPhase per nucleus) for global coherence — it is a different feel, not strictly better. Keep it opt-in; the per-preset authored drift is the existing contract and some presets want independent orbits.

More depth axes = more uniforms = budget.ts pressure. Each new per-nucleus scalar (depth, mergeK) multiplies by MAX_NUCLEI=6 across the uniform arrays; verify against the per-tier uniform/cost caps the resolver enforces (the profile:budget gate) before adding arrays. Pack where possible (e.g. depth into an unused component of an existing vec).

Progressive/depth blur in a single fragment pass is fake (you can only vary the noise frequency content per-zone, not do true neighborhood blur without taps). True depth-of-field blur is multi-pass — on WebGL2, approximate via per-zone fBm octave reduction (fewer octaves = softer) rather than claiming real blur. Don't oversell single-pass blur.

WebGPU is production-deployable in 2026 but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available (~95/5 split). Any depth/Kuwahara feature gated to WebGPU MUST have a tested WebGL2 fallback rendering the identical composition (the engine's stated zero-regression posture) — never make the depth axis WebGPU-only or low-end devices lose the composition.

notes.facet: Aurora-borealis physics-inspired rendering (curtains, rays, value mottling) for the namesake aesthetic
sotaTechniques: nimitz triangle-wave-noise aurora curtain (Shadertoy 'Auroras' XtGGRt): the canonical real-time northern-lights idiom is a 2D fBm built from TRIANGLE waves `tri(x)=abs(fract(x)-0.5)` instead of smooth value/perlin noise (`triNoise3D` accumulates `tri(p.z+tri(p.x+tri(p.y)))` over ~4 octaves with per-octave scale*1.8 and a `+time*0.1*spd` advection) because the sharp triangle creases read as the FILAMENTARY vertical striations of a curtain, then the field is raymarched as an emissive volume with `col += aurora_emission * transmittance` so overlapping folds glow additively — this is the single most-cited browser-grade aurora.

Lawlor & Genetti physically-based factorization (Interactive Volume Rendering Aurora on the GPU, WSCG 2011 + Sagrista 2024 reimpl): an auroral display is EMISSIVE-ONLY (no scattering) and factors into a height-dependent ENERGY-DEPOSITION function E(h) times a 2D ELECTRON-FLUX MAP f(lat,lon) — the curtain footprint — so a ray-march only integrates `emission(x) = E(altitude(x)) * f(footprint(x))` with an analytic integrable atmosphere-density approximation along the ray; the folded-curtain ribbon shape lives entirely in the 2D flux map (authored as splines fed through a stem-like fluid sim, stored as a cubemap/SDF to dodge polar UV seams).

Altitude→color emission banding (the physics that names the colors): vertical color stratification is the literal physics — green oxygen at ~100-150 km, red oxygen at 200+ km (lower density, longer-lived 1S/1D transitions), blue/violet nitrogen at the lower fringe; SOTA maps a normalized HEIGHT coordinate through the palette LUT (not a spatial-distance or fBm id), giving the green-base→red-tip vertical gradient inside each curtain that is the unmistakable aurora signature.

Curl-noise / domain-warped flow for the drape and sway (al-ro, Three.js-Blocks TSL curl utils, tuxalin tileable-shaders): a divergence-free curl-of-fBm field `curl(F)=(∂F/∂y,-∂F/∂x)` advects the curtain coordinate so the ribbon DRAPES and folds like a hanging cloth without sources/sinks; modern design-system aurora backdrops (Framer 'Aurora Background', shadcn/21st aurora components, 2025) build the curtain by warping the noise DOMAIN (`p += warpAmount*fbm(p+fbm(p))`, Quilez domain-warp) then sampling, which the engine already does for region boundaries — the aurora extension is to add a VERTICAL-anisotropy + height-falloff envelope on top.

Anisotropic Kuwahara + structure-tensor / edge-tangent-flow finish (Kyprianidis & Kang 2009; Papari circular 8-sector extension; Maxime Heckel 'On crafting painterly shaders' 2024): build the 2x2 structure tensor `J=[[Gx²,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy²]]` via Sobel, smooth it, eigen-decompose for orientation θ=½atan2(2Jxy,Jxx-Jyy) and coherence A=(λ1-λ2)/(λ1+λ2), then squeeze a circular Kuwahara kernel into an ellipse aligned to the minor eigenvector and pick the sector of lowest variance — this is the SOTA 'make a gradient read as painted curtains' operator and a genuinely multi-pass pass (the WebGPU-branch finish).

Interleaved-Gradient-Noise dithering against gradient banding (Jorge Jimenez COD:AW; frost.kiwi 2024): large smooth OKLCh aurora washes band hard at 8-bit; add `color += (1.0/255.0)*ign(gl_FragCoord.xy) - 0.5/255.0` where `ign=fract(52.9829189*fract(dot(uv,vec2(0.06711056,0.00583715))))` BEFORE the sRGB OETF/quantization — a zero-texture, GPU-cheap hash that beats white noise and is invisible to the eye; the canonical fix for the wide low-contrast bands an aurora curtain produces.

Perceptual OKLCh height-gradient interpolation (Ottosson OKLab; cross-browser stable by 2026): interpolating the green→red→violet curtain stops through OKLCh instead of linear-sRGB/YIQ avoids the muddy gray mid-tone (the path curves around the brighter route) — the engine already does in-shader OKLCh palette mixing (`mixPaletteOklchArc`), so the aurora vertical band inherits perceptually-uniform color for free.

pitfalls: Raymarched VOLUMETRIC aurora (nimitz/Lawlor full form) is a 3D camera-space technique with a march loop — it does NOT fit the engine's normalized 0..1 vUv full-screen-2D contract (DESIGN.md §7 'no live uRes/uDpr surface'). Porting the literal volume march would violate the single-pass-cheap fallback invariant and blow `profile:budget`. Take the 2D-projection / flux-map-as-2D-field interpretation (the Sagrista 2D-SDF footprint, the design-system 2D-curtain idiom), NOT the orbital volume renderer.

Triangle-wave noise (`abs(fract(x)-0.5)`) has SHARP C0 creases — that's why it reads as filaments, but it also bands and aliases more than smooth noise. Without the IGN dither and without enough octave-blending it will show hard contour lines, especially under the low-contrast OKLCh wash. Always pair the triangle field with the dither pass.

Altitude color banding is HUE-SPECIFIC physics (green/red/violet). Forcing it onto arbitrary consumer palettes (the brand-token presets) breaks the 'presets in consumers' rule and the painterly-poles aesthetic. Keep literal-aurora as an OPT-IN preset/atom with its own physically-motivated palette stops; do not retrofit the green-red mapping onto the existing soak-stain presets.

The curtain look fundamentally wants VERTICAL anisotropy and additive emission; the existing engine is built on softmax metaball REGIONS with multiply-style medium overlays. Naively reusing `nucleiField` for curtains produces blobs, not ribbons. The curtain needs its own field function (triangle-noise vertical-anisotropic envelope), composed at the `composition.glsl.ts` dispatch level — not shoehorned into the nuclei softmax.

Anisotropic Kuwahara is MULTI-PASS (structure-tensor pass → Kuwahara pass) and is explicitly BANNED on the WebGL2 path (invariant 8); it only lives on the WebGPU branch. A literal-aurora that DEPENDS on the Kuwahara finish for its look would regress the WebGL2 fallback. Keep the curtain legible on the single-pass WebGL2 path; treat Kuwahara as the WebGPU-only enhancement, per the existing fallback contract.

WebGPU is production-deployable in 2026 but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available (~95% per DESIGN.md §7); Safari only shipped default WebGPU 2025-11. Any literal-aurora feature that lands ONLY on the WebGPU multi-pass branch reaches ~95% of users with a degraded WebGL2 fallback — fine for the Kuwahara finish, unacceptable for the core curtain shape. Core curtain MUST render single-pass WebGL2.

Per-pixel structure-tensor + curl-noise + triangle-fBm + medium overlay can exceed the fragment cost cap in `budget.ts`/`profile:budget` on low-tier devices (the `hardwareConcurrency<=4` → CSS-placeholder tier). Validate octave counts against the per-tier uniform/cost caps; the curtain must degrade to the CSS-gradient placeholder on the low-power path like the rest of the engine.

Triangle-noise time advection (`+time*spd`) drives continuous motion — must route through the AW.W8 `masterTempo()` integrated-dt seam (NOT `uTime` scaling) and zero under `prefers-reduced-motion`, or it escapes the WCAG 2.2.2 / 2.3.3 + DockBackgroundToggle pause contract that `proof:aurora-interaction-prm` enforces.

notes.facet: WebGPU compute pipelines for multi-pass image filters (smoothed structure tensor + anisotropic Kuwahara) — workgroup design
sotaTechniques: **Anisotropic Kuwahara via smoothed structure tensor (Kyprianidis & Kang, NPAR/PG 2009 — the canonical 'gradient-reads-as-oil' operator).** Build the per-pixel RGB structure tensor J=[[E,F],[F,G]] (E=fx·fx, G=fy·fy, F=fx·fy summed over channels via Sobel), GAUSSIAN-SMOOTH it (σ≈2), then closed-form eigen-decompose: λ₁,₂=½(E+G ± √((E−G)²+4F²)); orientation φ=½·atan2(2F, E−G); anisotropy A=(λ₁−λ₂)/(λ₁+λ₂). Partition a disc into N=8 sectors, each squeezed into an ELLIPSE with semi-axes a=α/(α+A)·r and b=(α+A)/α·r (α≈1) rotated to φ; per sector compute weighted mean mᵢ and std σᵢ; output = Σ wᵢmᵢ with wᵢ=(1+σᵢ²)^(−q/2) normalized, q≈8 — low-variance sectors dominate so edges stay crisp and flat zones flatten into paint. This is EXACTLY what painterly.wgsl.ts already encodes (8 sectors, eccentricity from eigenratio, lowest-variance-wins).

**Polynomial sector weighting (Kyprianidis et al., TPCG/NPAR 2010) — convolution-free real-time sector functions.** Replaces the offline-convolved characteristic functions (which had to be baked into a weight texture) with a closed-form polynomial per sector, e.g. [(x+ζ) − η·y²]² evaluated on the fly (Maxime Heckel's practical port uses η=0.1, λ=0.5). Computed via rotational symmetry (one sector function rotated 8×). Eliminates the precomputed weight-LUT texture and a texture fetch per tap — the single biggest real-time win, and the form the codebase's painterly comment already references (η≈0.1, λ≈0.5).

**Tiled shared-memory compute with cooperative apron/halo loading.** A @workgroup_size(16,16) compute tile cooperatively stages a (16+2R)×(16+2R) neighborhood into var<workgroup> shared memory (each edge thread loads R extra apron texels), workgroupBarrier(), then every invocation reads its kernel window from LDS instead of re-fetching texture. Amortizes the halo cost across the workgroup (R extra loads per block edge, not per thread) — the textbook bandwidth-reduction pattern for the Gaussian-smooth pass and the Kuwahara RADIUS=6 gather.

**Separable two-pass Gaussian on the tensor field with 1D workgroups.** The smoothed-tensor pass factors into a horizontal then vertical 1D convolution; each pass uses a 1D workgroup (Gx1 / 1xG, e.g. 128×1) with a line-shaped LDS tile + apron. Cuts the smooth from O(k²) to O(2k) taps — already the shape of PAINTERLY_SMOOTH_WGSL's `dir`-selected separable pass; a compute port keeps the same separability.

**WebGPU workgroup-size discipline: 64-invocation default, 256-invocation cap, 16×16 max 2D tile.** WGSL @workgroup_size(x,y,z) with x·y·z ≤ maxComputeInvocationsPerWorkgroup (default 256); the cross-hardware sweet spot is ~64 lockstep invocations. For 2D image work 8×8 (64) or 16×16 (256) are the canonical tiles; dispatchWorkgroups(ceil(W/tx), ceil(H/ty)) covers the image. Hardware runs invocations in fixed-width subgroups (32 or 64), so a tile that is a multiple of the subgroup width avoids idle SIMD lanes.

**Subgroup-accelerated per-sector reductions (Chrome 134+, GA 2025).** `enable subgroups;` + subgroupAdd()/subgroupShuffle()/subgroupBallot() do cross-lane sums without LDS round-trips — the Kuwahara per-sector mean/variance accumulation (currently 8 serial array accumulators per invocation) can be expressed as subgroup reductions where the access pattern aligns. Google Meet measured 2.3–2.9× on matrix-vector shaders; the gain is hardware-gated (query subgroupMinSize/subgroupMaxSize).

**Read-write storage textures via texture-formats-tier2 (Chrome 2025).** texture_storage_2d<rgba16float, read_write> lets a compute pass read-modify-write the tensor/color targets in place, collapsing some ping-pong FBOs. Gated behind the 'texture-formats-tier2' device feature (auto-enables tier1) — must be feature-detected, not assumed.

**Downsampled / multi-scale tensor (Kyprianidis NPAR 2011) — compute the structure tensor and its smoothing at a lower mip and upsample.** The orientation field is low-frequency, so the expensive smoothed-tensor pass runs at ½ or ¼ resolution then bilinearly upsamples into the full-res Kuwahara gather — large constant-factor saving on the dominant cost with no visible orientation degradation.
notes.applicability: "OUR ENGINE STATE: painterly.wgsl.ts already implements the correct 3-pass painterly chain (tensor → separable smooth → 8-sector anisotropic Kuwahara) but as FRAGMENT passes (`@fragment fn tensor_main/smooth_main/kuwahara_main`) over render-pass FBO ping-pong, and createGPUCanvas's seam is render-pass-shaped (setup→frame draws ONE render pass; the multi-pass seam is declared generic but unwired). The facet — compute pipelines + workgroup design — is the natural AX evolution of these passes. PATH FORWARD, in priority order: (1) BENCHMARK BEFORE PORTING. The single highest-signal finding (lisyarus, compute-blur) is that a hand-rolled LDS-tiled separable blur ran ~2× SLOWER than the naive fragment shader because the hardware texture cache already serves the overlapping reads — and a single-pass LDS variant was 15–30× slower. So do NOT reflexively convert the smooth/tensor passes to compute: keep them as fragment passes unless a tile+LDS compute version measurably wins on our target hardware. The defensible compute candidate is the Kuwahara GATHER pass (RADIUS=6 → ~113-tap disc per pixel, 8× the read pressure of the blur), where the neighborhood reuse across a 16×16 tile is large enough that cooperative LDS staging can beat the cache. (2) If porting the Kuwahara pass to compute: use @workgroup_size(16,16), stage a (16+12)×(16+12) color tile + the smoothed-tensor tile into var<workgroup>, one workgroupBarrier(), then the 8-sector loop reads LDS. dispatchWorkgroups(ceil(W·dpr/16), ceil(H·dpr/16)). Write the result via texture_storage_2d (or keep a fragment output if tier2 is absent). (3) ADOPT POLYNOMIAL WEIGHTING — the codebase comment already cites η≈0.1, λ≈0.5 but the current kuwahara_main uses uniform per-sector means with no spatial weighting; adding the convolution-free polynomial weight per tap is a pure quality win (smoother sector boundaries) at near-zero cost and needs no extra pass or LUT. (4) ADD THE DOWNSAMPLED TENSOR — run tensor+smooth at ½-res (the orientation field is low-frequency) and upsample into the full-res Kuwahara; biggest constant-factor saving, fits the existing pass structure. (5) Subgroups (Chrome 134+) and read_write storage (tier2) are OPPORTUNISTIC, feature-gated speedups — wire them behind device.features.has(...) so the WebGPU path degrades to the plain-compute or fragment form, exactly mirroring the existing WebGL2-fallback posture. The masterTempo/park gate, offscreen-pause, and PRM-freeze all already extend to the compute dispatch via the shared createCanvasLifecycle core — no new lifecycle work. The proof:webgpu-substrate-single clause-2 invariant (no pass-count/format/sector-count baked in the substrate) is preserved: workgroup size, tile dims, and dispatch live in the CONSUMER's painterly encoder, not createGPUCanvas."
pitfalls: TEXTURE CACHE OFTEN BEATS HAND-ROLLED LDS. Measured: a tiled shared-memory separable Gaussian ran ~2× slower than the naive fragment shader (0.54ms vs 1.06ms) because the GPU's L1/texture cache already serves overlapping reads; a single-kernel LDS variant was 16–29ms (15–30× slower). Never assume compute+LDS is faster — benchmark per pass, and expect the smooth/tensor passes to STAY fragment.

WORKGROUP SIZE IS HARDWARE-DEPENDENT AND UN-QUERYABLE. WebGPU exposes no optimal-size hint; 16×16 (256) hits the maxComputeInvocationsPerWorkgroup cap so 16×16×2 is INVALID. A tile larger than the device's actual sweet spot de-parallelizes (runs subgroup-by-subgroup). Pick 8×8 or 16×16 and treat it as a tuned constant, not a guarantee.

rgba16float STORAGE-TEXTURE WRITE + read_write IS FEATURE-GATED. Plain rgba16float as a storage texture and especially read_write access require texture-formats-tier1/tier2 (Chrome 2025); on devices without them the in-place tensor read-modify-write is unavailable — must feature-detect and fall back to ping-pong render targets (the format is fine as a render/sample target regardless, which is why the existing fragment passes are the safe floor).

SUBGROUPS ARE NOT BASELINE. enable subgroups + subgroupAdd require the 'subgroups' device feature (GA Chrome 134, not all engines/devices); subgroup width varies (32 vs 64). Any subgroup-reduction Kuwahara path needs a non-subgroup fallback, or it breaks Safari/older hardware — the same fallback discipline as WebGPU-vs-WebGL2.

WORKGROUP DIVERGENCE IN THE SECTOR LOOP. The anisotropic Kuwahara per-tap sector assignment (atan2→floor→sector index) is data-dependent; neighboring invocations branch differently. Keep the per-sector accumulation branch-free (accumulate into all sectors with a mask) so SIMT lanes don't serialize on divergent control flow — the current array-indexed accumulation is already close to this.

FORGETTING workgroupBarrier() AFTER THE COOPERATIVE LOAD is a silent race — invocations read LDS apron texels a neighbor hasn't written yet, producing seam artifacts at tile boundaries. Exactly one barrier between the cooperative load and the gather.

COST SCALES AS R² × SECTORS. RADIUS=6 is ~113 taps × 8 sectors of work per pixel at full DPR; at retina DPR on a phone this is the frame-killer the lygia note ('seconds on iPad 2') warns about. Mitigate with the downsampled tensor, a smaller radius on the WebGPU-but-weak tier, and the existing budget.ts DPR clamp — don't ship a fixed RADIUS=6 to all devices.

DON'T LEAK PASS PARAMETERS INTO THE SUBSTRATE. proof:webgpu-substrate-single bans baking pass-count/format/sector-count in createGPUCanvas; a compute port must keep @workgroup_size, tile dims, dispatch math, and RADIUS in the consumer's painterly encoder. The render-pass-only setup→frame seam may also need a generic compute-pass capability added WITHOUT hardcoding the painterly specifics.

PORTABILITY: WGSL has NO node-side execution (proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence already certifies the color twin against the GLSL oracle at 1e-6). A compute Kuwahara can't be unit-tested headless the same way — equivalence has to be asserted against the fragment-pass reference output, and the fragment path must remain the tested zero-regression fallback.

notes.facet: WGSL address-space discipline — uniform vs storage for dynamically-indexed/variable-length arrays (the W01 bug class); std140/430 layout
sotaTechniques: DYNAMIC-INDEX-FORCES-STORAGE (the W01 rule itself). WGSL permits declaring a fixed-size array<vec4f,N> in a var<uniform> block, but the moment a *non-uniform / per-invocation* index reads it (a loop counter `i`, a `floor(t)` palette index, a vertex/instance/fragment-derived value), Metal/Naga must map it to MSL `constant` address space — and MSL forbids per-instance dynamic indexing of `constant` (it requires `device`). The canonical SOTA fix is to flip the binding to read-only storage: `var<storage, read> U: Uniforms;` (CPU side: change GPUBufferUsage.UNIFORM → STORAGE). Storage is always-legal for dynamic indices; uniform is the hazard. (gpuweb #2559; webgpufundamentals storage-buffers.)

STD140 (uniform) vs STD430 (storage) LAYOUT DIVERGENCE. Uniform buffers inherit the legacy Vulkan-std140 / D3D-cbuffer rule: every array element stride and any struct-typed member offset must be `RoundUp(16, …)` — i.e. StrideOf(array<T,N>) = 16·k. An array<vec2f> (stride 8) or a tightly-packed array<f32> is ILLEGAL in uniform memory; you must widen to vec4 or pad. Storage buffers use the relaxed std430-like rules (vec2 keeps an 8-byte stride; scalars pack). So the same struct laid out for `<uniform>` is over-padded vs the `<storage>` byte layout — the packing code must track which address space it targets. (W3C WGSL §14.4.5; learn-wgpu alignment; slang #4985.)

RUNTIME-SIZED ARRAY (variable-length, storage-only). `array<T>` with no length is legal ONLY as the whole storage buffer or the LAST member of a storage struct; `arrayLength(&U.nuclei)` returns the runtime count. This RETIRES the `MAX_NUCLEI 6 / MAX_STOPS 8` compile-time caps and the `if (i >= n) break;` over-iteration guard — the buffer is exactly nuclei.length long and the loop bound is `arrayLength`. Uniform arrays MUST stay fixed-size; only storage gets true variable length. (tour-of-wgsl runtime-sized-arrays; gpuweb #1329.)

TEXTURE-LUT PALETTE (the dependent-read-aware escape hatch). Instead of a uniform/storage vec4 array dynamically indexed per-pixel, bake the palette into a 1D (or Nx1 2D) `texture_2d<f32>` and `textureSampleLevel` it with `id` as the U coord. HARDWARE bilinear filtering gives free smooth interpolation between stops (replacing the hand-rolled `mix(labA,labB,f)` nearest-pair), it sidesteps the uniform-dynamic-index hazard entirely, and it scales to any stop count. Cost: it is a *dependent texture read* (the sample coord is computed, not interpolated), which forecloses some driver prefetch paths — set MIN/MAG to control interpolation deliberately. (NVIDIA GPU Gems 2 ch.24; frost.kiwi WebGL-LUTs; mattdesl/glsl-lut.)

UNIFORM-BUFFER-STANDARD-LAYOUT (the forward relaxation, proposed). gpuweb #4973 proposes letting uniform buffers opt into the storage/std430 layout (dropping the RoundUp-16 stride tax), since the underlying APIs already support it (Vulkan VK_KHR_uniform_buffer_standard_layout, mandatory in 1.2+; Metal native; D3D `-no-legacy-cbuf-layout`). Status as of late-2024: PROPOSED, not shipped, no feature-detect — so it is NOT something to depend on; treat std140-for-uniform as still-binding and design the storage flip rather than wait for it. (gpuweb #4973.)

STRUCT-OF-ARRAYS vs ARRAY-OF-STRUCTS packing parity. The aurora bridge already pads each nucleus into TWO vec4 lanes (nucleiPos.xyzw, nucleiMod.xyzw) — a deliberate SoA-of-vec4 form that is std140-legal in BOTH uniform and storage. Keeping each logical record vec4-aligned (never vec2/vec3/scalar array members) is the portable canon that survives the uniform→storage flip with ZERO re-packing: only the binding keyword and the buffer-usage flag change, the Float32Array byte layout is identical. (webgpufundamentals uniforms + storage-buffers.)
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD FOR OUR ENGINE — the W01 bug is LIVE in src/components/custom/aurora/constants/shaders/aurora.wgsl.ts. The `Uniforms` struct is declared `@group(0) @binding(0) var<uniform> U` (line 79) yet its `palette`, `nucleiPos`, `nucleiMod` arrays are dynamically indexed inside the fragment loops: `U.nucleiPos[i]` / `U.nucleiMod[i]` in nucleiField() (lines 149-153, index `i` is the loop counter) and `U.palette[i0]` / `U.palette[i1]` in samplePalette() (lines 121-122, index from `i32(floor(t))`). These are per-fragment dynamic indices into a uniform — the exact Metal/constant-address-space hazard. It may pass on Chrome/Dawn-D3D today and FAIL or silently de-opt on Safari/Metal (the very platform AW.W7 added WebGPU for — Safari 26 was the last engine to ship it). FIX A (minimal, recommended first): flip `var<uniform> U` → `var<storage, read> U` and the gpuRuntime.ts buffer usage from UNIFORM (0x40) → STORAGE (0x80); the std140 vec4-padded packing in packGPUUniforms already satisfies std430, so NO re-packing is needed and visual parity holds byte-for-byte. FIX B (the architectural win that also retires the caps): split into a small `var<uniform>` scalar block (the 16 scalars — they are broadcast, never dynamically indexed, so uniform is correct and faster) + a `var<storage, read>` runtime-sized `array<Nucleus>` and `array<vec4f>` palette, with `arrayLength()` replacing WGSL_MAX_NUCLEI/MAX_STOPS — this lifts the MAX_NUCLEI 6 / MAX_STOPS 8 caps the DESIGN.md §aurora.wgsl header *already claims* storage lifts (lines 17-19) but doesn't actually deliver (the twin still hardcodes the caps for WebGL2 parity). FIX C (palette-only alternative): move the palette to a 1D LUT texture for free hardware-bilinear OKLab interpolation — but note our interp runs in OKLab space (lines 121-123), so a texture LUT would need to store pre-OKLab-converted stops or interpolate in linear-sRGB, a behavior change to weigh. The painterly.wgsl.ts passes are CLEAN on this axis — they index textures and fixed local `array<vec3f,8>` sector accumulators by loop/spatial coords (function-scope `var`, not uniform memory), so no address-space violation there. RECOMMENDATION: land FIX A as the born-RED proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence-adjacent gate (a storage-binding assertion + a Metal/Safari e2e), then FIX B as the cap-lifting follow-up so the WGSL twin's storage promise becomes real.
pitfalls: The hazard is PLATFORM-SPLIT and silent: dynamic-indexed uniform arrays compile and render correctly on Chrome/Dawn (D3D/Vulkan backends) but break or de-opt on Safari/Metal because only MSL enforces the constant-vs-device address-space rule. CI on Linux/Chrome will be GREEN while real Safari users (iOS 26 / macOS Tahoe — the exact platforms AW.W7 targeted) get a blank or wrong canvas. This is precisely the W01 class: a portability bug invisible to the dev's own browser.

gpuweb #2559 is still UNRESOLVED at spec level — WGSL does not *currently* hard-forbid uniform dynamic indexing, so naga/Dawn may accept it without a validation error and then either (a) silently move it to `device` space (unpredictable perf, the 'spooky action at a distance' the committee feared) or (b) emit broken MSL. Do not rely on a validation error to catch it; the storage flip is a discipline, not a guaranteed-enforced rule.

std140 (uniform) ≠ std430 (storage) byte layout. If you flip a struct from uniform to storage WITHOUT auditing the packing, a struct with vec2/vec3/scalar array members will SHIFT — uniform pads each to 16, storage packs to 8/12/4. Our aurora bridge is safe ONLY because it already pads everything to vec4 lanes; a future field added as `array<f32>` or `array<vec2f>` would lay out differently in the two spaces and corrupt the read. Always vec4-pad array members, or branch the packer on address space.

Don't reflexively 'fix' by switching the static palette to storage everywhere — webgpufundamentals' own guidance is that uniform is simpler/faster for the *non-indexed broadcast* case. The 16 scalar fields (time, beta, counts…) are correctly uniform; only the *dynamically-indexed* arrays need storage. A blanket storage conversion loses the uniform fast-path for the scalars. The correct shape is the split-binding (small uniform + storage arrays).

Texture-LUT palettes introduce a DEPENDENT texture read (sample coord computed from the nuclei field), which disables some driver prefetch optimization and adds a sampler binding + filtering-mode decision (NEAREST for hard stops, LINEAR for smooth) — and crucially our OKLab-space interpolation does not survive a naive linear-sRGB texture LUT, so a LUT swap is a color-correctness change that must be re-gated against proof:single-color-core, not a free perf win.

Runtime-sized arrays cannot be passed to user functions or copied like values, and `arrayLength` needs a pointer to the runtime array (`arrayLength(&U.nuclei)`); refactoring nucleiField()/samplePalette() to take the array by value will not compile. The loop must index the storage binding directly. Also: removing the `MAX_*` caps removes the budget.ts cost ceiling the resolver enforces — the per-tier uniform/cost caps must move to a runtime length clamp so a 50-nucleus config can't blow the frame budget.

The DESIGN.md header on aurora.wgsl.ts (lines 17-19) ALREADY ASSERTS 'a storage buffer is dynamically sized — lifts the MAX_NUCLEI/MAX_STOPS caps', but the code declares `var<uniform>` with hardcoded fixed-size arrays. This is a doc-vs-code drift: the doc describes FIX B, the code ships the W01-buggy fixed uniform. Any AX wave must reconcile the two — either deliver the storage path the doc claims, or correct the doc to say 'uniform, caps retained'.

notes.facet: WebGPU multi-pass FBO/texture ping-pong patterns + render-bundle reuse
sotaTechniques: RENDER-TO-TEXTURE PASS CHAIN (offscreen FBO). Create each intermediate texture with usage RENDER_ATTACHMENT | TEXTURE_BINDING; pass N renders into tex.createView() as its colorAttachment, pass N+1 binds that texture as a sampled input via a bind group. ALL passes share ONE GPUCommandEncoder and one device.queue.submit([encoder.finish()]) — sequential beginRenderPass/end calls in submission order give correct read-after-write ordering with NO explicit barrier (WebGPU inserts the texture-state transition). This is exactly the tensor->smooth->kuwahara->composite chain painterly.wgsl.ts already shapes.

TEXTURE PING-PONG (A/B swap) for iterative passes. Two same-format textures; each iteration reads A, renders to B, swaps the JS references. This is the canonical separable-Gaussian-blur structure (horizontal then vertical reusing the same two textures) and the stable-fluids self-advect+dissipate loop wake.wgsl.ts implements. The swap is needed because a render pass cannot sample the texture it is simultaneously writing (no read-write aliasing on a render target).

STORAGE-TEXTURE COMPUTE PING-PONG (the WebGPU-native upgrade). In a compute pass you bind one texture as texture_2d<f32> (read) and another as texture_storage_2d<rgba16float, write> and textureStore() to arbitrary pixels — no fragment/full-screen-triangle plumbing, workgroup-tiled (e.g. @workgroup_size(8,8)). DESIGN.md already reserves compute for the structure-tensor pass; storage-texture ping-pong is the idiomatic form. Caveat: storage textures still need TWO textures for an in-place iterative kernel (you cannot read+write the same storage texture binding in one dispatch), but storage BUFFERS can be updated in place without a swap.

SEPARABLE GAUSSIAN as a 2-pass ping-pong. The smoothed-structure-tensor step (W7c pass 2) is a 1D blur applied twice (dir=(1,0) then dir=(0,1)) over the same A/B pair — O(2r) taps instead of O(r^2). painterly.wgsl.ts's PAINTERLY_SMOOTH_WGSL already takes a dir uniform; the orchestration just runs it twice swapping the target. Sigma~2, 9-tap is the shipped weight set.

ANISOTROPIC KUWAHARA (Kyprianidis-Kang, the canonical 'gradient -> oil paint' finish). Compute the structure tensor J=[[Gx^2,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy^2]] (Sobel), Gaussian-smooth it, eigen-decompose closed-form: theta=0.5*atan2(2*Jxy,Jxx-Jyy), anisotropy A=(l1-l2)/(l1+l2). Sample N=8 polynomial-weighted sectors of an ELLIPTICAL kernel rotated to the tangent and squeezed by A (eccentricity from the eigenratio); the lowest-variance sector's mean wins — edges stay crisp, flat zones flatten into paint. This is exactly painterly.wgsl.ts; the polynomial sector weight [(x+zeta)-eta*y^2]^2 (Papari) lets a smaller radius look good. Radius (R=6 shipped) and sector count are the cost dials.

RENDER BUNDLES (GPURenderBundle) for CPU-overhead amortization. Pre-record setPipeline/setBindGroup/setVertexBuffer/draw into a bundle via device.createRenderBundleEncoder({colorFormats,depthStencilFormat}).finish(), then replay each frame with passEncoder.executeBundles([bundle]) — validation/encoding happen ONCE at record time, not per frame. Resources are MUTABLE while commands are frozen: per-frame uniform changes go through device.queue.writeBuffer() into the SAME buffer the bundle's bind group references, so a slider drag or uTime tick needs no re-record. Bundle state is reset before AND after execution (each bundle must be self-contained).

TIMESTAMP-QUERY PROFILING (timestamp-query optional feature). Allocate a GPUQuerySet(type:'timestamp'), attach via the timestampWrites descriptor on beginRenderPass/beginComputePass (beginningOfPassWriteIndex/endOfPassWriteIndex), resolveQuerySet into a buffer, map and diff. This is the per-pass budget instrument for the AX waves — measure the kuwahara pass in isolation to keep it inside profile:budget. Chrome quantizes to 100us unless enable-webgpu-developer-features is set.

WEBGPU CANVAS SWAPCHAIN as the terminal pass. The final composite pass renders into context.getCurrentTexture().createView() with alphaMode:'premultiplied' to match the WebGL2 premultiply-after-OETF discipline. The intermediate FBO chain stays in linear/working space; only the last pass closes the OETF + premultiply, mirroring the single-pass contract exactly.
notes.applicability: "Path forward for the AX aurora waves, grounded against the existing src/. (1) The seam is ALREADY carved correctly: createGPUCanvas/gpuRuntime expose a setup(device,context,format)->frame-hooks seam where the CONSUMER owns pass count/format/sector count (proof:webgpu-substrate-single clause 2), and the WGSL passes (PAINTERLY_TENSOR/SMOOTH/KUWAHARA_WGSL, WAKE_ADVECT_WGSL) are written. What is MISSING is the orchestration inside gpuRuntime's frame(): today it does ONE beginRenderPass(swapchain). The AX work is a buildPasses() helper that (a) allocates the intermediate textures once in setup (a base-field FBO + a tensor FBO in PAINTERLY_TENSOR_FORMAT='rgba16float' + a smooth A/B pair + a color FBO), (b) in frame() chains base->tensor->smoothX->smoothY->kuwahara->swapchain on ONE encoder/one submit, (c) for the wake, holds a rg16float A/B pair swapped each frame with the advect pass, sampled additively into the flow lookup. (2) Allocate-once, resize-on-resize: build every intermediate texture in setup() and rebuild only in resize() (DPR change) — do NOT createTexture per frame (per-frame allocation is the classic multi-pass GC/VRAM stall). (3) Render bundles help ONLY if the per-frame JS draw-call overhead is the bottleneck; for ~4-6 full-screen-triangle passes it is marginal — the higher-value win is amortizing the bundle if the base field itself grows multi-draw, OR skipping it entirely (KISS) until timestamp-query shows CPU-bound. Keep uTime/config in the SAME uniformBuffer writeBuffer'd each frame (already the pattern in gpuRuntime), which is render-bundle-compatible by construction. (4) The whole chain MUST ride the existing shouldContinue()/park gate — a parked rAF (offscreen/PRM/DockBackgroundToggle-paused) attaches ZERO passes, including the wake self-advection (proof:offscreen-pause already extends to the WebGPU dispatch via createCanvasLifecycle). (5) WebGL2 stays the single-pass zero-regression fallback (invariant 8); none of this touches aurora.frag.ts. (6) Instrument each pass with timestamp-query and assert the multi-pass total stays inside profile:budget — this is the gate that proves the enhancement does not regress the wispy-sky default (which renders identically on both paths and triggers NO multi-pass passes when medium is smooth)."
pitfalls: rgba16float portability: it IS renderable AND filterable in CORE WebGPU (float16 formats are required renderable per spec; rgba16float supports linear filtering), so the tensor target and a filtering sampler are safe. The trap is rg/rgba32FLOAT — those are NOT filterable without the (non-core) float32-filterable path and NOT blendable without the float32-blendable feature. The wake's rg16float is in the safe 16-bit family. Do NOT reach for 32-bit float targets; 16-bit covers the tensor magnitude range (which exceeds [0,1], so an 8-bit LDR target would clip to garbage — RGBA16F is mandatory there, exactly as painterly.wgsl.ts notes).

Sampler-type mismatch validation error ('Filtering sampler is incompatible with non-filtering sampler binding'): if a bind-group layout declares a non-filtering sampler but the shader/sampler does linear filtering on a float target, WebGPU rejects the pipeline. Match the GPUSamplerBindingType ('filtering' vs 'non-filtering') to the actual sampler. This bites multi-pass code that mixes a point-sampled tensor with a linearly-sampled color.

Render-bundle restrictions: a bundle CANNOT contain setViewport/setScissorRect/setBlendConstant/setStencilReference, occlusion queries, nested executeBundles, or compute. The wake (compute) and any per-pass viewport/blend-constant change cannot be bundled — only the static full-screen-triangle draws can. Bundle state resets before AND after execution, so a bundle must self-contain pipeline+bindgroup; you cannot lean on state set outside it.

Render bundles only help CPU-bound apps. A ~4-6-pass full-screen aurora at full DPR is GPU-bound (fill-rate/sample-count), so bundles give near-zero win there — measure with timestamp-query before adding the complexity. Adding bundles to a GPU-bound pipeline is pure ceremony.

Self-sampling / read-write aliasing: a render pass cannot sample the texture it is writing, and a storage texture cannot be read+written in the same dispatch binding. Every iterative kernel (blur, wake advect) MUST ping-pong two textures. The separable-Gaussian and the stable-fluids advect both require the A/B swap; forgetting it produces feedback artifacts or a validation error.

Per-frame texture allocation: createTexture()/destroy() every frame for the FBO chain causes VRAM churn and GC stalls. Allocate all intermediates ONCE in setup(), rebuild only on resize (DPR change). The aurora root already carries contain:content + content-visibility:auto to cap paint area / VRAM — the multi-pass intermediates must respect the same budget posture (extra full-res FBOs multiply VRAM; consider half-res for the tensor/smooth passes since orientation is low-frequency).

Device loss has no webglcontextlost analogue — handle device.lost (a promise) in setup and re-route to the WebGL2 fallback on loss, since createGPUCanvas binds no context-loss event. A multi-pass pipeline that assumes a live device will silently stop painting on a GPU reset; the fallback to the single-pass WebGL2 path must be reachable at runtime, not just at probe time.

Premultiplied-alpha + OETF seam: only the TERMINAL pass should close the sRGB OETF and premultiply (matching gpuRuntime's blend:{one,one-minus-src-alpha}). Intermediate FBOs must stay in linear/working space; applying the OETF mid-chain (e.g. before the kuwahara variance compare) double-encodes color and reintroduces the AV.W1 'too dark' class. The variance/lowest-sector selection should run in the working color space, not gamma.

WGSL twin drift: the multi-pass passes that splice OETF_WGSL/OKLCH_MATRICES_WGSL (kuwahara does) must keep splicing the shared procedural-color WGSL twin — never re-author the matrices inline. proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence + proof:webgpu-substrate-single clause 3 guard this; a hand-copied matrix in a new pass is the divergence bug.

Compute on Safari: DESIGN.md already notes Safari compute limits and chose a FRAGMENT path for the base field. If the tensor/kuwahara passes go compute-storage-texture, validate workgroup-size limits and storage-texture support on Safari 26; the fragment render-to-texture form is the more portable floor and keeps a single code path with the base field.

notes.facet: WGSL ↔ GLSL parity strategy — single-source shared chunks, codegen, and equivalence testing on a REAL device (for the AX aurora WebGPU/WebGL2 dual-backend engine)
sotaTechniques: REAL-DEVICE WGSL EXECUTION via dawn.node (the `webgpu` npm package) — Google's Dawn compiled as a Node native addon ships prebuilt binaries for macOS (Intel+ARM), Windows, Linux; `create([])` yields a headless `navigator.gpu`, you `requestAdapter()`/`requestDevice()`, run a real WGSL compute or render-to-texture pass, and `mapAsync`/`getMappedRange` reads the bytes back into a typed array. This makes the WGSL string ACTUALLY COMPILE AND RUN in CI — closing the 'WGSL cannot run in node' caveat that forces glass-ui's current hand-transcribed `aurora-color.wgsl-port.ts` mirror.

GENERATE-DON'T-TRANSCRIBE single-source codegen (Naga IR) — Naga (Rust, powers wgpu/Firefox; also a Go port and a wasm `glsl_wgsl_compiler`) parses GLSL into a common IR and emits WGSL via its wgsl-out backend, at build OR runtime. The strategy g-device-api (antvis) ships: author ONCE in GLSL, machine-emit the WGSL. This makes drift structurally IMPOSSIBLE (one author-source, generated twin) rather than gated-after-the-fact — the strongest form of the single-source discipline glass-ui already aspires to with its spliced shared chunk.

DIFFERENTIAL / METAMORPHIC TESTING across backends (DarthShader, ECOOP/PLDI 2024-2025; ETH 'Divergence-Aware Testing' OOPSLA 2025) — the academic SOTA for shader-translator equivalence: take ONE source, translate to GLSL/HLSL/MSL/WGSL, run all backends, flag any numeric divergence; metamorphic transforms preserve semantics so output mismatch = a real bug. Named primitives: oracle reference impl, metamorphic equivalence, coverage-guided generation, and EXPLICIT NaN/Inf/precision divergence classes.

CPU REFERENCE-ORACLE differential testing (SwiftShader / WARP pattern) — the GPU-compiler-testing canon uses a CPU software rasterizer (SwiftShader, or D3D12 WARP on GH CI) as the trusted golden and compares mean per-pixel delta against a tolerance (threshold ~20/255 in the literature to suppress false positives). The WebGPU CTS itself runs this way on wgpu/Dawn CI. glass-ui's TS-port-vs-TS-port at 1e-6 is a degenerate one-pixel-no-device form of this — the real version renders both backends and diffs pixels.

PIXEL-READBACK GOLDEN-IMAGE regression in a headless browser (Playwright + GPU) — drive real Chromium/WebKit with `--use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan --ignore-gpu-blocklist` under xvfb (headless Chromium has NO GPU by default — must run headed-in-xvfb), screenshot the WGSL canvas AND the GLSL canvas, and compare with a perceptual/SSIM threshold. Storage-efficient variant: on-device MD5/hash of the GPU framebuffer instead of storing full goldens (IJETCSIT 2024).

NODE-GRAPH TRANSPILE (Three.js TSL) — the framework answer: author a JS node graph that transpiles to WGSL for WebGPU and GLSL for WebGL from one source. Named here as the canonical single-source approach AND as the one glass-ui must REJECT — TSL is inseparable from Three.js (no standalone node graph, no raw-shader authoring), which violates the engine's zero-dep / no-Three.js/TSL posture.

COLUMN-MAJOR-IS-THE-INVARIANT matrix convention — both GLSL `mat3` and WGSL `mat3x3f` are column-major and `mat * vec` is M·v, so a value.js row-major constant written as columns (the transpose) is byte-identical across both languages with NO re-transpose. This is the one piece glass-ui already has exactly right and is the load-bearing reason its verbatim-copy of the Ottosson matrices is sound.

pitfalls: atan2 IS A REAL-DEVICE PORTABILITY HAZARD, not a 1e-6-CPU concern. The WGSL spec allows atan2 a 4096-ULP error and leaves (0,0) UNDEFINED; NVIDIA/Intel-on-DirectX return 0 instead of small near-zero values for large args (gpuweb issue #3209). glass-ui uses atan2 in THREE load-bearing places: `oklabToOklch` (hue), the structure-tensor `theta = 0.5*atan2(2*Jxy, Jxx-Jyy)`, and the Kuwahara sector `atan2(ry, rx)`. A flat zone where `Jxy≈0 AND Jxx≈Jyy` hits atan2(≈0,≈0) — DESIGN.md notes the atan2 form is robust there for the eigenvector, but the DEVICE may still return a backend-specific value. The CPU port (Math.atan2, IEEE-exact) will NEVER reveal this — only a real-device readback across vendors does. Guard against (0,0) explicitly and treat hue/orientation as tolerant-not-exact across backends.

pow() OF A NEGATIVE BASE IS UNDEFINED in WGSL (imaginary result). The OKLab cube-root step uses `sign(lms) * pow(abs(lms), 1/3)` — CORRECT, it pre-takes abs(). But any future shared-math edit that drops the abs() (or any `pow(x, n)` where x can dip negative through a warp/jitter) is undefined on device and may NaN on one backend while the CPU port and the other backend stay finite. Audit every pow() in the shared chunk for a guaranteed non-negative base; the current code is safe but fragile.

textureSample REQUIRES UNIFORM CONTROL FLOW in WGSL (uniformity analysis). The painterly.wgsl.ts Kuwahara/tensor/smooth passes `textureSample` inside nested `for` loops with `if (dot(o,o) > R*R) continue;` and an early `break`. WGSL's uniformity analyzer can reject `textureSample` reached through non-uniform control flow with 'possibly non-uniform value passed here' (gpuweb #4332, #2899) — and Chrome TIGHTENED this in updates, so a shader that compiled last year can fail today. Use `textureSampleLevel` (explicit LOD, no implicit-derivative uniformity requirement) inside loops, or hoist the sample out of the conditional. This will surface ONLY on a real compile (dawn.node/browser), never in the CPU port — another argument for real-device gating.

HAND-TRANSCRIPTION DRIFT is the meta-pitfall the current design institutionalizes. `aurora-color.wgsl-port.ts` is a THIRD hand-written copy (GLSL string + WGSL string + the TS port that mirrors the WGSL). The gate proves port==oracle, but NOTHING proves port==actual-WGSL-string — the human can mis-mirror the WGSL into the TS port in a way that accidentally matches the oracle. Every additional hand-maintained mirror multiplies the surface for an undetected three-way disagreement. Codegen (Naga) or real-device execution collapses the copies; keeping all three hand-written is the anti-pattern.

DERIVATIVES DIVERGE: GLSL `fwidth`/`dFdx`/`dFdy` vs WGSL `fwidth`/`dpdx`/`dpdy` are SCREEN-SPACE and quad-based — they are NOT computable in a CPU port AT ALL, and the impasto relight (`relightImpasto` derives a normal from dFdx/dFdy(height)) plus any `fwidth` AA depend on them. The 1e-6 color equivalence covers none of this; only a real-device render diff covers the derivative-dependent surfaces. Be explicit that the equivalence gate's scope STOPS at the color/noise core and that derivative-bearing passes need pixel-readback parity.

HEADLESS GPU IS A CI TRAP. Headless Chromium uses NO GPU by default (SwiftShader/llvmpipe fallback), so a Playwright pixel-parity job that thinks it's testing 'the GPU' may be testing a CPU rasterizer with DIFFERENT precision than the user's device — masking real divergence. Must run headed-under-xvfb with explicit ANGLE/Vulkan flags, or use dawn.node with an EXPLICIT non-fallback adapter and assert `!adapter.isFallbackAdapter` (which the runtime's `resolveRenderModeAsync` already checks — reuse that guard in the test).

DON'T REACH FOR TSL. The obvious 'single-source' framework answer (Three.js TSL node graph → WGSL+GLSL) is disqualified: it cannot be used without the full Three.js renderer and forbids raw-shader authoring, directly violating the engine's hand-written-WGSL/no-Three.js/no-TSL/zero-dep invariant. Naga-as-a-build-tool (codegen, not a runtime dep) is the posture-preserving equivalent.

pitfalls: FP16/f16 PORTABILITY CLIFF on mobile. WebGPU shader-f16 excludes ~58% of Android devices: it requires uniformAndStorageBuffer16BitAccess (only 42% of Android) and ZERO Qualcomm/Adreno devices are in the support list (gpuweb#5006). f16 MUST be capability-gated behind adapter.features.has('shader-f16') with a separate f32 fallback. On WebGL2/GLSL, mediump is a HINT: desktop drivers silently promote to highp (no win), mobile honor it (the win) with real precision loss. Never assume the speedup; profile.

FP16 PRECISION BREAKS THE COLOR/STRUCTURE MATH. The OKLab path uses pow(abs(lms), 1/3) and matrix transforms; f16's ~3 digits visibly shift hue/chroma and can NaN on sign(x)*pow(abs(x),..) near zero. The eigen-decomp squares gradients (Jxx=Gx*Gx) then sqrt(disc): squaring small luma deltas underflows f16 to zero, collapsing the tensor to the degenerate fallback everywhere. exp(-beta*d2) softmax and /max(accumW,1e-4) have no native f16 instruction (AMD) and amplify error. KEEP these f32; relax only the [0,1] color-blend/tooth/grain tail.

TEXTURE-LUT VIOLATES THE ZERO-DEP / ZERO-FBO INVARIANT IF DONE WRONG. DESIGN.md invariant 8 is ONE full-screen triangle, ONE fragment program, ZERO deps, no FBO ping-pong on WebGL2. A noise LUT is fine ONLY baked as an inline dataURI/Uint8Array (not an external fetch), uploaded once at init: never a second pass or external file. The half-res tensor FBO is a WebGPU-branch-only relaxation; do NOT add an FBO to the WebGL2 path.

DEPENDENT-TEXTURE-READ STALL on mobile if the LUT coord comes from a prior texture read. Apple/PowerVR: a sample whose coords come from ALU (not a varying) is a dependent read, free on ES3.0 hardware but stalls texel prefetch on weaker mobile GPUs. A noise LUT sampled at hash(p)-derived coords is inherently dependent; acceptable but don't CHAIN them (one LUT read feeding another's coords serializes the TMU).

PER-PIXEL BRANCH DIVERGENCE in the tensor degenerate guard. if (disc<1e-7) diverges across a warp -> lock-step stall; convert to branchless step/mix. Conversely do NOT optimize the UNIFORM medium-dispatch if/else chain: it's already optimal (every pixel same branch) and a switch/computed-dispatch refactor can defeat the compiler's uniform-branch elision.

TEMPORAL/RENDER-SCALE ARTIFACTS. Sub-native render scale + bilinear upscale softens the IGN dither and can REINTRODUCE the 8-bit banding the engine specifically fixed: the ign() display-space dither must run at OUTPUT res, AFTER upscale. Temporal amortization (redraw on breath clock) risks judder because the cursor-interaction write-path is rAF-independent per DESIGN.md and expects a live field; throttle ONLY the non-interactive idle drift, never the interactive axes.

MICRO-OPTIMIZATIONS THAT DON'T MOVE THE NEEDLE. proceduralpixels' loop-unroll, squared-distance, pipe-balance wins were each ~0.02-0.03ms: tiny vs the 0.43ms LUT win and 0.22ms geometry-reduction win. Chasing [unroll] or hand-inlining hash before fixing the 8x sampleBase recompute is premature. Profile FIRST (the engine has no GPU timer query in the loop): the smooth-default and vangogh-oil mediums differ ~10x in ALU, so measure per-medium before picking levers.
notes.facet: GPU performance for full-screen procedural shaders — ALU budget, texture-cache, FP16, early-out (applied to glass-ui's aurora WebGL2/WGSL fragment engine)
sotaTechniques: REDUNDANT-RECOMPUTE ELIMINATION (the #1 lever for THIS engine). The biggest ALU sink is sampleBase(): a FULL composition recompute (domainWarp -> nucleiField softmax loop -> samplePalette OKLab interp) called 8x inside structureTensorField() (the Sobel 3x3) and 4x inside mediumWatercolor(). Every neighbor tap re-runs the whole fbm-double-warp + nuclei + OKLab-cbrt chain. SOTA practice (proceduralpixels, IQ): never recompute across taps when the field is locally smooth. Path: factor sampleBase into a LUMA-ONLY tap (skip the vec3 OKLab interp + saturate) for the gradient taps, and cache the center sample as the (0,0) tap. Pure dead-work removal, zero visual delta.

TEXTURE-LUT FOR NOISE/HASH (offload SFU -> TMU, parallel with ALU). proceduralpixels measured procedural value-noise/sine-hash -> 64x64 LUT going 1.02ms -> 0.59ms (0.43ms of the win) because a 64x64 tex fits in L1 (~100% hit) and the texture unit runs concurrently with ALU. Aurora's fbm calls vnoise->hash21 up to 5x/octave; cellular does 9 sin-based hash22. Path: bake a tileable noise/gradient LUT (RG16F value+gradient) sampled with texture(); the cellular sin-hash is the top candidate. Keep the procedural path as the LUT-free zero-dep fallback.

FP16 / mediump RELAXATION ON COLOR & STROKE MATH (2x packed ALU + lower register pressure -> higher occupancy). AMD v_pk_*_f16 = two f16 ops/instruction; WebGPU enable f16 exposes it; Intel reports up to 25% ALU-bound. Aurora declares precision highp float GLOBALLY, never lowers. Color blend, stroke composite, paper-tooth noise, granulation, breath/grain post are [0,1] data: textbook mediump/f16 targets. Path: tag the medium-overlay and post stages mediump/f16vec3; KEEP highp/f32 for OKLab cbrt matrices, the eigen-decomp, and exp/division.

EARLY-OUT / UNIFORM-COHERENT BRANCHING over per-pixel divergence. GPUs run a warp lock-step; a divergent branch stalls the warp (Imagination/Apple/Samsung TBDR docs). Aurora's medium dispatch (if uMedium==1 ... else if) is UNIFORM: coherent and free, keep it. Hazard: structureTensorField's if (disc<1e-7) guard is per-pixel divergent. Path: branchless mix(fallbackDir, tangent, step(1e-7, disc)); add a UNIFORM early-out so the 8-tap tensor is skipped on smooth/pastel/watercolor (only oil/vangogh/crayon force tensor).

ANALYTIC / FEWER-OCTAVE FBM + SQUARED-DISTANCE (IQ canon). IQ: avoid if (smoothstep/clamp/step), reduce octaves to the visible minimum, never sqrt in a loop. Aurora's cellular() does min(m, dot(r,r)) then one sqrt: already correct. But fbm runs up to 5 octaves; on a soft DRIFT backdrop the top 1-2 are sub-pixel and invisible after the DPR-2 downscale. Path: budget-cap uNoiseOctaves to 3 for smooth/default; reserve 4-5 for painterly mediums (the proceduralpixels 4->3 layers 0.07ms win, per-medium).

SEPARABLE / DECIMATED MULTI-PASS FOR THE PAINTERLY FINISH (WebGPU branch). Kyprianidis-Kang 2009 anisotropic-Kuwahara + smoothed structure tensor (DESIGN.md staged AW.W7) is O(sectors x r^2)/pixel naively. SOTA: smooth the tensor with a SEPARABLE Gaussian (two 1D passes, O(2r)) and run the tensor pass at HALF res (low-frequency, upsamples cleanly). Path: on the WebGPU path compute the tensor in a half-res rg16float target, separable-blur, bilinear-upsample into the full-res Kuwahara finish: the standard real-time Kuwahara recipe.

SUB-NATIVE RENDER SCALE + TEMPORAL AMORTIZATION (cheapest global lever after offscreen-park). A drift backdrop has near-zero high-frequency content; native-DPR fill is wasted. Aurora caps DPR at 2 (AV_DPR_MAX) but full-canvas every frame. SOTA (UE TSR/TAAU: run image-space work at lower res before upscale): render the field to an offscreen FBO at 0.5-0.75x and upscale, and run painterly passes at a fraction of the breath framerate (field changes over 30-60s). Path: add a renderScale budget knob beside AV_DPR_MAX; couple painterly-pass cadence to the breath clock, not the rAF tick.

WORKLOAD BALANCING ACROSS PIPES (TMU || ALU || SFU). proceduralpixels' final win mixed ALU-hash and texture-hash so no single pipe bottlenecks. Aurora's hot mediums are ALU+SFU heavy (cos/sin/atan/pow/exp: OKLab cbrt pow(,1/3), exp(-beta*d2) softmax, atan per-stroke). A noise LUT moving hash to the TMU frees ALU for the OKLab/eigen math concurrently. Path: once a LUT lands, keep the TMU busy WHILE the ALU chews color/tensor math rather than serializing.
notes.applicability:
CONCRETE PATH FORWARD for the AX aurora waves, ranked by ROI against the actual hot paths in mediums.glsl.ts / composition.glsl.ts / aurora.frag.ts:

(1) HIGHEST ROI — kill the sampleBase recompute storm. structureTensorField calls sampleBase 8x and mediumWatercolor 4x; each re-runs domainWarp(double-fbm) + nucleiField(softmax loop) + samplePalette(OKLab interp). The Sobel only needs LUMA, so a sampleBaseLuma() that stops at dot(samplePalette(...), W_LUMA) and skips the vec3 saturate/value-variance chain slashes per-tap cost; reuse the center tap. Single-pass WebGL2, zero visual delta, inside profile:budget.

(2) HIGH ROI, LOW RISK — per-medium octave + tensor budgeting. Add AV_OCTAVES_SMOOTH=3 to budget.ts; gate structureTensorField behind a uniform uStrokeOrient==1 early-out so smooth/pastel/watercolor never pay the 8-tap tensor. The fbm loop already has the uNoiseOctaves break; clamp the default lower.

(3) MEDIUM ROI — noise/hash LUT. Bake a tileable RG16F value+gradient texture; route vnoise/hash22 through it on WebGL2 with the procedural form as the zero-dep fallback (a baked inline dataURI/Uint8Array LUT is not an external dep, preserving the no external libs invariant). cellular()'s sin-hash is top candidate.

(4) MEDIUM ROI — precision relaxation. Tag the medium-overlay + post stages mediump/f16 (color blend, tooth noise, granulation, grain). KEEP highp on the OKLab matrices, eigen-decomp, exp/division. On the WGSL twin this becomes enable f16, gated behind the shader-f16 adapter feature.

(5) FORWARD (WebGPU branch, AW.W7 staged) — half-res separable-Gaussian structure tensor in rg16float + bilinear upsample feeding the anisotropic-Kuwahara finish; makes the multi-pass headline frame-budget-safe.

(6) GLOBAL — add a renderScale knob beside AV_DPR_MAX and decouple painterly-pass cadence from rAF (couple to the 30-60s breath clock). The offscreen-park / content-visibility machinery the engine already has (createCanvasLifecycle) IS the modern-web-guidance efficient-background-processing pattern: already SOTA-aligned.

All of (1)-(4) and (6) are single-pass WebGL2-compatible and fit the existing budget.ts token-first ceiling pattern; only (5) needs the WebGPU branch.
