notes.facet: prefers-reduced-motion + offscreen/visibility/tab-hidden park strategies for continuous WebGL/WebGPU backdrops
pitfalls: Battery Status API is deprecated/removed in most browsers — do NOT gate quality on navigator.getBattery() (unavailable in Firefox/Safari, removed from Chromium); use connection.saveData + hardwareConcurrency + prefers-reduced-motion proxies. glass-ui correctly uses these, not Battery.

contentvisibilityautostatechange does NOT bubble in some implementations — attach DIRECTLY to the content-visibility:auto element or use {capture:true}. glass-ui attaches to canvas.parentElement which IS the cv:auto .aurora-root; silently breaks if a wrapper is ever nested between root and canvas.

Gating PRM on the SUSPEND SET (not the reschedule) blanks an on-screen reduced surface — under reduce you must draw ONE static frame then park; a 'reduce' suspend reason means the canvas never paints. glass-ui is reschedule-gated (correct); #1 trap when extending the park machinery.

Init-once PRM read misses runtime toggles — flipping OS reduce-motion (or a recorder forcing it) must freeze/wake LIVE; an init-time matchMedia().matches snapshot goes stale. glass-ui lifted this to a live change listener (AV.W7 G1); new axes must read the SAME live ref.

Freezing the rAF loop alone does NOT satisfy WCAG 2.3.3 — an input write-path (pointermove->uniform) fires outside the loop, so a parked-but-cursor-live field still moves under reduce unless the write-path early-outs. Easy to forget on a new interaction axis.

Scaling the absolute clock uTime under tempo makes the flow JUMP when tempo changes — scale the INTEGRATED dt of each axis, let the clock march; otherwise a reduce-toggle or pause/resume produces a visible discontinuity.

WebGL per-page context cap (~8 in Chromium) — N live contexts silently start losing the oldest; thumbnail baking MUST share one capture-mode context + dispose() via WEBGL_lose_context, never a context per preset.

Dynamic resolution scaling on web is hard — the web lacks reliable GPU frame-begin/end timestamps (gpuweb 2024-12-04), so a naive frame-time DRS reads JS/GC-polluted main-thread time and oscillates; if added, hysteresis + a dead-band are mandatory. The static DPR<=2 clamp is the safer default.
iOS low-power-mode + Safari cross-origin-iframe silently throttle rAF (~30fps / on-interaction) — the loop MUST be dt-driven, never frame-counted, or motion speed changes with the throttle.

WebGPU device.lost is a one-shot PROMISE not a re-fireable event — re-create the device AND all pipelines/bind-groups on loss (a fresh device invalidates every prior GPU object), unlike WebGL's same-canvas webglcontextrestored re-setup.

content-visibility:auto can clip overflowing effects — the blob's overflowing satellites needed contain:layout style, not the aurora's contain:content; match the contain keyword to whether effects bleed past the box.

prefers-reduced-motion is NOT prefers-reduced-data nor a low-power signal — conflating over-suppresses; glass-ui ORs them only for the conservative mount-time CSS-floor, but the runtime PRM freeze must be driven by PRM alone.
sotaTechniques: content-visibility:auto + contentvisibilityautostatechange park (BASELINE since 2025-09-15): set content-visibility:auto on the host, listen for contentvisibilityautostatechange whose `skipped` boolean signals the browser content-skips the offscreen element — pause rAF on skipped:true, wake on false. modern-web-guidance names this the PRIMARY mechanism for rendering-heavy canvas/WebGL over IntersectionObserver because it fires on the browser's own render-skip lifecycle (incl. pre-render margin).

IntersectionObserver rootMargin:200px park as the COMPAT-FLOOR: feature-detect 'contentVisibility' in document.documentElement.style; when absent (Firefox <130, Safari <26) fall back to an IO with rootMargin:'200px' driving the SAME pause()/resume() seam — the canonical pre-render-margin approximation so work wakes ~200px before scroll-in.

Page Visibility tab-hidden owner: a visibilitychange listener that suspends on document.hidden and resumes on show, each suspend reason owned by exactly one writer so a tab-show can never lift an offscreen suspension. Browsers throttle background-tab rAF to ~1Hz, but an explicit cancelAnimationFrame attaches ZERO frames and releases the draw entirely.

Live-monitored prefers-reduced-motion freeze (the JS gate a CSS reset cannot reach): matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') with a change listener; under reduce draw exactly ONE static frame then park — gate the RESCHEDULE never the suspend Set so an on-screen reduced surface paints once and never blanks. Live re-monitoring means toggling the OS setting freezes/wakes live. Mandatory because a WebGL rAF loop is invisible to a CSS @media(prefers-reduced-motion){animation:none} reset.

Demand-driven scheduling (render-on-demand / dirty-gate): reschedule ONLY while there is live motion (drift uniforms non-zero OR cursor still easing OR a decaying interaction burst). At steady-state the next frame is pixel-identical so the loop parks itself even on-screen/unreduced — zero idle GPU for a settled field. The single biggest battery lever for a 'continuous' backdrop that is visually static most of the time.

WCAG 2.2.2 Pause/Stop/Hide control (Level A, INDEPENDENT of PRM): any auto-starting non-essential motion >5s running in parallel with content MUST expose a user-reachable pause/stop/hide control to ALL users (not gated behind prefers-reduced-motion). The control binds the existing renderer suspend seam (a manual reason), not a parallel pause path. No 5-second exception for continuously-updating content.

Master-tempo scalar suppression seam: a single tempo multiplier (0 under reduce, 1 otherwise) scaling the INTEGRATED dt of every axis — NEVER the absolute clock uTime — so every drift/interactive axis freezes through one seam. Scaling the integration step lets tempo change mid-flight without the flow jumping; the absolute clock keeps marching so a time-orbited term stays frozen-consistent under reduce.

Interaction write-path PRM early-out: a pointermove/scroll write that mutates shader state fires INDEPENDENT of the parked rAF, so freezing the loop is not enough — the write-path must early-out on the live reducedMotion ref or a parked loop with a live cursor write still moves the field (WCAG 2.3.3). The write-path reads the SAME single live PRM ref as the loop — no parallel matchMedia.

DPR clamp + adaptive resolution scaling (the GPU fill-rate lever): clamp backing-store devicePixelRatio to <=2 so a 3x phone does not pay 9x fragment cost for a soft gradient where 4x is imperceptible. The SOTA extension is FRAME-TIME-DRIVEN dynamic resolution scaling — measure frame/GPU cost and down-scale the render-target under a budget, trading sharpness for FPS (VR/console DRS idiom, emerging on web via per-frame backbuffer resize).

Device-tier substrate downgrade at mount (CSS-floor over WebGL): resolve a low-power tier ONCE at setup from hardwareConcurrency<=4 OR prefers-reduced-motion OR connection.saveData, and on any low signal never arm WebGL — paint a zero-JS/zero-GPU CSS-gradient placeholder (from the same palette stops) as the permanent surface. Doubles as the WebGL2-unavailable fallback and lazy-arm first frame.

Backend-agnostic lifecycle carve (WebGPU parity): factor the schedule (suspend Set, demand gate, content-visibility park, tab-hidden owner, live PRM) into ONE backend-agnostic core; WebGL2 and WebGPU backends are thin wrappers. A parked rAF attaches zero frames on BOTH backends so the WebGPU dispatch inherits the park gate for free. WebGPU additionally needs the device.lost promise self-heal (re-create device + ALL pipelines on loss) analogous to the WebGL webglcontextlost/restored pair.

Shared offscreen capture context under the per-page WebGL-context cap (~8 in Chromium): bake N preset thumbnails through ONE capture-mode context (renderAt(frozenT)+toDataURL per preset, then dispose() via WEBGL_lose_context) rather than N live contexts that blow the cap. Capture-mode pre-seeds a manual suspend so the loop never auto-runs.

Shader-cost reduction for the painterly field (Inigo Quilez fBm idiom): keep fBm octaves low and PREVENT loop-unrolling on the fbm() loops (a real IQ optimization cut runtime 1.2x and compile time 4s->1s) — fewer noise taps per pixel is the per-frame fill-rate win that compounds with the DPR clamp on mobile where a full-viewport fragment shader is fill-rate-bound.

notes.facet: Cursor-as-light interaction — pointer-driven uLightDir, specular catch-light tracking, decaying swirl-burst on flick
sotaTechniques: IQ exponential impulse envelope — expImpulse(x,k)=k*x*exp(1−k*x): a one-line shaping curve that snaps to a peak of 1 at x=1/k then decays slowly. The canonical 'grows-fast-decays-slow' envelope for a flick burst; its quadratic-cheap twin is 2*sqrt(k)*x/(1+k*x*x) (no exp), and the sustained variant min(x²/f², 1+(2/f)*s*exp(−k*s)) gives independent attack(k)/release(f) widths — the right shape for a 'hold-then-release' swirl that the current linear `burst *= 0.96` per-frame ramp only crudely approximates.

Framerate-independent exponential smoothing — pos += (target−pos)*(1−exp(−lambda*dt)) (Holmer/Driscoll): the dt-correct replacement for a fixed per-frame lerp constant. A spring-mass-damper (critically-damped SmoothDamp: x' += (−omega²*(x−target) − 2*omega*v)*dt; v integrates) adds the ease-in S-curve a raw exponential lacks — the standard for camera/pointer follow that feels weighted, not robotic.

Pointer-event input fidelity for rAF shaders — getCoalescedEvents() unpacks every hardware sample coalesced into one frame-aligned pointermove (Chrome dispatches pointermove right before rAF since Chrome 60), so a 120/240Hz pen path is reconstructed instead of one point/frame; pointerrawupdate is the un-coalesced high-precision stream; getPredictedEvents() returns extrapolated future positions to 'draw ahead' and hide latency. Integrate per-sample velocity across the coalesced batch, not just (last−prev), for an accurate flick magnitude.

Stable-fluids pointer wake (Stam 1999 semi-Lagrangian + Dobryakov WebGL-Fluid-Simulation) — a ping-pong velocity texture: trace-back advection v(x)=v(x−v*dt), multiply by a dissipation factor, then add a delta-tracked Gaussian splat (exp(−|x−p|²/r²)) along the pointer velocity; a click adds a radial outward impulse. Vorticity confinement (Steinhoff/Fedkiw) re-injects energy at detected curls so eddies persist rather than dampening to mush — the SOTA 'lingering swirl' vs an instantaneous deflection.

Pointer-as-light specular tracking (Apple Liquid Glass 2025 idiom; Blinn–Phong half-vector) — the highlight is spec=pow(max(dot(N,H),0),shininess) with H=normalize(L+V) and L driven from the pointer (and DeviceOrientationEvent.beta/gamma on mobile, requestPermission-gated on iOS13+). Liquid Glass moves the catch-light from BOTH pointer-track and gyroscope. Modulate shininess by surface 'wetness'/height so ridges catch a sharp glint, flats a broad sheen.

Structure-tensor-derived normal for painterly relight — the same Sobel structure tensor J=[[Gx²,GxGy],[GxGy,Gy²]] that orients ETF strokes also yields a height/gradient normal N≈normalize(−dFdx(h),−dFdy(h),1/scale); lighting that normal with a pointer-driven L makes the catch-light rake ACROSS the painted bands as the cursor moves (light congruent with the brushwork), the painterly-NPR relight result.

CSS-custom-property pointer light (the 'spotlight follows pointer' design-system pattern) — write --mouse-x/--mouse-y once per rAF and let a radial-gradient/mask or color-mix paint the catch-light on the compositor with pointer-events:none; zero per-frame JS paint. The reduced-motion / non-WebGL2 fallback tier for cursor-as-light that still reads as a tracked highlight on the CSS placeholder.
notes.applicability: "The engine already has the SEAMS — uLightDir (movable impasto catch-light via relightImpasto's Blinn half-vector), uCursorVelocity/uCursorBurst flow deflection, a linear cursorModel, and a staged WebGPU wake.wgsl.ts. The SOTA upgrades drop onto these without new architecture. (1) Replace the linear `burst = min(1, burst + speed*4)` ramp + `burst *= 0.96` decay in cursorModel.ts with an IQ expImpulse/sustained-impulse envelope keyed off a flick-trigger timestamp — gives a crisp snap-and-tail flick instead of a saturating accumulator; it routes through the same tempo-scaled advanceCursor so PRM-freeze is preserved. (2) Swap the fixed-constant lerps (CURSOR_POS_LERP=0.22, CURSOR_STRENGTH_LERP=0.18) for dt-correct 1−exp(−lambda*dt) so easing is identical at 60/120/144Hz — the rest-epsilon demand-park logic is unchanged; optionally a critically-damped spring for uLightDir so the catch-light glides with weight. (3) In useCursorInteraction.onPointerMove, consume e.getCoalescedEvents() and integrate velocity across the sub-frame samples before injectCursorVelocity — a fast flick currently under-reports because one pointermove/frame loses the intra-frame path; getPredictedEvents() can pre-aim uLightDir to cut perceived lag. (4) Make uLightDir's L truly pointer-driven in frameLoop.ts (today it orbits on uTime and only PULLS toward cursor by strength) — drive L.xy from the eased cursor and lift L.z so the Blinn highlight in relightImpasto rakes the impasto/ETF bands; add a DeviceOrientationEvent (requestPermission-gated) fallback for touch devices with no hover. (5) The wake.wgsl.ts stable-fluids pass is already correct Dobryakov pattern — add vorticity confinement to the advect step so a flick leaves a persistent eddy, and feed the IQ radial-impulse envelope into the click rippleAmp. (6) Author a CSS-custom-property catch-light on the aurora-placeholder (--aurora-light-x/y radial-gradient) as the renderMode:'css' / PRM tier so cursor-as-light degrades gracefully. All of this is single-pass WebGL2-safe except the wake (WebGPU, already gated); nothing violates DESIGN.md invariant 8."
pitfalls: uTime-vs-dt discipline (already a documented W11 rule): scale the INTEGRATED dt of the burst/velocity by the master tempo, never uTime — scaling the clock makes the flow jump when tempo flips. The IQ expImpulse must be driven by (now − flickStart) wall-clock so it keeps decaying through a parked-then-resumed loop without a discontinuity; gate INJECTION (not the envelope's clock) by tempo.

PRM / WCAG 2.3.3 + 2.2.2: cursor-as-light is motion-from-interaction — the pointermove write-path (injectCursorVelocity) fires INDEPENDENT of the parked rAF, so it must early-out on handle.reducedMotion (the engine already does this; any new coalesced-events path must preserve the early-out). DeviceOrientation light-drive is also motion and must be PRM-gated and permission-gated (iOS requestPermission must be behind a user gesture or it silently no-ops).

getCoalescedEvents portability: coalesced events are NOT hit-tested — currentTarget/eventPhase are defaults and stopPropagation is a no-op on them; only read clientX/Y/movement. Safari historically lagged on coalesced/predicted events; feature-detect (typeof e.getCoalescedEvents === 'function') and fall back to the single event. Always clamp the per-sample delta (the engine's 0.12 CLAMP) so a tab-in/scroll-jump teleport doesn't inject a giant burst.

Specular instability from derivative normals: N from dFdx/dFdy(height) is screen-space and noisy at low DPR — a pointer-driven sharp shininess can shimmer/alias on thin strokes. Clamp shininess by paint height (the engine's mix(8,64,height) is the right instinct) and keep the spec term in LINEAR before aces() (the proof:aurora-space-gamma seam) or the catch-light blows out post-tonemap.

Velocity from a single pointermove under-samples on high-refresh displays AND over-samples on 240Hz pens — without coalesced-event integration the flick magnitude is framerate-dependent, which is exactly the bug class the dt-correct smoothing is meant to kill. Compute speed from summed coalesced sub-deltas / real elapsed time, not per-event.

WebGPU wake portability: the stable-fluids ping-pong + vorticity confinement is WebGPU-only (multi-pass) — it must stay the capability-gated ENHANCEMENT with the WebGL2 single-pass uCursorBurst deflection as the zero-regression fallback (DESIGN.md invariant 8). A software/fallback adapter (isFallbackAdapter) is slower than the WebGL2 path — don't run the wake on it. The velocity texture format (rg16float) needs a feature/limits check.

Spring/critically-damped smoothing can overshoot — for a light direction a small overshoot reads as a pleasant 'settle', but for the cursor POSITION feeding nucleus-drag it would cause the dragged nucleus to wobble past the pointer; keep the existing snappy lerp for position-CRUD and reserve the spring for the light/aesthetic axes only.

Don't let the catch-light create a single focal locus — DESIGN.md non-invariant: 'no single focal point driving palette'. The pointer-light must modulate the impasto RELIGHT (a material highlight) only, never the palette-id or composition, or it reintroduces the v1–v3 visible-locus error.

notes.facet: Velocity-reactive flow fields + scroll-coupled palette/breath motion
sotaTechniques: CURL-NOISE (DIVERGENCE-FREE) FLOW FIELD — Bridson's standard. Build velocity as the curl of a noise potential field: in 2D from a scalar potential psi(p,t), v = (∂psi/∂y, -∂psi/∂x), sampled by central differences over a small span. The curl operator is divergence-free BY CONSTRUCTION (no sources/sinks), so the field reads as incompressible turbulent gas rather than radial fans — every streamline closes into eddies. Time-animate by panning the sample point: psi sampled at p + panSpeed*t (the field scrolls; nothing pumps).

VELOCITY-AS-POTENTIAL-PERTURBATION (the velocity-reactive seam). Pointer velocity feeds the FLOW by perturbing the potential/advection — a fast flick injects a transient additive term to psi (or biases the curl sample) that decays over ~1s, distinct from a steady positional attractor. This is the SOTA upgrade over the current discrete swirl-burst: instead of rotating the final dir by atan2 blend, add the velocity vector into the potential field so the deflection is itself divergence-free and curls naturally.

SEMI-LAGRANGIAN STABLE-FLUIDS POINTER WAKE (Stam 1999 / Pavel Dobryakov WebGL2 ping-pong). A persistent RG16F velocity texture: each frame backward-advect (sample velocity at p - v*dt, unconditionally stable), apply dissipation (multiply by ~0.98), and SPLAT a Gaussian pointer impulse delta-tracked from pointer motion. The cursor leaves LINGERING self-advecting eddies, not an instantaneous swirl. A click writes a radial-ripple impulse. This is the genuinely-stateful form the DESIGN.md already stages for the WebGPU `wake` axis (§7); it requires FBO ping-pong → WebGPU/multi-pass only.

SCROLL-VELOCITY VIA SPRING-SMOOTHED DERIVATIVE (Motion's useScroll→useVelocity→useSpring→clamp chain). Take d(scrollProgress)/dt, pass through a spring (stiffness~100, damping~30-50, restDelta~0.001) so it ramps and DECAYS smoothly to zero at rest, then clamp/map the smoothed velocity to a bounded effect factor (Motion clamps skew to ±30°). The clamp + spring-decay-to-rest is the key idiom: fast scroll spikes the factor, scroll-stop springs it back to baseline — no permanent drift.

NATIVE SCROLL-DRIVEN ANIMATION (animation-timeline: scroll()/view(); scroll-animations-1). Couple a CSS custom property (e.g. --aurora-scroll-progress) to scroll position WITHOUT JS — the progress runs on the compositor, always in sync with the user's scroll, GPU-accelerated. Read it into the shader via a CSS var → uniform bridge. Baseline-limited (Chrome/Edge 115+, Safari 26; NOT Firefox) so it is the @supports-gated primary over a JS useScrollProgress fallback — exactly glass-ui's existing scroll-driven.css pattern.

scrollend EVENT FOR DEFERRED HEAVY WORK (replaces setTimeout scroll-debounce). The browser fires scrollend EXACTLY when scroll rests (transitions done, touch released). Use it to gate any expensive re-bake (palette LUT re-derive, render-mode re-probe) so per-frame scroll only nudges cheap uniforms and the costly work lands once at rest.

OKLCh PALETTE BREATHING (perceptually-uniform hue/L drift). Animate palette stops in OKLCh — drift L or h on a slow sinusoid (the existing breath uniform) so the wash brightens/hue-rotates without chroma or lightness jumps that RGB/HSL would introduce. Scroll-couple by mapping smoothed scroll progress onto the breath phase or a hue offset, so scrolling 'advances' the palette through its arc. glass-ui already has the in-shader OKLCh interpolation (mixPaletteOklchArc) — this is just driving its phase from scroll.

LAYERED MULTI-OCTAVE TIME-OFFSET WAVES (Alex Harri's flowing-gradient recipe). Stack 3-4 simplex-noise octaves at staggered wavelengths (L, L/1.3, L/1.86, L/3.25) and speeds with per-layer phase offsets to prevent synchronization, and drive a 'breathing' blur/value via pow(noise,4) biasing — organic non-repeating motion from pure time accumulation. The directional drift constant F (~0.043) added to x is the cheap global-flow term.

MASTER-TEMPO dt-SCALING (NOT clock-scaling) — the suppression discipline. Scale the integrated dt of every motion axis by a single tempo scalar (0 under prefers-reduced-motion/pause, 1 otherwise), NEVER uTime itself. Scaling the absolute clock makes the flow jump when tempo changes; scaling only the integration step keeps the clock marching and freezes cleanly. glass-ui already encodes this in advanceCursor's `k` factor — the SOTA confirmation is to route scroll-velocity and breath-phase integration through the same seam.
notes.applicability:
PATH FORWARD for glass-ui's engine (grounded in the read of cursorModel.ts / flow.glsl.ts / useAurora.ts):

(1) UPGRADE THE VELOCITY-REACTIVE FLOW from discrete-swirl to curl-coherent. The current `uCursorBurst` branch in flow.glsl.ts (lines 80-92) rotates the final `dir` by an atan2 angle-blend toward the velocity direction — it works but the deflection is not divergence-free and reads as a local twist. SOTA: inject the smoothed `uCursorVelocity` as an additive perturbation to the curl-noise POTENTIAL before taking the curl (or add a Gaussian-weighted velocity vector into the flow field pre-normalize), so the velocity wake is itself incompressible and curls into eddies. The CPU model in cursorModel.ts (velX/velY/burst, CURSOR_VELOCITY_LERP=0.3, CURSOR_BURST_DECAY=0.96) is already the right shape — it is the SHADER consumption that should move from angle-blend to potential-perturbation. Keep the 0.12 delta clamp (teleport guard) — it is correct.

(2) REPLACE THE CRUDE SCROLL→cursorRadius COUPLING. useAurora.ts lines 238-244 currently maps scroll progress onto `setCursorRadius(0.2 + p*0.25)` — a weak, semantically-odd axis (scroll should not change the pointer halo size). SOTA path: (a) add scroll VELOCITY not just position — derive d(progress)/dt, spring-smooth it (the Motion idiom; glass-ui already ships useSpringOrchestrator in composables/motion), clamp it, and map onto a bounded `uScrollFlow` term that biases the global flow drift direction/speed (fast scroll = field streams faster, decays to breath-pace at rest); (b) map scroll POSITION onto the OKLCh breath PHASE (a `uBreathPhaseOffset` uniform) so scrolling advances the palette through its hue/L arc — the 'scroll-coupled palette' headline — rather than mutating cursor radius. Both ride the existing uniformBridge breath/paletteDrift seam (uniformBridge.ts lines 329-331).

(3) PREFER NATIVE scroll() TIMELINE where possible. glass-ui already has scroll-driven.css with @supports-gated scroll()/view() recipes and a JS useScrollProgress fallback. Bridge a `--aurora-scroll-progress` custom property via animation-timeline: scroll() into the breath-phase uniform read on the compositor thread, falling back to the existing useScrollProgress watch (Firefox + Safari<26). This moves the per-frame scroll read off the main thread.

(4) THE WEBGPU `wake` AXIS = STABLE-FLUIDS. The DESIGN.md §7 already stages 'stateful pointer wake (WebGPU)' as Dobryakov's ping-pong velocity texture — confirmed SOTA. The applicability is: this is the ONLY place a true lingering wake belongs (it is multi-pass / FBO ping-pong, banned on the WebGL2 single-pass fallback by invariant 8). The WebGL2 path stays the curl-potential-perturbation approximation; WebGPU gets the advected RG16F velocity field + Gaussian splat + dissipation + click-ripple impulse.

(5) GATE HEAVY RE-BAKES ON scrollend. Any scroll-coupled palette re-derive (deriveAurora) must NOT run per scroll frame — nudge cheap uniforms per frame, fire the costly LUT re-bake on the scrollend event. Per-frame work stays uniform-upload only.

All of this routes through the master-tempo seam (advanceCursor's k) so prefers-reduced-motion / DockBackgroundToggle pause zeroes the velocity, scroll-flow, AND breath-phase integration — the single suppression seam glass-ui already binds.
pitfalls: CLOCK-SCALING JUMP: scaling uTime by tempo (instead of the integrated dt) makes the flow field VISIBLY JUMP the instant tempo changes (PRM toggle, pause). glass-ui's advanceCursor already scales the retained fraction, not the clock — any new scroll/breath axis MUST follow suit or it will tear on reduced-motion toggle.

POINTERMOVE/SCROLL FIRE FASTER THAN rAF: pointermove and scroll/wheel events fire more often than one frame; calling injectCursorVelocity or a scroll handler synchronously per event piles up work and janks the compositor. Throttle velocity injection to rAF (coalesce deltas) and register scroll listeners as { passive: true } so the browser need not wait on the handler to scroll.

VELOCITY SPIKE ON TELEPORT: tab-in, programmatic scroll, or a scroll-jump produces a huge instantaneous delta → a giant burst/velocity spike. The existing 0.12 clamp in injectCursorVelocity guards pointer; the scroll-velocity path needs the SAME clamp (and ideally ignore the first sample after a visibility change).

SCROLL-DRIVEN-CSS PORTABILITY: animation-timeline: scroll()/view() is NOT Baseline — Firefox has zero support and Safari only from 26 (Sep 2025). It MUST be @supports-gated ((animation-timeline: scroll()) and (animation-range: 0% 100%)) with the JS useScrollProgress fallback; do NOT ship the scroll-timeline-polyfill (known-broken per modern-web-guidance). The (animation-range) clause in the @supports is mandatory to exclude partial-support browsers.

STABLE-FLUIDS IS WEBGPU-ONLY: the lingering pointer-wake (ping-pong velocity texture + advection) is genuinely multi-pass and CANNOT run on the WebGL2 single-pass fallback (DESIGN invariant 8). Attempting it on WebGL2 violates the zero-dep single-pass contract. The WebGL2 path must stay the stateless curl-potential approximation; the wake is a capability-gated WebGPU enhancement only.

RG16F / float-texture support: a fluid velocity field wants a half-float render target (rgba16float / RG16F). On WebGL2 this needs EXT_color_buffer_float (not universal on older mobile GPUs); the format/pass-count belongs in the CONSUMER per proof:webgpu-substrate-single, not the substrate.

OKLCh BREATHING OUT-OF-GAMUT: drifting L or h in OKLCh can push a stop outside sRGB gamut (especially high-chroma blues), producing a clipped/desaturated flash. Clamp the breath excursion or gamut-map; do not let scroll position drive an unbounded hue rotation.

SCROLL COUPLING + content-visibility PARK INTERACTION: the aurora root carries content-visibility:auto and parks its rAF offscreen. A scroll-coupled axis must not assume the loop is running — the scroll handler can fire while the surface is parked (it scrolled offscreen). Route scroll nudges through the demand-driven render-request, not a direct uniform write to a dead loop (mirrors the existing injectCursorVelocity early-out-on-reducedMotion discipline).

SCROLL-VELOCITY WITHOUT SPRING DRIFTS: mapping raw d(progress)/dt to an effect without a spring leaves a permanent offset when the user stops mid-scroll. The spring-decay-to-rest (restDelta) is what returns the field to breath-pace; a raw clamp alone does not decay.

WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions): velocity-reactive flow IS animation-from-interaction — it must be suppressible. glass-ui binds this via the master tempo + PRM seam; any scroll/velocity axis added outside that seam re-opens the violation (proof:aurora-interaction-prm is born-RED to catch escapes).

notes.facet: Atom-based parametric control models — collapsing the ~28-field AuroraConfig to <=7 intuitive atoms (zones/noise/color/mood/medium/medium-texture/motion + seed/interactivity). Grounded against the EXISTING resolveAtoms door at src/components/custom/aurora/composables/atoms.ts (AW.W6), which is a pure/total/default-preserving clamped-override mapper over DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG.
sotaTechniques: Disney 'Principled' artist-friendly parameter design (Burley 2012) — the canonical ruleset for collapsing many physical DOF into a few intuitive knobs: (1) use INTUITIVE not physical parameters, (2) AS FEW as possible, (3) each parameter normalized 0..1 over its plausible range, (4) allow push BEYOND [0,1] where meaningful, (5) EVERY combination must be robust + plausible (no setting produces garbage). This is the design-discipline backbone for the atom set itself.

Intuitive perceptual control space via PCA + RBF functionals (Serrano/Gutierrez & Myszkowski, SIGGRAPH Asia 2016) — compress the high-D low-level space with PCA to ~5 components, then train radial-basis-function functionals on a large user-rating study (56k ratings) that MAP a handful of perceptual attributes (e.g. 'glossy','metallic-like','soft') onto those components. The atom→config map is the same shape: a small semantic vector fanned (via a learned-or-authored functional) onto the full low-level config, with the functional guaranteeing perceptual monotonicity.

Semantic-slider mappers — Semantify (CLIP→3DMM, 2023) + Concept Sliders (LoRA, ECCV 2024) + TexSliders (CLIP-space, 2024): one slider PER semantic descriptor whose scalar value is a target 'amount' that a small mapper M (an MLP, or here a hand-authored recipe) expands into the many low-level coefficients; sliders are trained self-supervised (no manual labels) by optimizing a CLIP-score direction. The modern face of 'a few knobs drive a big config'; for glass-ui the mapper is hand-authored (Disney-style) rather than learned, but the slider-as-direction framing is the contract.

Inigo Quilez cosine-gradient palette — color(t)=a+b*cos(2pi*(c*t+d)), four RGB vectors (bias a, amplitude b, frequency c, phase d = 12 scalars) parameterize an ENTIRE continuous gradient. A maximally-compact 'color atom': a single seed + harmony can pick a,b,c,d and yield a full multi-stop ramp without authoring stops by hand — perceptually better if done in OKLab rather than RGB.

OKLCH algorithmic color-harmony generation — fix L (constant visual weight), fix C (constant saturation), step H at regular intervals to synthesize analogous/complementary/split/triadic/tetradic ramps; perceptually uniform so 'calm vs vivid' is literally a chroma scalar and 'lighter/darker mood' is an L scalar, with NO hue/sat drift (unlike HSL). This is the math under the existing `seed`+`harmony` atom and `deriveAurora`.

Seed→trait deterministic hashing (Art Blocks 'hash-to-traits', Chromie Squiggle) — a single hex seed deterministically derives every generative trait (gradient angle, colors, segment count). Same seed ⇒ same output, reproducible, while the combinatorial space stays vast. The `seed` atom should be the single source from which palette AND a stable nuclei arrangement (zones placement, drift phases) are derived via a seeded PRNG — glass-ui already has src/utils/prng.ts (mulberry32+hashString) to do exactly this.

Co-varying perceptual axes (the 'one knob moves several correlated low-level fields' principle, from both Serrano's attribute-correlation analysis and design-token semantic-axis practice) — a single 'mood/energy' atom must move the cluster of fields that are perceptually entangled (saturation + warpAmount + valueVariance + breathDepth) together along a monotone curve, because moving any one alone reads as a defect. The existing MOOD_ENERGY/MOTION_FIELDS records are exactly this pattern, but as 3-point LUTs; SOTA is a CONTINUOUS scalar t in [0,1] driving a curve, not 3 named stops.

Design Galleries / Sequential Gallery (Marks et al. SIGGRAPH 1997; Koyama et al. 2020; Shapira 2009) — dispersion-sampled thumbnail grids of representative points in the parameter space + a slider/bisection refinement loop, so the user picks visually rather than tuning numbers. The path forward for the demo panel: sample the atom space (seed×mood×medium) into a thumbnail gallery (the existing usePresetThumbnails bake harness already supports deterministic renderAt bakes) as the primary 'choose' UI, with the ≤7 atoms as the refine layer and the 28-field schema as the advanced escape hatch.

The current applyTexture/mood/motion fans are independent; they need cross-checks (the existing min() trick on breathDepth between mood and motion is the right instinct but is the only such guard). SEED DRIVES ONLY COLOR TODAY: `seed` fans to palette via deriveAurora but the nuclei come from the FIXED thirdsZones anchor table — so two different seeds produce identically-arranged compositions with only recolored zones. QUILEZ-COSINE IN RGB IS A TRAP: the cosine palette is gorgeous but a+b*cos in RGB space produces the same muddy-midtone / center-biased problem the DESIGN.md non-invariants explicitly ban (no bell-shaped fBm color-id). If adopted it MUST run in OKLab; otherwise it reintroduces a banned failure mode.

GALLERY THUMBNAIL CONTEXT-CAP: the design-gallery grid bakes many thumbnails; Chromium caps ~8 live WebGL contexts/page (already a documented hazard in DESIGN.md §7). A dispersion grid of 20+ atom samples MUST reuse the single shared offscreen capture context (update(frozen)+renderAt+toDataURL+dispose loop), never spin one context per cell.

DON'T SHIP ML INTO THE ZERO-DEP CORE: the strongest SOTA (Serrano RBF, Semantify CLIP, Concept Sliders LoRA) are LEARNED mappers. Importing any of them violates the aurora zero-dep + WebGL2-single-pass-universal invariants. They are research JUSTIFICATION for the atom→config shape, not a license to add a model. Any text-to-atoms LLM step lives in a consumer/demo, behind the door, never in src/.

Adding a Quilez cosine atom or a 'temperature/warmth' atom risks blowing the ≤7 budget that is the whole point (Disney rule 2: as few as possible). notes.facet: Generative-design parameter spaces — making every random seed yield a beautiful in-family result (total functions, clamped budgets)
sotaTechniques: Long-form 'weakest-output' curation loop (Tyler Hobbs, Fidenza): you do not curate OUTPUTS, you curate the PARAMETER SPACE itself — repeatedly generate large batches, find the worst examples, then narrow ranges or add combination-guards until bad results become statistically extremely rare. Quality is a property of the space, not of any one seed. This is the foundational mental model for the whole facet.

Total function / clamped-budget contract (shader & API robustness): every parameter mapper is a pure TOTAL function — every input (including out-of-range or adversarial) yields a valid in-range result via clamp/saturate, never NaN/undefined/out-of-gamut. GPU practice mirrors this with `saturate()`/`clamp()` at every uniform boundary and NaN-guards so one bad value cannot corrupt the pipeline. Out-of-range data is discarded/clamped at the boundary, not propagated.

Harmony-from-a-single-base-color (Sighack procedural color): never generate independent random channels — derive ALL palette stops as bounded perturbations of ONE seeded anchor (small hue variance for monochrome/analogous, bounded S/V jitter), because variations sharing a base 'tend to work together' by construction. Constrain randomness in a perceptual space (HSB/OKLCh), wrap hue at 360, clamp S/V/L, and bound the variance magnitude — perceptual jitter, not RGB jitter.

OKLCh perceptually-uniform palette generation with chroma-clamp gamut mapping (2024 design-token SOTA): build palettes in OKLCh so fixed-L across hues reads as equal brightness; generate harmonies by hue-rotation math (analogous ±30°, complementary 180°, triad 120°, split-complementary); and when a generated stop exits the sRGB gamut, GRACEFULLY reduce chroma (hold L+h, lower C until in-gamut) rather than hard-clip RGB. This is the canonical 'every derived stop is paintable' guarantee.

Inigo Quilez cosine palettes — color(t)=a+b·cos(2π(c·t+d)): a 4-vector (bias a, amplitude b, frequency c, phase d) closed-form palette that is C¹-smooth and total for ALL t∈[0,1]. Choosing a=b=0.5 centers output in [0,1] so it can never go out of range; integer c gives a seamless loop. A whole pleasing gradient family from 12 numbers — ideal for hashing a seed into 4 vectors that yield an always-smooth, never-muddy ramp.

Golden-ratio-conjugate hue stepping (φ⁻¹=0.6180339887): generate the i-th hue as (h0 + i·0.618033) mod 1. This low-discrepancy step maximally spreads N hues for ANY N with no clustering and no precomputation — each new hue bisects the largest remaining gap. The deterministic, total way to space multiple zones'/nuclei' palette positions so no two read as the same color.

Low-discrepancy / stratified-jittered placement (progressive multi-jittered sequences, golden-ratio LDS): place spatial elements (nuclei, focal points) by stratifying the domain into equal cells and jittering one sample per cell, or by a golden-ratio additive sequence, so layouts are evenly distributed and well-distributed at every prefix length — never clustered, never on a visible grid. Replaces a rule-of-thirds lookup with a total scatter that stays composed for any count.

Eased parameter remaps over linear (bell/sine/Bézier ramps): map a normalized control (0..1 'mood'/'energy') through a shaping curve before it hits the field — e.g. a bell-curve chroma ramp (peak chroma in mids, calm at the extremes) is the painterly 'saturated body, calm edges' law; warm-light/cool-shadow temperature coupling is a signed hue nudge across L. Co-varying axes through one eased knob keeps the high-D space on its aesthetic manifold.

MAP-Elites / Quality-Diversity illumination (academic, for offline validation): treat the parameter space as an archive binned over interpretable feature axes (e.g. mood × medium × zone-count), keeping the best exemplar per bin. As an OFFLINE tool it 'illuminates' which regions of your space produce good vs. degenerate results — the systematic, automatable version of Hobbs' weakest-output hunt, and a way to prove coverage (no dead bins) before shipping the space.

Deterministic seeded PRNG with stable hashing (fxhash long-form contract): one seed → reproducible output via a fixed PRNG; the same seed always paints the same image (essential for thumbnail bakes / SSR / snapshot tests). Combine with the above so a single integer/string seed fans out deterministically to a whole in-family config.
notes.applicability: OUR engine already implements the spine of this facet correctly — the work ahead is hardening and extending it, not inventing it. The seam is deriveAurora/deriveScene (color.ts), resolveAtoms (atoms.ts), and budget.ts. PATH FORWARD, mapped technique→site: (1) Weakest-output curation — the AX aurora waves should run a BATCH harness that samples N seeds × moods × mediums through resolveAtoms/deriveScene and surfaces the worst frames; this is the missing 'two months on Fidenza' step. proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip already asserts TOTAL+default-preserving; extend it to a coverage/degeneracy sweep. (2) Total-function contract — resolveAtoms IS already documented PURE+TOTAL with clampBudget at every override, and deriveAurora gamut-maps every stop via value.js gamutMapStop; this is exactly the SOTA contract — keep it and assert it for deriveScene too (it currently spreads MOOD_RECIPE values that are NOT all clamp-guarded the way resolveAtoms is). (3) Harmony-from-base + OKLCh — deriveAurora is already the textbook implementation: one OKLCh anchor, harmony hue-walk (deriveHue: analogous/complementary/triad/split-complementary/mono), DERIVE_L_BAND clamp [0.35,0.95] so no stop is pure black/white, bell chroma easing, gamut-map per stop. This is best-in-class; document it in the README as the named technique. (4) Cosine palettes — a candidate ADDITIVE harmony mode ('cosine'/'spectral') for deriveAurora that hashes the seed into IQ's 4 vectors for a guaranteed-smooth ramp, complementing the OKLCh hue-walk for rainbow/vivid moods. (5) Golden-ratio hue stepping — replace or augment the fixed hueSpread walk so N>4 stops never collide; and replace the 6-entry hardcoded thirdsNuclei/thirdsZones anchor LUT (which caps composed scatter at 6 fixed points) with a golden-ratio/stratified scatter that stays composed for any zone count up to MAX_NUCLEI. (6) Eased remaps — already present (bell/sine easeRamp, applyTemperature warm/cool) and is the right shape; the mood atom should co-vary through these curves rather than the current flat MOOD_ENERGY lookup where richer co-variation reads more 'designed'. (7) budget.ts caps (AV_MAX_COLORS=4, AV_MAX_BLOBS=3, AV_DPR_MAX=2, loop-duration band 8–15s) are the clamped-budget enforcement — resolveAtoms already clamps palette to AV_MAX_COLORS; ensure deriveScene + direct-config uploads ALSO clamp through the same caps at the uniformBridge boundary so an over-authored AuroraConfig cannot blow the frame budget (the budget.ts header already states this is the intent). (8) Deterministic seed — deriveAurora/deriveScene are DOM-free and deterministic; this already powers renderAt() thumbnail bakes.
pitfalls: Hard RGB clipping = ugly hue shifts. When an OKLCh stop exits sRGB, clipping channels independently shifts hue and posterizes. MUST reduce CHROMA holding L+h (value.js gamutMapOKLab) — our deriveAurora does this; any new palette mode (e.g. cosine) must route through the same gamut-map, not raw clamp.

Cosine palettes are NOT automatically in-gamut or non-muddy. IQ's formula is only guaranteed in-range when a+b≤1 per channel (a=b=0.5 is the safe centering); arbitrary hashed vectors can still produce muddy or clipped colors. A cosine mode must constrain the hashed a/b and re-validate against the same gamut+muddiness guards as the OKLCh path.

Linear interpolation in the wrong space muddies midtones. Interpolating two saturated complementary stops through sRGB/RGB passes through grey. Our shader already does in-OKLCh interpolation (mixPaletteOklchArc) and the in-srgb surface-tint choice is a DELIBERATE house identity (per CLAUDE.md AW.W26) — don't 'fix' that, but DO keep generated palette interpolation in OKLab/OKLCh.

Total ≠ tested-total. A clampBudget at each site is necessary but not sufficient — deriveScene currently spreads MOOD_RECIPE numbers that are not all individually clamp-guarded like resolveAtoms's overrides; an adversarial mood recipe edit could ship an out-of-range field. The proof must sweep deriveScene too, not just resolveAtoms roundtrip.

Hardcoded anchor LUTs cap variety and break above their length. thirdsNuclei/thirdsZones have exactly 6 hardcoded points; counts beyond that silently clamp and identical counts always produce identical layouts (no seed variety in placement). A golden-ratio/stratified scatter is the total replacement, but must stay deterministic for renderAt() bakes.

Golden-ratio hue stepping ignores harmony intent. φ-stepping maximizes DISTINCTNESS, which is the opposite of an analogous/monochrome family. Use it to de-collide stops WITHIN a chosen harmony band (jitter inside the band), not as the top-level hue walk, or it will fight the harmony scheme.

Determinism vs. interaction/animation. Seed-determinism only governs the static field; cursor/scroll/wake interactivity and time drift must NOT leak into the seed→config derivation, or thumbnail bakes (renderAt) and snapshot tests become flaky. Keep derivation pure; keep interaction in cursorModel/frameLoop.

Budget caps must bite at the LAST boundary (uniformBridge), not only in resolveAtoms. A consumer handing a raw AuroraConfig (bypassing atoms) can still over-author palette length / nuclei count; clamp at upload so no authoring path escapes AV_MAX_COLORS / MAX_NUCLEI / AV_DPR_MAX.

WebGPU/WebGL twin drift. Any new total-function color path (cosine, golden-hue) added to the CPU bake or the shared procedural-color chunk must be added ONCE in the shared GLSL/WGSL source (proof:single-color-core / proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence), or the seed→palette result diverges between backends — the same two-copy class as the AV.W1 'too dark' bug.

MAP-Elites is offline-only here. It's a validation/illumination tool for the dev loop, not a runtime dependency — don't ship an evolutionary loop into the bundle; use it to prove the space has no degenerate bins, then bake the learned ranges into clamped constants.

notes.facet: Preset + derive systems — named editable baselines vs commit-on-write; per-preset clone semantics
sotaTechniques: **Three-tier token resolution (primitive → semantic → component)** — the canonical design-system layering (PrimeNG `definePreset`, Figma aliasing, design-tokens W3C draft): a *primitive* layer holds raw values, a *semantic* layer aliases primitives into named roles, a *component/instance* layer overrides only what diverges. Resolution walks the chain and the first explicit value wins. Maps to aurora as: `OklchStop[]` primitives → `AuroraConfig` semantic fields → per-preset overrides.

**Figma 'extended collections' (parent baseline + inherit-unless-overridden)** — the production analog of per-preset clone done right: an extended collection is *tied to* a parent and inherits any variable the child has NOT explicitly overridden, so parent updates propagate to un-touched fields while branded overrides persist. The algorithm is: resolve(field) = childOverride if present else parentValue. This is structurally different from glass-ui's current `structuredClone` snapshot, which freezes the WHOLE config and loses parent-tracking.

**Sparse-override / delta-from-baseline model (Unity prefab variants)** — store only the DIFF between an instance and its named base, not a full clone. Each instance is `{ baseKey, overrides: Partial<Config> }`; resolution is `{ ...resolve(base), ...overrides }`. Gives free 'isDirty per field', cheap revert (drop one override), and 'revert-to-baseline' that re-pulls upstream edits. Unity surfaces per-property Apply/Revert from exactly this representation.

**Immer `produceWithPatches` (forward + inverse patch recording)** — every edit emits `[next, patches, inversePatches]` where a patch is `{op:'replace'|'add'|'remove', path:[...], value}`. inversePatches give O(1) undo; forward patches let you *replay an instance's edits onto an updated baseline* (fork-and-replay) — the exact operation needed if the library's `DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG` evolves and you want existing user-tuned presets to inherit the new defaults for fields they never touched.

**`structuredClone()` for snapshot isolation (already in use)** — native deep copy is the correct primitive for the *snapshot* step (saving an outgoing slot). SOTA guidance (2026 comparisons) confirms `structuredClone` over `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` for the clone, and reserves Immer/patches for the *diff/undo/replay* layer that snapshots alone cannot express. glass-ui's `defaultClone` (toRaw + structuredClone) is current best-practice for the clone leaf.

**Seed→full-palette derive in OKLCH (perceptually-uniform generative palette)** — the modern color-system generator (oklch.fyi, the HN OKLCH theme-builder, PalGen): take one seed `{L,C,h}`, walk hue by a harmony rotation (complement +180°, triad ±120°, analogous ±28–60°, split-complement, monochrome 0°), ramp L across a clamped band, fall C off toward the pale apex, and gamut-map every stop back into sRGB. Warm-light/cool-shadow temperature coupling (warm the lights, cool the shadows) is the single most-cited painting rule layered on top. This is *exactly* `deriveAurora`/`deriveScene` — glass-ui is already at SOTA here.

**Bell-curve chroma easing + warm/cool temperature shift** — the 'saturated body, calm edges' curve (chroma peaks in the mid-stops, desaturates the extremes via `sin(πt)`) plus a signed hue nudge toward ~70° (warm) at the light apex and ~250° (cool) at the deep base. Both are present in glass-ui's `deriveAurora` (the `bell()` and `applyTemperature()` helpers) and match the OKLCH-generator literature's recommendations for painterly ramps.

**Lightroom 'preset = stored instruction set over an untouched original' (non-destructive baseline)** — the photographic-tool canon: the preset is a named *delta of develop settings* applied over the original; selective copy/sync lets the user paste only chosen sub-settings. The analog is: an aurora preset should be a named atom/override set over `DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG`, with the FULL resolved config derived on demand — never the source of truth stored fully-baked.

**Two-tier atoms-of-control door (Stripe/paper.design progressive disclosure)** — a ≤7 intuitive 'atom' surface (`seed/mood/medium/texture/motion/zones`) that fans out to the ~28-field author schema, with the full surface under an 'Advanced' escape hatch. PURE + TOTAL + DEFAULT-PRESERVING (`resolveAtoms(DEFAULT_ATOMS)` deep-equals the default). glass-ui's `atoms.ts` already implements this exactly; SOTA validates the contract (clamped-total mapping, default pass-through).
notes.applicability:
"glass-ui is ALREADY near-SOTA on two of the three sub-axes and has a clear, named upgrade path on the third.

SEED-DERIVE (deriveAurora/deriveScene in color.ts): at parity with the OKLCH-generator literature — harmony rotations, clamped L-band [0.35,0.95], bell-curve chroma easing, warm/cool temperature coupling, and per-stop value.js gamut-mapping are all present and correct. The path forward is small: (a) expose the harmony/easing/temperature knobs as first-class atoms (currently only `harmony` is an atom; `temperatureShift`/`chromaEasing` are buried in DeriveAuroraOptions and the MOOD_RECIPE), and (b) consider a 'derive-locks' axis so a user can pin one derived stop and re-derive the rest around it (the OKLCH-generator 'key color' pattern).

ATOMS DOOR (atoms.ts): at parity with the Stripe/paper.design two-tier model — PURE/TOTAL/DEFAULT-PRESERVING is the right contract and it is machine-asserted. No change needed; document it as the canonical consumer entry in the README.

PER-PRESET CLONE (useConfiguratorState.ts): this is the facet's real gap. The current `per-preset` mode stores a FULL `structuredClone` per slot (`liveClones: Record<string, T>`), snapshotting the whole config on every switch. This is the 'commit-on-write but N copies' model — it works for aurora's 'named editable baseline you return to' need, but it is the *Unity Apply-All hazard* in miniature: because each slot is a full frozen clone, a user-tuned slot can NEVER inherit a later change to the preset DEFINITION or to `DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG` for fields the user never touched (the Figma 'extended collection inherits un-overridden parent updates' property is absent). The SOTA path forward: re-express a slot as a SPARSE OVERRIDE `{ baseKey, overrides: Partial<AuroraConfig> }` resolved as `{ ...clone(presetDef), ...overrides }`. That single change delivers (1) per-field isDirty for free (currently isDirty is whole-config JSON-equality), (2) per-field revert (Lightroom selective-paste / Unity per-property Revert), and (3) baseline-inheritance so library default evolution flows into untouched fields. The `resolveAtoms` mechanism already proves the 'clone default + apply present overrides' pattern is viable and TOTAL — the configurator should adopt the same sparse-override shape that atoms.ts uses, unifying the two derive paths on one representation.

OPTIONAL (Immer): if undo/redo or 'fork an instance and replay onto a new default' is ever wanted, `produceWithPatches` is the named tool — but it is heavier than the sparse-override map and only warranted if interaction history becomes a requirement. The sparse-override model alone covers the named-baseline + per-field-revert needs without a new dependency."
pitfalls: **Full-clone-per-slot blocks baseline inheritance (the Figma/Unity lesson).** glass-ui's current `per-preset` mode `structuredClone`s the whole config into each slot, so a user-tuned slot is frozen against ALL fields — it can never pick up a later change to the preset definition or to `DEFAULT_AURORA_CONFIG` for fields the user never touched. Figma's extended collections and Unity prefab variants both avoid this by storing only the override delta and re-resolving the base live. Sparse overrides fix it; full clones cannot.

**Whole-config JSON-equality isDirty is coarse and fragile.** `defaultEquals` is `JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b)`, which (a) gives no per-field dirty signal (can't drive a per-property Apply/Revert UI), (b) is key-order-sensitive and breaks on `undefined`/`NaN`/`Infinity` (the aurora config has clamped floats — a `-0` vs `0` or float-format drift flips dirty falsely), and (c) is O(size) on every reactive read. A field-level diff over a sparse-override map is both cheaper and more precise.

**structuredClone throws on functions/proxies/class instances.** `defaultClone` already guards via toRaw + a typed error, but any future AuroraConfig field carrying a function (e.g. a custom easing callback or a ColorResolver injectable) will hard-throw. The sparse-override model narrows the clone surface (you clone the base def once, not the live config repeatedly), shrinking this blast radius. Keep the `clone` escape-hatch option.

**Snapshot-on-switch bleed.** `snapshotInto` deep-clones `config` into the outgoing slot on every `selectPreset`; if a consumer holds a reference to the live `config` proxy AND mutates it asynchronously after a switch, the snapshot can capture an in-flight intermediate state. The current code is correct (snapshot before write), but the ordering is load-bearing and untested for the async-mutation case — a sparse-override model sidesteps it because the override delta is computed, not snapshotted.

**Derive-everything-from-one-seed has a ceiling.** The OKLCH-generator discussions warn that a single seed cannot express a multi-pole composition (e.g. a warm-AND-cool dual-anchor scene) — `deriveAurora` walks ONE hue path. aurora's `nuclei` carry independent `paletteBias`, so the composition is multi-pole even when the palette is single-seed-derived; do NOT over-fit the derive to try to encode composition. Keep palette-derive and nuclei-layout as orthogonal axes (they already are).

**Gamut-map AFTER all ramp math, never before.** A common derive bug: clamp chroma/lightness into a per-stop budget and THEN gamut-map, vs gamut-map first and lose the ramp shape. glass-ui correctly gamut-maps each final `{L,C,h}` as the last step (`gamutMapStop` at the end of the loop). Preserve that ordering — temperature shift and chroma easing must run in unclamped OKLCh, with the single gamut-map as the exit.

**Atoms TOTAL-ness is a standing invariant, not a one-time check.** `resolveAtoms` must stay PURE/TOTAL/DEFAULT-PRESERVING as `AuroraConfig` grows (new fields, new mediums). Every new field needs either a default that survives the empty-atom pass-through or an explicit atom mapping with a `clampBudget`. The `proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip` gate enforces it; any new field added to AuroraConfig without touching atoms.ts is silently fine ONLY because of the clone-default base — but a new ATOM that forgets a clamp breaks TOTAL-ness. Treat clamp coverage as part of the field-addition checklist.

**Don't let URL/persist state freeze a stale full config.** If presets are ever made shareable (querystring/permalink), encode the SPARSE atoms/overrides + a version, NOT the fully-resolved config — otherwise a shared link freezes the library defaults at share-time and never inherits later default evolution (same failure class as full-clone slots, now persisted). Encode the derive inputs, re-derive on load.

notes.facet: ACES / filmic tonemapping + dithering for backdrop color grading; never-pure-black/white floors
sotaTechniques: AgX display transform (Sobotka, 2022; Blender 4.0 default) — the headline successor to ACES. Log2-encode linear color over a fixed EV window (AgxMinEv -12.47 .. AgxMaxEv 4.03), apply a per-channel sigmoid IN A ROTATED 'inset' primary basis (AgXInsetMatrix), then de-rotate (AgXOutsetMatrix). The inset rotation is the whole trick: it desaturates BEFORE the sigmoid so highlights roll toward white instead of skewing hue, killing ACES's notorious bright-blue->magenta and over-saturated-primary skews. three.js ships a LUT-FREE 6th-order polynomial fit of the sigmoid (agxDefaultContrastApprox = 15.5x^6 -40.14x^5 +31.96x^4 -6.868x^3 +0.4298x^2 +0.1191x -0.00232) — pure ALU, no texture, drop-in for a single-pass WebGL2 fragment shader. Optional 'Punchy'/'Golden' look = a post offset/slope/power + saturation grade.

Khronos PBR Neutral tonemapper (2024) — a 13-line, texture-free, hue-AND-saturation-PRESERVING operator built specifically for product/UI color fidelity (the design-system case, not the cinematic case). It is a 1:1 passthrough for colors below startCompression (0.8-0.04=0.76); only the brightest channel is compressed (newPeak = 1 - d*d/(peak+d-startCompression)), with a tiny selective desaturation (g, factor 0.15) ONLY in the compressed highlight region. A small black-offset (offset = x<0.08 ? x-6.25x^2 : 0.04 on the min channel) lifts near-blacks. Already in Three.js/Babylon/Filament/Blender 4.2+/model-viewer. Analytically invertible.

Hue-preserving luminance tonemap (the delta/Reinhard-Jodie family) — apply the tone curve to LUMINANCE only (L = dot(c, 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722)) then rescale color by L_out/L_in, OR blend per-channel<->luminance (Reinhard-Jodie: mix(c/(1+L), c/(1+c), c/(1+c))). Preserves hue exactly (no desaturation) at the cost of highlights staying colored rather than blooming to white. The minimal upgrade over the current per-channel Narkowicz ACES when hue stability matters more than filmic highlight rolloff.

TPDF (triangular-PDF) dithering over the current single-sample RPDF — Wronski's standard: subtract two independent uniform samples (r1+r2-1, range [-1,1]) instead of one (ign-0.5, range [-0.5,0.5]). TPDF DECOUPLES the dither's variance from the signal level, removing the residual noise-modulation/banding that a single RPDF sample leaves at quantization boundaries; cost is one extra hash. Amplitude stays 1 LSB = 1/255 for 8-bit. This is the single highest-signal dither upgrade for a slow/near-static gradient.

Blue-noise / spatiotemporal-blue-noise dithering as the perceptual ceiling — IGN (Jimenez) is specifically TAA-optimized; for a NON-TAA, slow-drifting backdrop, a precomputed blue-noise texture (or void-and-cluster mask, scrolled per frame) gives the least-visible stipple because its energy sits at high spatial frequencies the eye discounts. Trade-off: it costs a texture fetch, which collides with the zero-dep texture-free WebGL2 invariant — so it belongs on the WebGPU branch, not the WebGL2 fallback. For the fallback, TPDF white-noise via the existing hash is the right zero-texture choice; the frost.kiwi 'how to fix banding' reference confirms the exact IGN+1/255 form the engine already uses as the texture-free baseline.

Dither in the QUANTIZATION (display/sRGB) space, after the OETF — thetenthplanet 'Correct sRGB Dithering' + threadlocalmutex: 8-bit quantization happens on the sRGB-ENCODED value, so the additive noise must be added there (which the engine already does — IGN is post-OETF). The 'dither in linear' camp refers to gamma-AWARE error-diffusion where the level-selection WEIGHTING is computed by physical (linear) luminance; for additive-noise dithering the correct placement is post-transfer, matching the engine. This is a CONFIRMATION the current placement is right, not a change.

Chromatic (warm/cool, complementary-tinted) never-pure-black/white floors — the painting-practice SOTA: pure black and pure neutral white never appear in nature; shadows are darkened with the COMPLEMENT or a warm/cool bias, and neutral 100% white is reserved for specular highlights only. A perceptual floor authored in OKLCh (lift L off 0, keep a small C and a hue) reads as 'paint' rather than 'crushed black'; the current achromatic floor (clamp(col*0.985+0.008)) is a neutral grey lift that throws away this chromatic richness.

Tony McMapface (Stachowiak, 2023) — a maximalist hue-preserving display transform that explicitly models perceptual phenomena (Bezold-Brucke hue shift, Abney-effect avoidance, selective desaturation to avoid posterization). It is LUT-based (48^3 3D texture) so it violates the texture-free WebGL2 invariant; noted as the highest-fidelity option for the WebGPU enhancement branch only, not the fallback path.
notes.applicability:
"OUR engine today: a per-channel Narkowicz ACES fit (2.51/0.03/2.43/0.59/0.14) in tonemap.glsl.ts, clamped [0,1] in linear; an achromatic floor clamp(col*0.985+0.008); a separate hash21 film-grain term added in LINEAR before the OETF; and a 1-LSB single-sample IGN dither added in DISPLAY space after linearToSrgb. The whole pipeline is linear until the mandatory OETF at main(). PATH FORWARD (mapped to the AX aurora waves):

1) REPLACE Narkowicz ACES with a tonemap SELECTOR. The Narkowicz per-channel fit is exactly the operator that produces the ACES blue->purple skew and the bright-primary over-saturation the AW audit flagged ('specular extreme', aurora 'core dark'). Add an enum uniform (uTonemap) routing to: (a) AgX analytical (three.js polynomial fit — texture-free, single-pass-legal, the new default for vivid/cinematic presets), (b) Khronos PBR Neutral (13 lines, hue+saturation preserving — the right default for the wispy-sky / quiet content-over-aurora presets where brand color fidelity matters), and (c) keep Narkowicz as a legacy/cheap option. AgX + PBR Neutral are BOTH zero-dep, texture-free, and fit the §2 invariant-8 single-pass WebGL2 contract; the WGSL twin already has the OETF/OKLCh splice pattern (procedural-color.glsl.ts) so the same tonemap chunk can be twinned for the WebGPU branch with the existing proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence 1e-6 gate.

2) Note the input-range caveat: AgX and PBR Neutral are designed for HDR/EV-windowed input. The aurora field is a roughly-[0,1] linear palette LUT with modest valueVariance/breath overshoot, NOT a wide-EV HDR render. AgX over a near-SDR input will look LOW-CONTRAST/milky unless you pre-scale exposure into its EV window (or pick PBR Neutral, which is built for well-exposed [0,1]-ish input and is the safer drop-in here). PBR Neutral is likely the better headline default for this engine precisely because the aurora is a well-exposed designed backdrop, not an HDR scene — it preserves the authored OKLCh palette's hue/saturation and only tames the breath/valueVariance overshoot.

3) UPGRADE the dither RPDF->TPDF: change `(1.0/255.0)*(ign(fragCoord)-0.5)` to a two-sample triangular `(1.0/255.0)*(ign(fragCoord) - ign(fragCoord+vec2(0.0,height-ish offset)) )` (or two decorrelated hashes), keeping placement post-OETF and amplitude 1/255. Keep IGN as the generator on the WebGL2 fallback (texture-free, the frost.kiwi-confirmed baseline); stage a blue-noise texture only on the WebGPU branch. This directly attacks 8-bit mid-tone banding on the soft gradient, the worst at the low-chroma washes.

4) CHROMATIC FLOOR: replace the achromatic clamp(col*0.985+0.008) with an OKLCh-authored never-pure-black/white floor — lift L off zero by a few percent but with a small retained chroma and a warm-or-cool hue tied to the preset palette (e.g. floor toward the darkest palette stop's hue, not toward grey), and cap the ceiling below pure white reserving 1.0 for the impasto specular catch-light only. This is a one-function change in tonemap.glsl.ts that makes the darks read as 'deep paint' (Twombly/Frankenthaler soak-stain lineage in DESIGN.md §1) instead of 'crushed neutral'. It composes with the OKLCh color core already spliced into the shader (oklabToOklch/oklchToOklab are present), and it should run BEFORE the OETF in linear/OKLCh, with the OETF closing the seam unchanged.

5) The film-grain term (hash21 added in linear before OETF) and the IGN dither (after OETF) are TWO different noise stages with two different jobs — keep them separate: grain is a material/aesthetic linear-space texture (paperGrain), dither is a display-space quantization fix. Do not merge them; the README/wave docs should state this explicitly since they look redundant but aren't."
pitfalls: AgX/PBR-Neutral expect HDR/EV-windowed input; the aurora field is near-SDR [0,1] linear. AgX applied to it without exposure pre-scaling reads milky/low-contrast (the three.js forum's exact 'ACESFilmicToneMapping leading to low-contrast textures' complaint applies doubly to AgX). Validate the wispy-sky DEFAULT renders identically-or-better, not washed out — pick PBR Neutral as the safe default and gate AgX behind a per-preset 'cinematic' opt-in with an exposure pre-scale.

Tonemap operator swap shifts EVERY authored preset's look. The 11 demo presets (Sky/Dawn/Meadow/Oil*/Crayon*) were hand-tuned against Narkowicz; changing the operator changes their color. Per the 'presets in consumers' memory rule, re-tune presets in demo/stories/aurora/presets.ts, NOT by compensating in the library tonemap. Treat the operator as the library identity and let presets re-baseline.

WGSL twin divergence: any new tonemap GLSL must get a hand-transcribed WGSL twin certified to 1e-6 by proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence, or the WebGPU branch silently diverges from WebGL2 (the AV.W1 '~2.2x too dark' two-copy bug class). AgX's polynomial and the inset/outset matrices must be VERBATIM-copied (column-major already matches), never re-derived per-backend.

Blue-noise dithering needs a texture fetch — it VIOLATES the zero-dep, texture-free, single-pass WebGL2 invariant (DESIGN.md §2 invariant 8 / §3 'no external libraries, no FBO'). Restrict blue-noise to the WebGPU enhancement branch; keep TPDF white-noise (IGN-based, ALU-only) as the WebGL2 fallback dither. Do not smuggle a noise texture into the fallback.

Dither space is a known footgun: applying the noise in linear (before OETF) instead of display space (after OETF) re-introduces banding because 8-bit quantization happens post-transfer. The engine is already correct (IGN is post-OETF) — do NOT 'fix' it by moving the dither into linear during a refactor. Document this so a well-meaning cleanup doesn't break it.

Hue-preserving luminance-only tonemap keeps over-bright pixels COLORED instead of blooming to white — for an impasto specular catch-light (uLightDir relight) you actually WANT the highlight to desaturate toward white, so a pure luminance-only operator can make specular glints read as saturated color blobs. AgX/PBR-Neutral's selective highlight desaturation is the right middle ground; pure Reinhard-Jodie is not, on the painterly mediums.

Narkowicz ACES is NOT the real ACES RRT+ODT — it's a rational fit that ALREADY bakes in slight oversaturation; comparisons/screenshots that call it 'ACES' overstate fidelity. When documenting the change, name it precisely (Narkowicz fit -> AgX analytical fit / Khronos PBR Neutral) so the wave docs and README don't claim a swap of 'full ACES'.

The clamp(col*0.985+0.008) floor currently runs in LINEAR before the OETF; an OKLCh chromatic floor must also run in linear/OKLCh-from-linear and let the existing linearToSrgb close the seam — authoring the floor in display space would double-apply the transfer and shift the floor color. Keep the proof:aurora-space-gamma seam (tonemap+OETF order) intact.

Over-lifting the black floor or capping the white ceiling too aggressively reduces usable contrast and makes the backdrop muddy (the CSS guidance's 'color-mix toward white/black over-desaturates' caution). Keep the lift in the few-percent-L range and tie hue to the palette, not a fixed warm constant, or low-key dark presets will all converge to the same muddy tint.
