notes.facet: Compositing a backdrop UNDER content — opacity-ceiling, per-route saturation clamp, text-contrast over gradient art
sotaTechniques: **Worst-case-luminance contrast guarantee (WCAG G18/G145 + APCA dual-polarity).** For text over a VARIABLE backdrop, you do not test the average — you test the single lightest pixel (for light text) and single darkest pixel (for dark text) the text overlaps, because contrast must hold pixel-to-pixel under every character. APCA (Lc 0..±108) is the perceptual successor: it scores readability from luminance, font size/weight, AND polarity (dark-on-light positive Lc, light-on-dark negative Lc) instead of one blanket ratio, and clamps near-black with the Bclamp constants (Bthresh=0.022, Bexp=1.414) so dark regions that are visually indistinguishable are treated correctly. The math: pick the worst Y the glyph can sit over, require WCAG 4.5:1 (body) / 3:1 (large) or APCA |Lc|≥60 (body) / ≥45 (large) against it.

**Backdrop output-luminance band clamp (the shader-side contrast guarantee).** Instead of fixing contrast at the text layer, constrain the BACKDROP so its output luminance can never enter the band that breaks the overlaid text. Mathematically: remap final luma into [Lmin,Lmax] (a dynamic-range compression: out = Lmin + (Lmax−Lmin)·luma) so a 'content' route's backdrop is guaranteed e.g. ≥0.7 luma everywhere, making dark text pass at every pixel. Aurora already does a degenerate version (`clamp(col·0.985+0.008)` to dodge pure black/white); the SOTA is a parameterized, route-driven luma floor/ceiling.

**Per-route saturation + value clamp via perceptual desaturation (recede-behind-content).** To make a brand-register backdrop recede under form/text density, reduce CHROMA and compress VALUE range, not just opacity. In OKLCh: scale C toward 0 and pull L toward a mid-band. This is perceptually grounded (the Hunt effect — colorfulness drops as a region reads as 'background'), and it preserves hue identity while killing the figure/ground competition that pure opacity reduction (which just bleeds the page bg through) does worse. The current `opacityCeiling` is the coarse first axis; a `saturationCeiling`/`valueBand` is the perceptually-correct second.

**Scrim / gradient-protection overlay (Material's text-protection scrim).** A solid-to-transparent gradient (or flat tint) layered between backdrop and text: black 30–40% (rgba(0,0,0,0.30–0.40)) for white text, white 20–30% for dark text. The canonical number: a single `rgba(0,0,0,0.30)` overlay is often the exact line between failing and passing WCAG. EaseOut/cubic scrim stops (not linear) read more natural. Material 3 now prefers a uniform scrim tint over a gradient for content-dense surfaces.

**`contrast-color()` — native auto-picked accessible text color (Baseline newly-available, April 2026).** `color: contrast-color(var(--bg))` returns black or white by max WCAG-2 contrast against the input. Chrome 147 / Firefox 146 / Safari 26 all ship it (Widely-Available target 2028-10-10). Pairs with `light-dark()` and OKLCh relative color. Limitation: WCAG-2 math only and black/white only, so it underperforms on MID-TONE backdrops (a royal-blue mid-tone yields unreadable black). For a variable gradient you feed it the worst-case sampled color, not the average.

**`isolation: isolate` compositing-root containment.** Setting `isolation:isolate` on the backdrop root creates a new stacking/compositing context so any `mix-blend-mode` on the backdrop's own layers blends only within it (not up to the page root), and the backdrop is confined as its own paint root. This is the correct primitive for stacking the placeholder+canvas+optional-scrim as one composited unit under content without z-index leakage. (Aurora already gets a compositing root from `contain:content` + `content-visibility:auto`; `isolation` is the explicit, blend-safe form.)

**`backdrop-filter` legibility-on-demand (content-side, not backdrop-side).** Rather than dimming the whole backdrop, the content panel sitting OVER it carries `backdrop-filter: blur()/saturate()/contrast()` so legibility is created locally where text lives (the glassmorphic move), leaving the hero backdrop full-register elsewhere. This inverts the opacity-ceiling axis: clamp at the consumer's content surface, not the library's backdrop, when only part of a route is text-dense.

**OKLab/OKLCh interpolation for the scrim/placeholder gradient itself.** Per modern-web-guidance css §8: gradients and color-mix should interpolate `in oklab` (gamut-safe, the right default for a tint/scrim) or `in oklch` (chroma-preserving). `in srgb` is explicitly discouraged except for color-pickers — relevant because the CSS placeholder gradient and any scrim should not muddy through sRGB midpoints. (Note: glass-ui's documented `in srgb` surface-tint divergence is a separate, deliberate brand-calibrated exception.)
notes.applicability: ["**opacityCeiling is the right primitive but is only ONE of three needed axes.** The current `--aurora-opacity-ceiling` (uniform on placeholder+canvas, clamped [0,1], cross-fade-preserving) is well-designed and matches the design-system scrim literature. PATH FORWARD: add a perceptually-correct second axis — a `saturationCeiling` (or fold both into a `recede` atom) that scales OKLCh chroma + compresses the value band IN-SHADER (a `uReceed` uniform feeding the existing `saturate3`/post stage in tonemap.glsl.ts), and optionally a third luma-floor/ceiling clamp. Opacity alone bleeds the page background through and muddies the painted image; chroma+value compression makes it genuinely recede while keeping hue identity. This is the single highest-value AX aurora wave for this facet.", "**Add a backdrop output-luminance band clamp as a content-route contract.** Aurora's existing `clamp(col·0.985+0.008)` is a degenerate floor/ceiling. Parameterize it: a `uLumaFloor`/`uLumaCeil` (default 0/1 = no-op hero, e.g. 0.62/1.0 for a dark-text content route) remaps final luma so the backdrop CANNOT enter the band that breaks overlaid text — this is the shader-side worst-case-luminance guarantee, far more robust than a CSS scrim because it acts per-pixel at the source. Lands cleanly on the WebGL2 single-pass path (post stage, before OETF), no multi-pass needed, inside profile:budget.", "**Wrap the root in `isolation:isolate`, not just `contain:content`.** The aurora-root already gets a compositing root from `contain:content`+`content-visibility:auto`. Adding `isolation:isolate` makes the placeholder/canvas/(future scrim) stack blend-safe and z-index-leak-proof as one unit under content — the explicit primitive for the under-content compositing contract, and a prerequisite if any future scrim layer uses mix-blend-mode.", "**Document the consumer text-contrast contract in the README (W33) — worst-case + contrast-color()/backdrop-filter.** Aurora paints art; the LIBRARY cannot know the consumer's text color, so the honest contract is: (a) test contrast at the gradient's worst-case luminance point, (b) for content-over-aurora use `:opacity-ceiling` (now + a `recede`/saturation axis) to clamp the backdrop, (c) put text inside a glass/scrim surface (`backdrop-filter`) or use `contrast-color(<sampled-worst-case>)` for the text color. This is a README contract + a demo story (a 'content-over-aurora' route showing form+text legible over the clamped field), not a shader change.", "**An optional scrim slot/companion (consumer-owned, not baked).** Per 'presets in consumers', do NOT bake a scrim into the library default. Instead expose a documented recipe: a `::after` gradient-scrim (rgba(0,0,0,.30) for white text / rgba(255,255,255,.25) for dark) the consumer adds on the content wrapper, interpolated `in oklab`. Keep the library's job to the backdrop-side clamps (opacity/saturation/luma); the scrim is the content-side complement.", "**`contrast-color()` is now usable for the demo/consumer text over aurora (Baseline Apr 2026), behind `@supports`.** Demo stories and the README recipe can use `color: contrast-color(var(--worst-case-bg))` with an `@supports not (color: contrast-color(red))` fallback to a white-text-plus-text-shadow scrim. Useful for the demo's text-over-aurora showcase; not a library-source change (the library has no text)."]
pitfalls: **`contrast-color()` is WCAG-2-only, black/white-only, and FAILS on mid-tone backdrops.** Aurora's painterly fields are largely mid-tone/mid-chroma — exactly the case where contrast-color() returns an unreadable black or white. Never feed it the average backdrop color; feed the worst-case sampled luminance, and even then a scrim/clamp is usually still required. Treat it as a demo/consumer convenience, not a guarantee.
**`contrast-color()` is Baseline NEWLY-available (Apr 2026), NOT widely-available (target 2028-10-10).** Must be `@supports`-gated. Do not put it on the library's core path; demo/README only.

**Opacity-only receding bleeds the page background and muddies the art.** Lowering `--aurora-opacity-ceiling` composites the page bg through the painted image — on a non-neutral page bg this shifts hue and flattens the painterly value structure. Chroma+value compression in-shader is the correct receding mechanism; opacity is the blunt fallback. Do not over-rely on the single existing axis.

**Testing contrast at the AVERAGE backdrop color is the classic gradient-accessibility bug.** A field that averages 0.6 luma can still have a 0.95-luma highlight and a 0.15-luma trough under the same line of text. Always evaluate the lightest AND darkest pixel the glyphs overlap (WCAG G18 variable-background clause). For an ANIMATED backdrop the worst case is over TIME too — breath/drift can move a bright lobe under static text mid-cycle, so the luma-band clamp (which is temporally invariant) is safer than a one-frame contrast check.

**Forced-colors / high-contrast mode strips backgrounds.** Per modern-web-guidance css §5, `@media (forced-colors: active)` removes `background-image` and the canvas paint should be treated as decorative — the backdrop and any scrim disappear and text falls back to system colors. Ensure text legibility does NOT depend on the aurora or a `background-image` scrim in forced-colors mode (the placeholder gradient and scrim both vanish); the content surface must carry its own solid bg fallback.

**`mix-blend-mode` without `isolation` blends to the page root.** If a future scrim or the canvas uses a blend mode, without `isolation:isolate` on the aurora-root it blends against everything behind it up the document, not just the backdrop layers — visually unpredictable across consumers. Isolate first.

**APCA/WCAG-3 is still a CANDIDATE, not normative.** As of the Aug-2025 WCAG 3 draft the contrast method is NOT finalized. Use APCA as the perceptual sanity check and design target, but the shippable conformance floor is still WCAG 2.x (4.5:1 / 3:1). Don't claim APCA conformance.

**The shader luma-band clamp must live BEFORE the OETF and after ACES, in linear.** Aurora's space/gamma seam (proof:aurora-space-gamma) locks the tonemap→OETF order. A luma remap inserted in the wrong place (post-OETF, in gamma) will compute the wrong luminance and trip the gate. Insert it in the linear post stage alongside saturate3, before linearToSrgb.

**`in srgb` vs `in oklab` for any scrim/placeholder gradient.** The default should be `in oklab` (gamut-safe tint) per css §8 — but note glass-ui deliberately keeps `in srgb` for its surface-tint family (brand-calibrated). Do not blindly 'fix' the placeholder gradient to oklab if it's meant to match the surface-tint house identity; decide per-case and document.

notes.facet: Dynamic/interactive backdrop ergonomics — when to animate, taste in restraint, and the "arresting but not distracting" balance
sotaTechniques: **The periphery test (calm-technology core law).** Weiser & Brown's foundational rule: a calm interface lives in the user's *attentional periphery* and moves to the center only when summoned, then recedes. The operational heuristic distilled by the ambient-animation literature: 'if someone's eyes are drawn to the motion, it's already too much — dial it back until it's something you'd only catch if you were really looking.' This is the single governing law of the facet — the backdrop creates a MOOD, it never signals where to look.

**Slow-and-seamless timing grammar.** SOTA ambient motion uses long cycles (the Smashing case studies cite 3–6s for micro-elements, 20–30s rotation cycles, and layered 100/200/300s tracks for parallax depth), ease-in-out / cubic-Bézier curves (never linear), and seamless loops via matched start/end keyframes or `animation-direction: alternate`. Rotational deltas stay tiny (±2°). The rule: slow + organic + no abrupt reset = atmosphere; fast + linear + visible loop = distraction.

**Motion hierarchy / one-loud-element budget.** Reserve the single most-visible motion for the element that needs the most impact; everything else is sub-threshold. Not everything that CAN animate SHOULD — the restraint discipline is choosing only elements with natural motion cues ('does it have weight, is it flexible, would it move in real life?') and leaving the rest still. A field where every region drifts equally has no hierarchy and reads as noise.

**Idle-variation / no-single-perpetual-loop (game-dev idle theory).** A single fixed loop becomes consciously noticeable after ~90 seconds — the brain detects the period. SOTA practice layers a base loop (a breathing 'ground texture') with 2–4 secondary variations triggered at random intervals or by context, and modulates intensity by recent activity (louder just after interaction, quieter at rest). This is the antidote to the 'aquarium effect' where a perpetual hero loop becomes wallpaper the user tunes out.

**Reduce-don't-remove under prefers-reduced-motion (graded fallback).** The current accessibility consensus (2024–2025) is that PRM should REPLACE motion with a gentler equivalent (crossfade, opacity-only, sub-5% scale, slowed cycle), not necessarily KILL it to a frozen frame — preserve the same content/meaning at reduced intensity. The most-triggering motion classes to suppress first: parallax (called out as 'universally triggering'), large zoom/scale, spinning, multi-axis, and large peripheral movement. A static single frame is the floor, but a slowed/dimmed live wash is the more humane SOTA target where the surface is decorative.

**WCAG layered obligation: 2.2.2 (auto-play) + 2.3.3 (interaction-triggered) + a user toggle.** Auto-playing, >5s, non-essential motion needs a pause/stop control reachable by ALL users (2.2.2 — not gated behind PRM); interaction-triggered non-essential motion (cursor swirl, scroll-coupled drift) must be independently disableable (2.3.3, AAA). The SOTA pattern is a single visible global motion toggle PLUS honoring `prefers-reduced-motion` — two distinct seams, both required, because the OS preference and the on-page control answer different user needs.

**LCP-honest progressive enhancement (placeholder-first, enhance-after-first-paint).** web.dev guidance: a heavy backdrop must never be on the critical render path. SOTA is paint a cheap static poster/gradient as the first frame (zero JS/GPU), then cross-fade the live WebGL/WebGPU surface in AFTER first paint, deferred to idle. The static layer doubles as the no-WebGL / save-data / low-power fallback. This keeps FCP/LCP fast while still delivering the arresting hero — the arrest is a reward, not a tax.

**Demand-driven rendering + offscreen/hidden parking (content-visibility).** SOTA for continuous canvas backdrops is to attach ZERO frames whenever the surface is invisible: `content-visibility:auto` + `contentvisibilityautostatechange` parks the rAF when content-skipped (now Baseline since 2025-09-15), tab-hidden via `document.hidden`, and offscreen via IntersectionObserver `rootMargin:200px` fallback. The deeper ergonomic move is a render-DEMAND gate — if the next frame would be pixel-identical (all drift uniforms at rest, cursor settled within ε), park the loop entirely. Battery/thermal restraint IS taste at the system level.

**Per-route compositing envelope (recede behind content).** A hero-register backdrop and a content-over-backdrop route demand different intensities from the SAME engine. SOTA is a single outer-opacity / saturation clamp dial (distinct from per-pixel pigment alpha) so text-dense and form routes drop the field to ~0.5 and let it recede, while hero routes stay at full register — no palette re-authoring. Arresting where arrest is wanted; quiet where it competes with reading.

**Taste-encoded procedural color (IQ cosine palette + OKLCh perceptual interpolation).** The shader-art SOTA for tasteful color is cheap, perceptually-even color rather than RGB lerps: Iñigo Quilez's cosine palette `color(t) = a + b·cos(2π(c·t + d))` (a=bias/brightness, b=contrast, c=cycle count, d=per-channel phase) gives harmonious ramps for free, and interpolating/jittering in OKLab/OKLCh keeps mid-tones from going muddy or neon. Restraint in COLOR (low chroma, narrow hue arc, no pure black/white) is as load-bearing as restraint in motion for the 'arresting but not distracting' read.
notes.applicability: PATH FORWARD for glass-ui's aurora (grounded in the read of Aurora.vue, DESIGN.md, frameLoop.ts, cursorModel.ts). The engine ALREADY embodies most of the SOTA — this facet is largely a VALIDATION + a few targeted refinements, not a rebuild. (1) ALREADY-SOTA, keep and document: breath-paced drift at warpDrift 0.005–0.010 / 40–60s cycle is exactly the slow-seamless grammar; the lazy-arm CSS-placeholder-first cross-fade is textbook LCP-honest progressive enhancement; the content-visibility+IntersectionObserver+document.hidden parking and the needsAnimation() demand gate are the offscreen/demand-driven SOTA; opacityCeiling is the per-route compositing-envelope dial; OKLCh in-shader interpolation is the perceptual-color SOTA; the DockBackgroundToggle (2.2.2) + masterTempo PRM seam (2.3.3) is the layered-WCAG pattern. The README should CITE these as research-backed rather than incidental. (2) THE periphery-test gap to instrument: there is no objective 'is it too loud?' guard. AX should add a perceptual-restraint check to the default preset — frame-to-frame mean-luminance delta and per-region motion magnitude should sit below a 'catch only if you look' threshold; the wispy-sky DEFAULT must pass it (the default is the brand's honest face and must be sub-threshold by construction). (3) REDUCE-don't-REMOVE refinement: today PRM freezes to ONE static frame (frameLoop returns 0 tempo, needsAnimation false). The humane SOTA for a DECORATIVE wash is a SLOWED/DIMMED live drift, not a hard freeze — consider a PRM path that scales the integration dt to a small non-zero floor (e.g. 0.1–0.2×) for the smooth medium while keeping a hard freeze for the painterly/high-energy mediums and honoring the toggle's full stop. This is a judgment call to surface in the AX waves, not an automatic change (a frozen frame is the safe floor and currently correct; the slowed-live option is the more refined target where the surface is purely atmospheric). (4) IDLE-VARIATION against the ~90s wallpaper-effect: the single 40–60s breath loop risks being detected and tuned out. Layer a second, much-slower incommensurate cycle (a golden-ratio-offset period on nucleiDrift/paletteDrift so the combined field never visibly repeats), and/or modulate intensity by recent interaction (slightly livelier ~2s after a cursor wake, quieter at rest) — the interactivity 'wake' axis already has the decay machinery (CURSOR_BURST_DECAY) to drive this. (5) MOTION-HIERARCHY taste in the resolveAtoms door: the ≤7-atom 'mood' (calm↔vivid) and 'motion' (still·breathing·drifting) axes are the right control surface; ensure the DEFAULT atom set lands firmly in the calm/breathing register (periphery-safe) and that 'vivid/drifting' is the opt-in escalation for a deliberate hero moment, never the default. (6) INTERACTIVITY restraint: the opt-in-default-OFF posture for light/flow/scroll/wake is correct per 2.3.3 — keep it OFF by default; cursor-triggered swirl is exactly the 'interaction-initiated non-essential animation' 2.3.3 governs, and the existing reducedMotion early-out on the injectCursorVelocity write-path is the right seam. Document that opt-in-OFF is a deliberate WCAG posture, not an omission.
pitfalls: **The aquarium / wallpaper effect.** A single perpetual loop is detected by the brain after ~90s and tuned out entirely — the arresting hero degrades to ignored wallpaper. A 40–60s breath cycle alone is vulnerable; mitigate with incommensurate layered periods so the combined field never visibly repeats.

**PRM hard-freeze vs reduce-don't-remove tension.** Freezing to one static frame is the SAFE floor and is never wrong, but for a purely decorative wash the more humane SOTA is a slowed/dimmed live drift. Do NOT blanket-apply a slowed-live PRM path to the high-energy painterly mediums (visible brush/impasto motion is more triggering) — the floor for those stays a hard freeze. This is a per-medium judgment, not a global switch.

**Two-seam confusion (PRM vs on-page toggle).** `prefers-reduced-motion` (OS preference) and the DockBackgroundToggle (on-page 2.2.2 control) are DISTINCT obligations answering different users; shipping only one fails WCAG. The toggle must be a full STOP (suspend the loop), reachable by ALL users, NOT gated behind PRM.

**Interaction motion is separately governed (2.3.3).** Cursor swirl, velocity-flow, scroll-coupling are interaction-TRIGGERED non-essential motion — they must be independently disableable and must early-out under PRM on the WRITE path (the pointermove listener fires independent of the parked rAF, so freezing uTime is insufficient — the engine's injectCursorVelocity PRM early-out is the correct pattern and must not regress).

**LCP regression if the WebGL arm ever blocks first paint.** The placeholder-first deferred-arm posture is load-bearing; any 'eager' default, synchronous shader compile on the critical path, or a WebGPU adapter probe that blocks first paint would tax LCP. Keep the probe behind the deferred schedule. Capture/thumbnail consumers are the ONLY legitimate eager path.

**Color over-saturation reads as 'distracting' even when motion is restrained.** High chroma, wide hue arcs, and pure black/white clipping make a backdrop loud independent of its motion. The taste budget is color AND motion; the default must stay low-chroma, narrow-arc, never-pure-black/white (the engine's clamp(col·0.985+0.008) already does the latter — keep it).

**Portability: content-visibility parking is Baseline only since 2025-09-15** (Safari 26 / Firefox 130). On older engines the `contentvisibilityautostatechange` event never fires, so the IntersectionObserver rootMargin fallback MUST stay wired or offscreen surfaces keep burning frames. Do not drop the fallback assuming Baseline.

**WebGPU multi-pass (Kuwahara/smoothed-tensor) is an enhancement, never the arrest mechanism.** The 'arresting but not distracting' read must be fully achieved on the WebGL2 single-pass fallback; if the hero only looks right on WebGPU, ~5% of users get a degraded brand face. Tasteful restraint must be substrate-independent.

**Mobile/coarse-pointer reality.** Cursor-as-light, velocity-flow, and pointer-wake have no analogue on touch; an interactivity story that only lands on desktop hover leaves the mobile hero static-and-flat. Ensure the breath-paced ambient register (no pointer needed) carries the experience on touch, with interaction as desktop-only enhancement.

Assistant# Aurora Component — Research-Backed README Outline & AX Path-Forward

## Part 1 — Component README Outline

### 1. Overview & Lineage
- One-paragraph identity: a **painterly soak-stain/atmospheric backdrop engine** (Frankenthaler/Twombly/DALL-E lineage), NOT a generic CSS mesh-gradient — it composes warped fBm region fields, OKLCh-perceptual palettes, and optional painterly NPR finishes.
- Dual mandate: **arresting where arrest is wanted, recede where it competes with content** — the periphery-test law (calm-technology: "if your eyes are drawn to the motion, it's already too much") governs the default register [facet: dynamic-backdrop-ergonomics].
- The wispy-sky DEFAULT is the brand's honest face — sub-threshold by construction, renders identically on WebGL2 and WebGPU.

### 2. Use Cases
- **Hero backdrop** (full register, full-viewport, deliberate arrest).
- **Content-over-aurora route** (receded via opacity + saturation/value clamp; text legibility contract).
- **Per-mood/per-medium presets** (atmospheric wispy-sky → gestural Van-Gogh oil → wet watercolor → oil-pastel).
- **Seed-driven generative variety** (one seed → a whole in-family scene) [facet: generative-design-parameter-spaces].
- **Aurora-borealis namesake mode** (literal curtains/rays — opt-in, NOT the default) [facet: aurora-physics-rendering].

### 3. Best Practices (consumer-facing)
- **Import via subpath** `@mkbabb/glass-ui/aurora` (standalone ~16KiB-gzip WebGL chunk, never reached by the root barrel).
- **Drive with the ≤7-atom door**, not the 28-field author schema, unless you need the Advanced escape hatch [facet: atom-based-parametric-control].
- **Presets live in the consumer** (`demo/stories/aurora/presets.ts`); the library's own defaults are its identity — don't fork them.
- **Always pair a pause control**: `DockBackgroundToggle` (WCAG 2.2.2) + honor `prefers-reduced-motion` — two distinct seams, both required [facet: PRM/offscreen-park].
- **Content-over-aurora**: test contrast at the gradient's WORST-CASE luminance (lightest + darkest pixel under the glyph, and over time), not the average [facet: compositing-under-content].

### 4. Design Considerations (the painterly law-set)
- **Color discipline**: low chroma, narrow hue arc, never-pure-black/white floors — restraint in color is as load-bearing as restraint in motion.
- **Motion grammar**: breath-paced drift (40–60s cycle, warpDrift 0.005–0.010), ease-in-out, seamless loop; the single loud element budget; idle-variation against the ~90s wallpaper-effect.
- **Within-region value variation** (no flat fills) — the no-flat-fill law via pigment-density turbulence.
- **Warm-light/cool-shadow temperature coupling** + bell-curve chroma (saturated body, calm edges) — the painterly "reads as real pigment" levers.

### 5. The Atom Model (≤7 intuitive knobs)
- **The door**: `resolveAtoms` is PURE + TOTAL + DEFAULT-PRESERVING — every input (incl. out-of-range) yields a valid, plausible config (Disney "Principled" 5-rule discipline) [facet: atom-based-parametric-control].
- **Atoms**: `seed` · `mood` · `medium` · `textureAmount` · `motion` · `zones` · `interactivity` (harmony rides seed).
- **Two-tier progressive disclosure**: ≤7 atoms → 28-field author schema (Advanced) → optional thumbnail design-gallery picker as the primary "choose" UI.
- **Seed→everything determinism**: one seed deterministically derives palette AND scene via the shared seeded PRNG (Art-Blocks hash-to-traits; mulberry32/hashString) [facet: generative-design].

### 6. The Medium Taxonomy
| Medium | Operator family | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **smooth / wispy-sky** | domain-warped fBm + OKLCh palette + IGN dither | the cheap, identical-on-both-backends DEFAULT |
| **watercolor** | wet-edge power-curve + granulation + pigment-density turbulence + boundary wobble | single-pass; KM glaze + fluid bleed are WebGPU-only |
| **oil-pastel / crayon** | tooth-deposition + scumble (broken/optical color) + waxy burnish + sgraffito | Kubelka-Munk subtractive mix is the headline fidelity lever |
| **Van-Gogh oil** | structure-tensor ETF orientation + energy-graded strokes + impasto height→GGX relight + directional broken color | multi-scale coarse-to-fine is the Starry-Night cascade |
| **aurora-borealis (namesake)** | triangle-noise curtain field + altitude→color banding + curl drape | opt-in; core curtain must render single-pass WebGL2 |

- The **anisotropic-Kuwahara finish** ("make a gradient read as oil paint") is the WebGPU-only multi-pass enhancement common to the painterly mediums.

### 7. The Color-Space Discipline (the non-negotiable substrate)
- **Linear-light compositing + single sRGB OETF close** at `main()` — the AV.W1 "~2.2× too dark" defect is exactly the missing-OETF failure; locked by `proof:aurora-space-gamma` [facets: OKLab-interpolation, gamut-mapping].
- **OKLab-rectangular default interpolation** (the muddy-midpoint kill); **OKLCh hue-arc** (shorter/longer/increasing/decreasing) reserved for deliberate rainbow travel; OKLab-rect for near-achromatic pairs.
- **Per-stop gamut mapping**: hue-preserving chroma reduction, NEVER per-channel RGB clamp (which hue-shifts).
- **Single-source shared chunk** (`procedural-color.glsl.ts`): one set of Ottosson matrices, column-major, GLSL+WGSL twins at 1e-6 (`proof:single-color-core` / `proof:aurora-wgsl-equivalence`) — the structural guard against the two-copy drift class.
- **Dither in DISPLAY space after the OETF** (IGN, 1/255) — dithering in linear under-corrects mid-tone banding.

### 8. WebGPU vs WebGL2 (the dual-backend story)
- **WebGL2 single-pass is the universal, zero-regression floor** (DESIGN.md invariant 8): one full-screen triangle, one fragment program, zero deps, no FBO. The wispy-sky default renders IDENTICALLY on both paths.
- **WebGPU is the capability-gated enhancement** for genuinely multi-pass operators: smoothed structure tensor, anisotropic Kuwahara, LIC smear, stable-fluids pointer-wake, wet-on-wet bleed [facets: structure-tensor, Kuwahara, WebGPU-compute, multi-pass-FBO].
- **Production reality**: WebGPU ships in all four engines (Safari 26, Nov 2025) but NOT yet Baseline-widely-available (~5% still WebGL2-only) — the painterly headline can NEVER be a hard requirement.
- **Address-space discipline (the W01 bug class)**: dynamically-indexed arrays MUST live in `var<storage, read>`, NOT `var<uniform>` — uniform dynamic indexing is silent-broken on Safari/Metal while green on Chrome/Dawn [facet: WGSL-address-space].
- **Parity strategy**: real-device WGSL execution (dawn.node) > hand-transcription; column-major-is-the-invariant; codegen (Naga, build-tool only) over a second hand-maintained copy [facet: WGSL↔GLSL-parity].

### 9. Examples / Snippets
- **Minimal mount** (subpath import + atom door).
- **Content-over-aurora** (opacity-ceiling + saturation clamp + `backdrop-filter` content surface + `contrast-color()` `@supports`-gated).
- **Per-preset editable baseline** (`cloneMode="per-preset"` via the Configurator).
- **Manual pause wiring** (`DockBackgroundToggle` → `pause()`/`resume()`).
- **Vite manualChunks** split recipe.

### 10. Accessibility & Performance Contract
- WCAG **2.2.2** (auto-play pause/stop, all users) + **2.3.3** (interaction-motion disableable) + live-monitored PRM freeze.
- **Offscreen/hidden/tab-backgrounded park** (`content-visibility:auto` + IntersectionObserver fallback + `document.hidden`) + **demand-driven** render-on-demand gate.
- **DPR ≤ 2 clamp**; per-tier substrate downgrade to CSS-placeholder on low-power signals (`hardwareConcurrency≤4` / save-data / PRM).
- **`profile:budget`** caps (`AV_MAX_COLORS`, `MAX_NUCLEI`, loop-duration band).

## Part 2 — Prioritized PATH-FORWARD for the AX Aurora Waves

Ranked by ROI × risk. Each item names the seam and the facet backing it.

### TIER 0 — The Core Fix (W01, blocking)
**Flip the dynamically-indexed WGSL arrays from `var<uniform>` to `var<storage, read>`.** [facet: WGSL-address-space]
- `aurora.wgsl.ts` declares `var<uniform> U` yet dynamically indexes `U.nucleiPos[i]` / `U.palette[i0]` per-fragment — the exact Metal/`constant`-address-space hazard. **Green on Chrome/Dawn, silently broken/de-opted on Safari/Metal** — the very platform AW.W7 added WebGPU for.
- **FIX A (minimal, land first)**: flip the binding + buffer usage (UNIFORM→STORAGE); the existing vec4-padded std140 packing already satisfies std430, so **zero re-pack, byte-identical visual parity**.
- **FIX B (cap-lifting follow-up)**: split into a small `var<uniform>` scalar block + a `var<storage>` runtime-sized `array<Nucleus>`/palette with `arrayLength()`, retiring `MAX_NUCLEI=6`/`MAX_STOPS=8` — delivering the storage promise the `aurora.wgsl.ts` doc header ALREADY asserts but the code doesn't ship (doc-vs-code drift).
- **Gate**: born-RED storage-binding assertion + a Metal/Safari e2e via **dawn.node real-device execution** (compile the ACTUAL WGSL string against the GLSL oracle at 1e-6) — closes the hand-transcription drift class [facet: WGSL↔GLSL-parity].

### TIER 1 — Color Correctness (CPU-side, cheap, no hot-path cost)
**A. Upgrade `gamutMapStop` from the blunt 0.999 chroma-shrink loop to Ottosson cusp / CSS-Color-4 deltaEOK-JND.** [facets: OKLab-interp, gamut-mapping, color-harmony]
- value.js ALREADY ships `findCusp`/`findGamutIntersection`/`computeMaxSaturation`/`deltaEOK`/`DELTA_E_OK_JND`; the current loop under-shrinks saturated stops AND over-desaturates. Swap to the binary-search + deltaEOK-0.02 channel-clip refinement (recovers chroma the shrink loop discards — P3 yellow ~103 vs ~25). **CPU bake, negligible cost.**

**B. Splice an analytic Ottosson cusp clip into the shared shader chunk + route mixPaletteOklab/OklchArc/brokenColorJitter/saturate3 through it.** [facet: gamut-mapping]
- Today the in-fragment interpolants hit the naive per-channel clamp + ACES (the hue-shift/grey-out fallback). Analytic cusp projection (cubic + 1 Halley + 1 Newton, **mind the blue-hue precision dip**) is branch-free, ~constant cost, single-pass-safe, WGSL-twinned at 1e-6.

**C. Add the OKLCh-total migration as a documented axis.** [facets: OKLab-interp, color-harmony, palette-derivation]
- Add a thin perceptual-correction layer on `deriveHue` (muddy-zone steer + threshold-adaptive L/C) and `correctLightness`-style stop reparameterization. Keep OKLab-rectangular the SHIPPED default; gate any Oklch+ (L^0.73 + Naka-Rushton C) path behind a flag for wide-hue presets only. **All CPU-side, deterministic, must not move the wispy-sky default** (`proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip`).

### TIER 2 — Medium-Fidelity Perfection (single-pass WebGL2 where possible)
**D. Oil-pastel: Kubelka-Munk subtractive mix (the headline).** [facets: oil-pastel, watercolor, gamut-mapping]
- Splice a reduced-band spectral.js-style K-M mixer into the shared chunk so scumbled/overlapped layers composite subtractively (blue+yellow→green, not muddy lerp). **Cost is the hazard** — gate to painterly mediums, ideally **bake the K-M mix into the CPU palette LUT** (zero per-pixel cost) rather than calling 38-band `spectral_mix` per fragment. Strip spectral.js's own companding (keep aurora's single shared OETF). Make scumble OPTICAL (let the lower palette color show through); add sgraffito as a cheap high-value gesture.

**E. Van-Gogh oil: the Starry-Night cascade + GGX relight + directional broken color.** [facets: van-gogh, SBR, impasto, structure-tensor, anisotropic-Kuwahara]
- **(1) Multi-scale coarse-to-fine `bestOil`** (Hertzmann; currently single-scale — the biggest quality lever): 2–3 descending brush radii, fine dabs only where the coarse layer's luma diverges from the base; cite the −5/3 Kolmogorov / −1 Batchelor turbulence scaling as the cell-size prior.
- **(2) Replace the fixed quadratic-bulge spine** with a short multi-step integration along the structure-tensor minor-eigenvector (genuinely meandering strokes that hug iso-bands).
- **(3) Blinn-Phong → GGX** (roughness 0.3, F0 0.08) + Schlick-Fresnel N·V rim (the principled catch-light, NOT a baked constant) + **geometric specular AA** (fold normal variance into roughness — mandatory once the lobe sharpens or it strobes) + 4-tap central-difference normal (kill dFdx quad-faceting).
- **(4) Directional complementary broken color** (push neighboring cells toward opposite OKLCh hue poles — divisionism, not i.i.d. jitter).

**F. WebGPU anisotropic-Kuwahara: hard argmin → soft polynomial blend.** [facets: anisotropic-Kuwahara, structure-tensor, WebGPU-compute]
- `painterly.wgsl.ts` uses the pre-2010 HARD sector-binning + winner-take-all variance — which **bands into an 8-spoke pinwheel on aurora's flat gradient fields (its worst case)**. Adopt: soft blend `w_k=1/(1+(scale·s_k)^(q/2))`, in-loop polynomial sector weights (ζ≈0.1), Gaussian sector-membership overlap, canonical `a/b` ellipse axes, per-pixel STATIC noise kernel-rotation. Compute mean/variance in linear/OKLab, not gamma. Keep `q`/`radius` on the consumer-owned seam (`proof:webgpu-substrate-single`).

**G. Watercolor: wet-edge power-curve + granulation 2.0 + boundary wobble.** [facet: watercolor]
- Replace the flat 0.78 multiply with `col = pow(col, 1+uWetEdge·k·edge)` (monotone, rim-stronger, pre-tonemap); add paper-height sedimentation + OKLab two-pigment split; wobble the edge sample coordinate via the existing fBm. **All single-pass.** Fluid wet-on-wet bleed + backruns ride the WebGPU wake texture.

### TIER 3 — Atom Simplification & Generative Robustness
**H. Make scalar atoms continuous curves, not 3-point LUTs.** [facet: atom-based-parametric-control]
- `mood`/`motion` are discrete enums backed by 3-stop Records — collapse onto a single `[0,1]` monotone scalar driving co-varying curves (saturation+warpAmount+valueVariance+breathDepth), keeping named stops as labels on the axis. (Type break — acceptable clean cut per no-backwards-compat.) Audit ALL atom pairs for garbage combinations (Disney rule 5).

**I. Unify `seed` into a true seed→whole-scene derivation.** [facets: generative-design, atom-control]
- Today `seed` drives only palette; the FIXED `thirdsZones` 6-anchor LUT means two seeds give identically-arranged scenes. Drive nuclei placement (positions, driftPhase, valueBias) via the seeded PRNG with golden-ratio/stratified scatter (stays composed for any count, deterministic for `renderAt` bakes). Run a **weakest-output batch curation sweep** (sample N seeds × moods × mediums, surface the worst frames) and extend `proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip` to a degeneracy/coverage sweep.

### TIER 4 — WebGPU Parity-or-Default-Off Decision
**J. WebGPU is an ENHANCEMENT, never the default and never a hard requirement.** [facets: WebGPU-compute, multi-pass-FBO, PRM-park, dynamic-backdrop-ergonomics]
- **Decision: default-off for the painterly multi-pass finish; parity-required for the core curtain/default field.** The wispy-sky default + any literal-aurora curtain shape MUST render acceptably single-pass WebGL2 (reaching ~100% of users); the Kuwahara/LIC/fluid finish is the gated bonus for the ~95% on WebGPU.
- **Before promoting any WebGPU pass**: benchmark first (lisyarus finding — texture cache often beats hand-rolled LDS; convert ONLY the Kuwahara gather, keep tensor/smooth as fragment passes); wire `device.lost` self-heal → WebGL2 fallback; route `isFallbackAdapter` (software) to WebGL2; instrument each pass with `timestamp-query` and assert the multi-pass total stays inside `profile:budget`; allocate intermediates once (rebuild on resize only); RGBA16F tensor target (renderable+filterable by default; never rgba32float).

### TIER 5 — Tonemap & Compositing Refinements (lower priority, real polish)
- **Tonemap selector** [facet: ACES/filmic]: Narkowicz ACES (the current blue→magenta-skewing per-channel fit) → **Khronos PBR Neutral** as the safe headline default (built for well-exposed [0,1] designed backdrops, hue+saturation preserving, 13 lines, texture-free) with AgX behind a "cinematic" opt-in + exposure pre-scale. Re-baseline preset thumbnails (presets-in-consumers).
- **Chromatic never-pure-black/white floor** [facet: ACES/filmic]: replace the achromatic `clamp(col·0.985+0.008)` with an OKLCh floor tied to the palette's darkest-stop hue (deep paint, not crushed neutral), pre-OETF.
- **TPDF dither upgrade** over the single-sample IGN; blue-noise on the WebGPU branch only (texture-free invariant).
- **Per-route compositing envelope** [facet: compositing-under-content]: add a `saturationCeiling`/`recede` atom (OKLCh chroma + value-band compression in-shader) as the second axis beyond `opacityCeiling`; add a parameterized luma-band clamp as the shader-side worst-case-luminance contract; wrap the root in `isolation:isolate`.
- **Cursor-as-light / velocity-flow refinements** [facets: cursor-as-light, velocity-flow]: IQ `expImpulse` flick envelope over the linear burst ramp; dt-correct `1−exp(−λ·dt)` smoothing over fixed-constant lerps; `getCoalescedEvents()` for accurate flick magnitude; route all new motion through the master-tempo dt-scaling seam (never `uTime`) so PRM-freeze holds. Stable-fluids wake stays WebGPU-only.

**Cross-cutting invariants every wave must respect**: single shared color chunk (no second copy → the AV.W1 defect class); column-major matrices verbatim; dither stays post-OETF; gamut-map before ACES/OETF in linear; the wispy-sky default unchanged (`proof:aurora-atoms-roundtrip`); WebGL2 the zero-regression floor; all new motion through the PRM/tempo seam.
